articles.title: Even as unemployment falls, lack of ‘decent work’ in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Poor-quality employment generation has consequences for economic growth; workers without social security spend less, save less and remain vulnerable to economic shocks

I ndia’s unemployment rate fell from 6.1% in 2017-18 to 3.2% in 2023-24. At the same time, female workforce participation increased for the first time in decades as has been widely reported in government documents. In light of these positive developments, it is the right time to ask what kind of jobs have been generated in India recently, and what working conditions accompany them.

This is important because employment alone does not inherently ensure dignity, security, or a stable livelihood. A worker engaged in garment sewing without a formal contract, a gig worker without insurance coverage, or a construction labourer without paid leave may technically be considered employed, but they remain outside the promise of decent work. The International Labour Organization (ILO) defines ‘decent work’ as employment that offers equitable income, workplace rights, social security and dignity. This principle is integrated into Sustainable Development Goal 8 (SDG-8), which advocates “decent work for all”. Measured this way, India’s labour market persistently exhibits high levels of informality, insecure employment, and increasing inequalities.

Using two rounds of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), 2017-18 and 2023-24, the quality of employment in India has been analysed. By constructing a multidimensional Decent Work Index (DWI) based on three subdimensions — employment status, employment opportunity, and social security — across five major industries (agriculture, manufacturing, construction, wholesale and retail, and transport), it was observed that India has made progress in improving work conditions over time. The overall DWI increased from 0.247 in 2017-18 to 0.302 in 2023-24. While this indicates some improvement in job quality, the overall level remains alarmingly low. More importantly, progress has been uneven across sectors, regions, gender and caste groups.

Manufacturing in the secondary sector and transport in the tertiary sector showed the highest improvement in decent work conditions during this period. The manufacturing sector’s DWI increased from 0.324 to 0.411 due to a gradual rise in formalisation and digitalisation. The transport sector also experienced significant progress (from 0.285 to 0.35), largely due to the expansion of urban logistics and app-based platform work.

However, these improvements also reveal an important concern. Even in sectors where employment conditions have improved, access to social security remains limited. A large number of workers still do not have written contracts, paid leave, provident fund benefits or insurance coverage. Though employment opportunities are increasing, labour protections and job security are not improving at the same pace. Agriculture, which continues to employ the largest share of India’s workforce, remains the lowest-quality employment generating sector. The agricultural sector’s DWI marginally increased from 0.211 to 0.267 during the study period; most agricultural workers continue to be self-employed or unpaid family workers without stable income or labour protections. The issue is not merely low productivity; rather it is the rise of informal jobs. Construction and retail sectors tell a similar story. Workers remain dependent on casual employment, subcontracting chains and insecure labour arrangements. Welfare schemes exist on paper but implementation gaps continue to exclude millions of workers.

Nearly 90% of India’s workforce remains informally employed, a share that has risen since 2019, according to the India Employment Report 2024 (ILO–IHD). It has expanded into supply chains, app-based work in the gig and platform economy, logistics, home-based production, and in even organised industries through contractualisation and outsourcing.

The challenge becomes even more serious when viewed in the context of social inequality. The analysis by the authors shows that decent work outcomes improve significantly with education, formal enterprise employment and skill training. However, informalisation of jobs reduces decent work creation in India over time. Especially concerning is the growing intersection of caste and gender disadvantage: women from Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes experienced a decline in decent-work outcomes between 2017-18 and 2023-24, even as outcomes for men improved. The labour market penalty for being both female and socially marginalised has intensified after the COVID-19 pandemic. This shows that inequality in India’s labour market is not just economic, it is also structurally rooted in caste and gender hierarchies.

Regional disparities further expose the uneven nature of labour market progress. States such as Goa, Keralam, Tamil Nadu, and Haryana perform substantially better in terms of decent-work creation; in contrast, Bihar, Jharkhand, and Uttar Pradesh continue to lag behind.
The findings point to a serious policy concern: while India has been able to create more jobs, it is still struggling to ensure that these jobs provide decent working conditions and security.

Poor-quality employment generation has consequences for economic growth. Workers without social security spend less, save less and remain vulnerable to economic shocks. Moreover, informality depresses productivity, weakens tax capacity, and increases inequality. India cannot measure labour market success only through reduction in unemployment rates and income growth. A country aspiring to become Viksit Bharat by 2047 cannot rely indefinitely on insecure, low-paid and unprotected labour. Economic growth without decent work can create a workforce that may have jobs, but still lives with insecurity, instability and a lack of protection. India has to shift from a ‘job-counting approach’ to a ‘job-quality approach’.

The findings point toward where policy should focus. First, social protection must extend to all workers — gig and platform workers, self-employed, farmers, and informal workers — through systems that are portable and accessible regardless of employment status. Platforms such as e-Shram are a good start, but registering alone does not guarantee protection; workers need real protection, not just a database entry.

Second, formalisation policies should focus on labour conditions, not just business registration. Enterprises receiving tax incentives or subsidies should be linked to mandatory worker protections such as written contracts, paid leave, and social security contributions.

Even as unemployment falls, lack of ‘decent work’ in India

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Poor-quality employment generation has consequences for economic growth; workers without social security spend less, save less and remain vulnerable to economic shocks

I ndia’s unemployment rate fell from 6.1% in 2017-18 to 3.2% in 2023-24. At the same time, female workforce participation increased for the first time in decades as has been widely reported in government documents. In light of these positive developments, it is the right time to ask what kind of jobs have been generated in India recently, and what working conditions accompany them.

This is important because employment alone does not inherently ensure dignity, security, or a stable livelihood. A worker engaged in garment sewing without a formal contract, a gig worker without insurance coverage, or a construction labourer without paid leave may technically be considered employed, but they remain outside the promise of decent work. The International Labour Organization (ILO) defines ‘decent work’ as employment that offers equitable income, workplace rights, social security and dignity. This principle is integrated into Sustainable Development Goal 8 (SDG-8), which advocates “decent work for all”. Measured this way, India’s labour market persistently exhibits high levels of informality, insecure employment, and increasing inequalities.

Using two rounds of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), 2017-18 and 2023-24, the quality of employment in India has been analysed. By constructing a multidimensional Decent Work Index (DWI) based on three subdimensions — employment status, employment opportunity, and social security — across five major industries (agriculture, manufacturing, construction, wholesale and retail, and transport), it was observed that India has made progress in improving work conditions over time. The overall DWI increased from 0.247 in 2017-18 to 0.302 in 2023-24. While this indicates some improvement in job quality, the overall level remains alarmingly low. More importantly, progress has been uneven across sectors, regions, gender and caste groups.

Manufacturing in the secondary sector and transport in the tertiary sector showed the highest improvement in decent work conditions during this period. The manufacturing sector’s DWI increased from 0.324 to 0.411 due to a gradual rise in formalisation and digitalisation. The transport sector also experienced significant progress (from 0.285 to 0.35), largely due to the expansion of urban logistics and app-based platform work.

However, these improvements also reveal an important concern. Even in sectors where employment conditions have improved, access to social security remains limited. A large number of workers still do not have written contracts, paid leave, provident fund benefits or insurance coverage. Though employment opportunities are increasing, labour protections and job security are not improving at the same pace. Agriculture, which continues to employ the largest share of India’s workforce, remains the lowest-quality employment generating sector. The agricultural sector’s DWI marginally increased from 0.211 to 0.267 during the study period; most agricultural workers continue to be self-employed or unpaid family workers without stable income or labour protections. The issue is not merely low productivity; rather it is the rise of informal jobs. Construction and retail sectors tell a similar story. Workers remain dependent on casual employment, subcontracting chains and insecure labour arrangements. Welfare schemes exist on paper but implementation gaps continue to exclude millions of workers.

Nearly 90% of India’s workforce remains informally employed, a share that has risen since 2019, according to the India Employment Report 2024 (ILO–IHD). It has expanded into supply chains, app-based work in the gig and platform economy, logistics, home-based production, and in even organised industries through contractualisation and outsourcing.

The challenge becomes even more serious when viewed in the context of social inequality. The analysis by the authors shows that decent work outcomes improve significantly with education, formal enterprise employment and skill training. However, informalisation of jobs reduces decent work creation in India over time. Especially concerning is the growing intersection of caste and gender disadvantage: women from Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes experienced a decline in decent-work outcomes between 2017-18 and 2023-24, even as outcomes for men improved. The labour market penalty for being both female and socially marginalised has intensified after the COVID-19 pandemic. This shows that inequality in India’s labour market is not just economic, it is also structurally rooted in caste and gender hierarchies.

Regional disparities further expose the uneven nature of labour market progress. States such as Goa, Keralam, Tamil Nadu, and Haryana perform substantially better in terms of decent-work creation; in contrast, Bihar, Jharkhand, and Uttar Pradesh continue to lag behind.

The findings point to a serious policy concern: while India has been able to create more jobs, it is still struggling to ensure that these jobs provide decent working conditions and security.

Poor-quality employment generation has consequences for economic growth. Workers without social security spend less, save less and remain vulnerable to economic shocks. Moreover, informality depresses productivity, weakens tax capacity, and increases inequality. India cannot measure labour market success only through reduction in unemployment rates and income growth. A country aspiring to become Viksit Bharat by 2047 cannot rely indefinitely on insecure, low-paid and unprotected labour. Economic growth without decent work can create a workforce that may have jobs, but still lives with insecurity, instability and a lack of protection. India has to shift from a ‘job-counting approach’ to a ‘job-quality approach’.

The findings point toward where policy should focus. First, social protection must extend to all workers — gig and platform workers, self-employed, farmers, and informal workers — through systems that are portable and accessible regardless of employment status. Platforms such as e-Shram are a good start, but registering alone does not guarantee protection; workers need real protection, not just a database entry.

Second, formalisation policies should focus on labour conditions, not just business registration. Enterprises receiving tax incentives or subsidies should be linked to mandatory worker protections such as written contracts, paid leave, and social security contributions.

⚡ 3-Point Exam Takeaway & Deep Breakdown
1. Core Context & Background: Poor-quality employment generation has consequences for economic growth; workers without social security spend less, save less and remain vulnerable to economic shocks

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: I ndia’s unemployment rate fell from 6.1% in 2017-18 to 3.2% in 2023-24. At the same time, female workforce participation increased for the first time in decades as has been widely reported in government documents. In light of these positive developments, it is the right time to ask what kind of jobs have been generated in India recently, and what working conditions accompany them.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Second, formalisation policies should focus on labour conditions, not just business registration. Enterprises receiving tax incentives or subsidies should be linked to mandatory worker protections such as written contracts, paid leave, and social security contributions.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu LIVE update: Orange alert in six Telangana districts, yellow alert in five; holiday announced for schools, colleges in T.N., A.P. districts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The cyclonic storm lay centred about 350 km east of Chennai, 400 km east-southeast of Nellore, 430 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 420 km east-southeast of Kavali, 450 km southeast of Ongole, and 520 km south of Visakhapatnam, according to IMD.
Chennai District Collector S. Malathi Helen and Tiruvallur District Collector S. Kavitha last night announced a holiday for schools and colleges on Monday.

According to data from the Regional Meteorological Centre here, till 10.30 p.m. on Sunday, in Chennai district, the Nungambakkam station recorded 20.4 mm of rainfall, Meenambakkam recorded 4.9 mm, YMCA Nandanam recorded 13.5 mm, Ennore Port 39 mm, Madhavaram 21 mm, Anna University 10.5 mm and Taramani 7.5 mm.
In Tiruvallur district, Puzhal recorded 11 mm, Poonamallee 0.5 mm, and in Chengalpattu district, VIT Chennai recorded 0.5 mm of rainfall.

In the wake of the cyclone, Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu today called Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to seek assistance from the T.N. government for the restoration of power systems, according to the A.P. CM office.
Mr. Naidu requested that manpower and machinery be sent for restoration, as a large number of power poles were damaged due to the Murasu cyclone.
Mr. Vijay has reportedly responded positively to the request.
Palnadu District Collector Kritika Shukla has announced holiday for all government and private schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres on Tuesday (November 2) in view of Cyclone Murasu.

articles.title: Rebel leaders of AIADMK do not take part in district secretaries’ meeting chaired by Palaniswami
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The party’s performance in the recent bypoll in Dharapuram and Madurantakam Assembly constituencies, and preparations for its general council and executive committee meetings, expected to be conducted in December this year, were among the issues discussed at the meeting

The rebel leaders in the AIADMK, S.P. Velumani and Natham R. Viswanathan, did not take part in the meeting of party’s district secretaries chaired by general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami at the party head office in Chennai on Sunday.

The party’s performance in the recent bypoll in Dharapuram and Madurantakam Assembly constituencies, and preparations for its general council and executive committee meetings, expected to be conducted in December this year, were among the issues discussed at the meeting. Senior leaders A. Tamilmagan Hussain, K.P. Munusamy, and Dindigul C. Sreenivasan were among those who attended the meeting.

Earlier, Mr. Palaniswami issued a statement criticising the TVK-led government over the rates of medicines in Mudhalvar Marundhagams (formerly Amma Marundhagams). Citing a report from the All India Drug Action Network, he said medicines at Amma Marundhagams were being sold at rates higher than the prices fixed, which is affecting the poor.
Retired Additional Superintendent of Police S. Velladurai, who was known for his involvement in many ‘police encounter’ cases, joined the AIADMK in the presence of Mr. Palaniswami on Sunday.

articles.title: Litigants will not be entitled to refund of court fees if disputes get settled out of court after commencement of trial, rules Madras High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice P.B. Balaji refuses to follow Supreme Court’s 2017 verdict in M.C. Subramaniam’s case and instead follows the top court’s 2010 judgment in Afcons Infrastructure case

Litigants will not be entitled to return of court fees if their civil disputes lead to an out of the court settlement after the commencement of trial in civil suits, the Madras High Court has held after refusing to follow the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the 2021 M.C. Subramaniam’s case.

Justice P.B. Balaji agreed with Advocate General (A-G) Vijay Narayan that the 2021 verdict in M.C. Subramaniam’s case had not factored in the top court’s 2010 judgement passed by a bench of co-equal strength in Afcons Infrastruture Limited versus Cherian Varkey Construction Company Private Limited.

“It is settled law that when there is an earlier ratio of a Coordinate Bench, it is binding on a later Bench of equal strength and if at all the later Bench is not agreeable to the ratio laid down in the earlier decision, it is only open to the later Bench to refer the matter to a larger Bench and not take a contrary view,” the judge said.
He went on to state: “In such view of the matter, I am emboldened to follow and rely upon the ratio laid down in Afcons case instead of following the ratio laid down in M.C.Subramaniam’s case.”

The judge said, the Tamil Nadu Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955 insists upon litigants to pay court fees for a reason. The court fee gets collected to meet all necessary and incidental expenses relating to provision of infrastructure for courts, conduct of trials, payment of salaries and allowances to the court staff and so on.

Section 69 of the 1955 Act, as it stood originally, provided for refund of 50% of court fees “whenever any suit is dismissed as settled out of court before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim.” In 2007, Section 69A was introduced to the Act providing for refund of 100% of the court fees if the dispute gets settled after the court concerned refers the matter for arbitration, mediation, conciliation, Lok Adalat or such other alternative dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms mentioned in Section 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC).

In 2017, the Act was amended again to provide for return of 100% court fees under Section 69 too. However, even then, the legislature consciously did not tinker with the words “whenever any suit is dismissed as settled out of court before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim.”

Further, Justice Balaji highlighted that the Supreme Court in Afcons Infrastructure case had held that the civil courts could refer disputes to the ADR mechanisms mentioned in Section 89 of CPC only before commencement of trial because otherwise, the litigants could use it as a ruse to protract the trial.

Therefore, the continued existence of Section 69 along with the words “before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim” and the Supreme Court’s 2010 ruling that courts could refer civil disputes for ADR only before commencement of trial would make it clear that litigants would not be entitled to refund of court fees after the trial commences, the judge held.

The verdict was passed while dismissing two civil revision petitions filed by different litigants. The first civil revision petition had been filed against the order passed by a district court in Tiruvallur district to refund only 50% of court fees and the second had been filed against Chengalpattu court’s order that the litigant would not be entitled to refund of the entire amount of ₹2.54 lakh paid towards court fees.

Justice Balaji held that both the petitioners would not be entitled to refund of any amount of court fees since the out of court settlement had been reached only after commencement of trial. However, since the State had not filed any revision petition against the order to refund 50% of court fees to the first petitioner, the judge refrained from interfering with the Tiruvallur court’s order.

The judge had requested the A-G to assist him in the case considering the important question of law involved in the case related to the State exchequer and recorded the court’s “deep appreciations” to him. He also appreciated senior counsel S. Parthasarathy and S. Subbiah, amicus curiae S. Suresh Sampath, advocates S. Ramesh, S.R. Sundar, A.V. Arun and all other Bar members who made their submissions following an open invitation extended to all of them.

articles.title: NTK cadre want Seeman to seek AIADMK, DMK support for Ambasamudram byelection
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: His decision to contest is being seen as ‘bold’ and has reportedly energised the cadre after a disappointing showing in this year’s Assembly elections

NTK chief coordinator Seeman’s decision to contest in the Ambasamudram Assembly bypoll (when notified) has set off a debate among the party’s senior office-bearers whether it should seek the support of the DMK and the AIADMK for fielding him as the “common candidate”.

A senior party office-bearer said Mr. Seeman had been facing “pressure” internally to reach out to the leadership of the DMK and the AIADMK and ask for support. “Though it is a longshot, our office-bearers are putting pressure on him to reach out to the other parties. Mr. Seeman has explained to them that such a move would go against the fundamental position of the NTK,” an office-bearer said.

Mr. Seeman’s decision to contest was being seen as “bold” and had reportedly energised the cadre after a disappointing showing in this year’s Assembly elections, which saw its vote share reduce by almost half — falling from 8% to around 4%.
Mr. Seeman is yet to win an election despite trying his luck since 2016. A senior member of the party said: “Only a leader who takes these risky moves can keep the party and its cadre with him.”

Regarding the possibility of a common candidate, a party leader admitted it may not “possible” given the current political dynamics in the State. “Our decision to announce that Seeman will contest has given rise to these speculations,” he said.
Party sources said while Mr. Seeman would not formally seek the support of the DMK and the AIADMK, he would nevertheless welcome if “they not contest the elections”.

articles.title: U.S. mid-term elections: How officials are facing the heat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Poor-quality employment generation has consequences for economic growth; workers without social security spend less, save less and remain vulnerable to economic shocks

A mericans vote tomorrow, November 3, to elect the Congress for the last two years of Donald Trump’s presidency. While Indian voters are used to a single counting day, with most results in by evening, a U.S. count can run for days, and in a close race for weeks. This year the worry is whether the outcome will be accepted at all. In 2020, doubts arose after the count, and Mr. Trump still has not accepted that defeat. This time, they are being raised before voting, with Mr. Trump stating that he will accept the result only “if the elections are honest”.

The U.S. does have a federal Election Assistance Commission (EAC), but its responsibility is limited to certifying voting machines and training election staff. The 50 States have thousands of county officials who man the booths, count the votes and declare results; India’s electronic voting machines can total crores of votes in a few hours. In the U.S., many votes come by post, and each envelope must be opened and its signature checked before the ballot is counted. Moreover, there is variance in the procedure followed by different States. California will accept a postal ballot up to a week after polling day if it was posted in time. Twenty-six States order an automatic recount when the margin is very narrow.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: U.S. mid-term elections: How officials are facing the heat. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates: Odisha expedites evacuation from vulnerable areas as storm intensifies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: System intensifies into ‘Severe Cyclonic Storm’, likely to cross the south Andhra coast, between 11.30 p.m. today and 4 a.m. on November 3.
The Odisha government on Monday (November 2, 2026) expedited the evacuation of people from vulnerable areas.

Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said southern districts Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri were on high alert, with more than 300 NDRF, ODRAF and Fire Service teams pre-positioned. Heavy rain with gusty winds of 40-50 kmph is forecast for parts of Gajapati and Ganjam.

Chennai International Airport, in a post on social media platform X, said eleven flights have been cancelled to and from Chennai owing to the Cyclone. IndiGo has also confirmed in a post on X that “flight operations to and from Rajahmundry, Vijayawada and Tirupati are impacted.”

Ten IndiGo flights scheduled from Gannavaram Airport today (November 2, 2026) were cancelled, affecting passengers travelling to and from Vijayawada. Passengers have been advised to check flight status with the airline before heading to the airport.
A total of eleven flights arriving and departing from Chennai airport has been cancelled due to cyclone Murasu on Monday (November 2, 2026).
In a statement, Airports Authority of India (AAI) said, flights to and from destinations including Vijayawada, Kadapa, Rajahmundry and Tiruchi will be cancelled.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said severe cyclonic storm ‘Murasu’ lay over the west-central Bay of Bengal at 8.30 a.m. IST today (November 2, 2026), about 160 km east-southeast of Nellore and 180 km northeast of Chennai, moving west-northwestwards at 22 kmph.

It is very likely to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast, between Nellore and Narsapur and south of Ongole, between 11.30 p.m. today and 4 a.m. on November 3, with winds of 100-110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph.

Northern Tamil Nadu received heavy rain, and several places in Chennai were inundated, as Cyclone Murasu lay about 250-260 km from Chennai, heading for landfall over south coastal Andhra Pradesh. Chennai, Chengalpattu and Tiruvallur have had torrential rain since Sunday night, with Madhavaram recording 11 cm, and Ennore Port and Nungambakkam 10 cm each over 24 hours.

The IMD has issued an orange alert for Chennai, and schools in the city have a holiday today (November 2, 2026). Chennai Airport authorities said certain flights have been cancelled, and passengers have been asked to contact their airlines.

Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu was centred about 180 km north-east of Chennai and 160 km east-south-east of Nellore at 8.30 a.m. on Monday (November 2, 2026), the IMD said in a post on X. It is very likely to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, from 11.30 p.m. on Monday to 4 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).
Wind speeds of 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph, are expected at landfall.

fullParagraphs: Keralam’s Community Study Centres play a critical role in equipping tribal students to navigate an education system that rewards competitive individualism

Samoohya Patana Muri or Community Study Centres (CSC) is an initiative of the Keralam government started in 2018 to support the learning needs of children from tribal communities. In a tribal hamlet in Kasaragod district, CSC can be inventoried quite easily: a few computers, learning materials, a room open even after school hours, and light refreshments for ₹20 per student per day. What cannot be inventoried is what matters the most: whether a tribal student who has failed an exam feels confident to walk in the next day and ask for help or are they pushed away?

Our education policies speak the fluent language of inventories. It counts enrolment, sq ft. of buildings, equipment, and pass percentages, among other things, and these are not trivial. But access does not ensure achievement unless there is active participation of the students in the process of learning. Policies usually consider only access, not participation. A child can be enrolled in school, given basic learning resources, and still be unable to use what is on offer. Persisting after failure and believing that school wants us to progress are not merely individual acts of will; they are social acts. They are promoted, or suppressed, in the social space through relationships.

articles.title: How did two foreign nationals die in a five-star hotel pool in Bengaluru? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The incident raised serious questions about electrical safety standards, maintenance protocols and emergency preparedness at swimming pools in general and luxury hotels

The tragic deaths of two foreign nationals following suspected electrocution in the swimming pool of Hotel Conrad, a five star hotel operated by the Hilton Group, in central Bengaluru, have raised serious questions about electrical safety standards, maintenance protocols and emergency preparedness at swimming pools in general and luxury hotels in particular.

On October 30, 2026, evening at around 5:15 p.m., a German national Alexander Maximilian Theiss (57), a Lufthansa Airlines crew member, resting in Bengaluru between flight schedules after arriving from Frankfurt and Juraj Horvat (45), a Slovakian national on a holiday to India with his wife and an American national Mathew Desantis (41), were in the swimming pool on the third floor of the hotel.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: List of flights cancelled to and from Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Cyclone Murasu comes just days after Cyclone Arnab made landfall in Andhra Pradesh on October 27,2026.

Cyclone Murasu, which has intensified into a ‘Severe Cyclonic Storm’ over the West Central and Southwest Bay of Bengal, has led to flight cancellations on November 2, 2026, owing to adverse weather conditions. Flight services to and from Chennai, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam have been impacted.

Chennai International Airport, in a post on social media platform X, said eleven flights have been cancelled to and from Chennai owing to the Cyclone. IndiGo has also confirmed in a post on X that “flight operations to and from Rajahmundry, Vijayawada and Tirupati are impacted.”

#FlightUpdate | In view of the adverse weather conditions due to #CycloneMurasu, the following flights have been cancelled. Passengers are requested to contact the concerned airline for further information and assistance. #ChennaiAirport #Cyclone #Murasu #MurasuCyclone #CycloneUpdate #CycloneMurasuUpdate #FlightCancellations #Chennai #Airport #AAIAirports @MoCA_GoI | @AAI_Official | @IndiGo6E | @Pib_MoCA | @PIBChennai

IndiGo, in its X post, has said that “We are notifying affected customers on the mobile number provided at the time of booking. Customers are advised to check their flight status before proceeding to the airport.We remain in close coordination with the relevant authorities and continue to closely monitor the situation. The safety and well-being of our customers and crew remain our highest priority.”
Chennai Airport has requested passengers to contact the airline for more information and assistance.

Travel Advisory Due to adverse weather conditions associated with Tropical Cyclone Murasu, flight operations to and from Rajahmundry, Vijayawada and Tirupati are impacted. We are notifying affected customers on the mobile number provided at the time of booking. Customers are advised to check their flight status before proceeding to the airport. We remain in close coordination with the relevant authorities and continue to closely monitor the situation. The safety and well-being of our customers and crew remain our highest priority.

According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD) , Cyclone Murasu is “very likely to cross the South Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, from 11.30 pm on November 2 to 4 a.m. on November 3, 2026.
Wind speeds of 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph are expected at landfall.

articles.title: Congress demands scrapping of Siang hydropower project, release of arrested protesters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Arunachal Pradesh Congress Committee urged indigenous organisations, student unions, youth groups, civil society organisations and traditional institutions to unite against the proposed project

The Congress on Monday (November 2, 2026) demanded the scrapping of a proposed 11,200-MW hydropower project in Arunachal Pradesh and the release of those who have been arrested for protesting against the construction of a dam on the Siang river.

In a statement, the Arunachal Pradesh Congress Committee said no development project should be executed at the "cost of indigenous communities' ancestral land, identity, culture and livelihood" and asserted that prior consent from people likely to be affected by the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) was essential.
The party said, "Different groups but one voice; different organisations but one collective resolve - Stop SUMP, Save Siang."
The APCC urged indigenous organisations, student unions, youth groups, civil society organisations and traditional institutions to unite against the proposed project.
The Congress expressed concern over the arrest of protesters, suspension of government employees and action against gaon buras (village headmen) opposing the project.

It demanded the immediate release of all arrested protesters, withdrawal of cases registered under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, revocation of suspension orders against government employees and withdrawal of cases against gaon buras.

The party also sought withdrawal of additional security personnel from the proposed project-affected areas, adequate compensation for those who suffered losses, and medical assistance and rehabilitation for injured protesters.
The APCC urged the State government and the Centre to restore peace in the Siang region through dialogue and confidence-building measures.
The party appealed to all sections of society to "maintain unity and pursue the movement through peaceful and democratic means".
"Save Siang, save our land and save our people," it added.

The project, envisioned as one of India's largest hydropower initiatives, has faced sustained opposition from sections of the indigenous Adi community, particularly residents of the proposed project-affected areas.

The opposition stems primarily from apprehensions over the submergence of ancestral villages, displacement, loss of agricultural land and forests, and the possible disruption of the community's traditional way of life.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: Odisha Government evacuates people from vulnerable areas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: After Murasu intensified into a severe cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal, the Odisha Government has prioritised evacuation from vulnerable areas and strengthened emergency response mechanisms
The Odisha government on Monday (November 2, 2026) expedited the evacuation of people from vulnerable areas after Murasu intensified into a severe cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal, officials said.
Southern Odisha is likely to receive heavy rainfall under the impact of the storm, which is expected to make landfall in adjoining Andhra Pradesh.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD), in its latest bulletin, said that severe cyclonic storm Murasu was moving at a speed of 25 kmph and lay centred around 200 km east-northeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 210 km east-southeast of Nellore (Andhra Pradesh), 270 km south-southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 220 km east-southeast of Kavali (Andhra Pradesh), and 260 km southeast of Ongole (Andhra Pradesh).

"It is very likely to move northwestwards and cross the southern Andhra Pradesh coast as a severe cyclonic storm with wind speed of 100-110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph between Nellore and Narsapur close to Ongole between 11.30 p.m. on Monday (November 2, 2026) and 4 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026)," it added.
Odisha short of equipment, may use explosives to rescue landslide victims
IMD sources said that several areas in Odisha have started experiencing light rainfall under the influence of the system and the intensity of the precipitation is likely to increase gradually.
Following the warning, the State has prioritised evacuation from vulnerable areas and strengthened emergency response mechanisms, officials said.

Odisha's Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said though the storm is likely to make landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast, it would impact several parts of Odisha, particularly the southern districts of Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri.
He said all the District Collectors have been put on alert and the southern districts on high alert.
The Minister said the disaster response teams which were deployed during Cyclone Arnab continued to remain positioned in the same places ahead of Cyclone Murasu.
Over 300 rescue teams comprising personnel of NDRF, ODRAF and Odisha Fire Service have been pre-positioned, he said.
The IMD has forecast heavy rainfall in some places in Gajapati and Ganjam districts on Monday (November 2, 2026) along with thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph.

articles.title: Bangladesh garment factories reopen as wage protests keep industry on edge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The latest unrest disrupted operations in key manufacturing hubs and raised ‌concerns over export shipments and buyer confidence in Bangladesh, the world’s ‌second-largest apparel exporter after China, as workers demanded a minimum monthly wage of ⁠30,000 taka ($243), up from 12,500 taka

Bangladesh’s garment factories reopened ​on Monday (November 2, 2026) after widespread closures and production disruptions a day ⁠earlier, but manufacturers remain concerned about further unrest over workers’ demands for higher wages.
The ready-made garment sector accounts for more than 80% of Bangladesh’s export earnings, employs about ‌4 million workers and contributes around 10% to gross domestic product.

The latest unrest disrupted operations in key manufacturing hubs and raised ‌concerns over export shipments and buyer confidence in Bangladesh, the world’s ‌second-largest apparel exporter after China, as workers demanded a minimum monthly wage of ⁠30,000 taka ($243), up from 12,500 taka.

The demand reflects mounting pressure from rising living costs and persistent inflation. The government formed a six-member minimum wage board on Sunday (November 1) to review the ​demand, but the move failed to ‌immediately quell unrest.
Workers set up road blockades in several industrial areas on Sunday, with police in the capital Dhaka using tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters.

“Bangladesh has among the lowest garment wages ‌in the world,” said Babul Akhter, general secretary of the Bangladesh Garment ​and Industrial Workers Federation and a workers’ representative on the wage board.
“If factory owners cannot pay workers properly, they should negotiate ⁠better prices with international buyers. They cannot build a business on the backs of underpaid workers.”
Factory owners said the industry ‌faces higher costs, energy market uncertainty linked to conflict in West Asia and slowing demand in key export markets.
The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said demonstrations in multiple cities disrupted operations at 529 factories and affected nearly 1 million workers.
“The government has already taken a step by forming the wage board. We expect workers to allow the review process to proceed,” said ‌BGMEA president Mahmud Hasan Khan.

“If protests break out later in the day and ​we are forced to shut factories, we will have no option but to invoke the ‘no work, no pay’ provision,” he said, adding ⁠industry representatives were scheduled to meet the Home Minister to discuss the unrest.
Selim Raihan, ⁠an economics professor at the University of Dhaka, said workers’ demands were understandable, given that high inflation and suppressed wages could cause further ‌unrest.

articles.title: Irish bookshops help meet U.K. demand for Sally Rooney novels
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Publisher Faber said it could no longer distribute Ms. Rooney's books in the United Kingdom because it could not transfer U.K. earnings to the author after she announced plans to donate those proceeds to Palestine Action, which is banned in Britain

Irish bookshops are helping readers in Britain and elsewhere obtain novels by Sally Rooney after her publisher halted U.K. supplies because of complications arising from the author's support for a pro-Palestinian group.

Publisher Faber said it could no longer distribute Ms. Rooney's books in the United Kingdom because it could not transfer U.K. earnings to the author after she announced plans to donate those proceeds to Palestine Action, which is banned in Britain.
But Jenni Doherty, owner of Little Acorns Bookstore in Londonderry, has continued stocking Rooney's bestselling books through suppliers in the Republic of Ireland.

"We're not banned from selling the books. We can still have access to the books," Ms. Doherty, 55, told AFP , surrounded by Ms. Rooney titles such as "Normal People" , "Intermezzo" and "Beautiful World, Where Are You".
Londonderry, known as Derry to republicans within Northern Ireland, is part of the United Kingdom but lies next to the border with EU member Ireland.
Its position allows Ms. Doherty to order stock through Irish distributors before sending books to customers around the world, including in Britain.
"To sell a writer's work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher," Faber said, as it announced its decision in mid-October.
The decision, made in agreement with Rooney, followed the author's declaration that she would donate her earnings to the pro-Palestinian direct action group.
Palestine Action was banned by the U.K. government in July 2025 under anti-terrorism laws, but is not prohibited in Ireland, where Ms. Rooney lives.
Its proscription, which places it on the same list as Lebanon's Iran-backed Hezbollah and the Palestinian militants Hamas, makes it illegal in Britain to belong to, support or finance the group.
Faber said it remained Ms. Rooney's publisher and would continue selling her work outside Britain.
The books themselves have not been banned, and copies already held by British retailers can remain on sale.

articles.title: Trump's Republicans scramble to stop Democratic midterms wave
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: While Tuesday is election day, early voting has already seen a record 54 million people cast ballots around the country, reflecting the intense political fervour

Republicans in the U.S. made a final push on Sunday (November 1, 2026) to prevent a predicted thumping in U.S. midterm elections where Democrats are gunning to win control of Congress and impose a first political check on President Donald Trump's pursuit of power.
Polls show Democrats are all but certain to take the majority from Republicans in the House of Representatives in Tuesday's (November 3) vote and have a real shot at winning the Senate.
But after a decade of Mr. Trump defying political gravity and two years of a second presidency in which he has ridden roughshod over every norm, Democrats remain nervous.
"Nauseously optimistic," Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock told CNN to describe the mood.

Those jitters increased on Sunday over an ugly party rift in Michigan, a key battleground where a Democratic congresswoman defected to back Republican Mike Rogers against the Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed.
The consensus among analysts, however, is that Democrats are surging.

Mr. Trump headlined the Republicans' last-ditch charge, holding rallies for candidates in Iowa and Kansas — States where ordinarily his party should be confident of victory and not require presidential boosts.
Along with making lurid claims that Democrats will turn the country communist, Mr. Trump is dangling the promise of $5,000 payments to everyone in the country if his party wins.
"We're going to win," he told the crowd in Iowa, painting Democrats as "extreme and dangerous radicals" who will "steal your wealth" and let in migrants to "ransack, rape and plunder."
But polls show Americans have soured on Mr. Trump's wrecking-ball presidency.
An NBC News poll released on Sunday showed 60% disapprove of Mr. Trump's performance, particularly over high prices exacerbated by his now eight-month, sputtering war against Iran.
While Tuesday is election day, early voting has already seen a record 54 million people cast ballots around the country, reflecting the intense political fervour.

articles.title: Binance sees outflows stabilising as exchange returns online after $6.3 billion heist
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: US President Donald Trump, however, later on Saturday said it remained unclear whether North Korea was involved

Binance customers pulled $3.64 billion, or 2.1% of its assets, as the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange resumed service after a security breach linked to North Korea saw $6.3 billion ‌stolen from the platform last week.

The exchange moved to reassure crypto investors and said withdrawals were stabilising after an initial ​spike and deposit volumes had remained “substantial” after, what analysts believe, may be the world’s biggest financial robbery ever.

After hitting ⁠a six-week low on Friday (October 30, 2026), bitcoin prices recovered slightly through the weekend to trade above $78,000 on Monday. Ether hit a two-month low on Friday and also recovered a little to $2,287.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally. It said on Sunday it had $171 billion ‌in total assets under management as of October 28.
The Binance theft adds to a string of recent crypto thefts. Attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 incidents last year, according to researchers at TRM Labs.
Withdrawal levels are an early ‌test of whether customers still trust Binance with their money after the attack. The exchange said it had covered 95% of the ‌assets ⁠stolen in the heist.

Stablecoin market capitalisations tend to fall when money is leaving cryptocurrencies and they have dropped since Friday. ⁠The combined capitalisation of the two largest stablecoins, USDT and USDC, has dropped by about $1.2 billion since Friday, according to Coinmarketcap.com.

Spot bitcoin ETFs shed $643 million on Friday, the largest daily outflow of October, and more than $1.3 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated, said Ari Redbord, global head of policy at US blockchain analysis firm TRM Labs.
“I get why, for ​conservative institutional investors, this is unsettling,” Redbord said.

“A hack at ‌a financial institution means stolen usernames and passwords. A hack at a crypto exchange is bank robbery at the speed of the internet, which creates an unstable risk profile for anyone responsible for other people’s capital.”

Binance said on Sunday it had covered $6 billion of stolen cryptocurrencies by using its money to buy replacement tokens. The remaining 5% of stolen tokens consist of less liquid assets and may ‌take longer to source, it said.
Despite those measures, some users were weighing options to hedge risks.

articles.title: Delhi High Court seeks report on qualifications of two doctors accused of mishandling child
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Justice Neena Bansal Krishna passed the order on October 30 while hearing a contempt petition filed by the child’s mother

The Delhi High Court has given the National Medical Commission (NMC) and the Delhi government’s Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) two weeks to submit a joint inquiry report on the medical qualifications of two doctors accused of mishandling a child during treatment.
Justice Neena Bansal Krishna passed the order on October 30 while hearing a contempt petition filed by the child’s mother, Sapna Jain, on behalf of her minor son.

According to the petition, the child suffered severe brain damage “after being mishandled by two unqualified doctors (misrepresenting as super-specialists) in the Neonatal ICU of Fortis Hospital, Shalimar Bagh”.

The petition claims that the child is now in a permanent vegetative state and suffers from West Syndrome, epilepsy and cerebral palsy. It also states that he continues to experience severe pain and suffering.

In March 2025, the High Court had called for affidavits clarifying whether the qualifications claimed by the two doctors “are qualifications entitling these Respondents (doctors) to undertake specialisation practice in this country.”
In May 2026, the court further directed the NMC Secretary and the DGHS to conduct a joint inquiry into the doctors’ qualifications and submit a report within eight weeks.
However, the fresh contempt petition alleged that the deadline of July 24, 2026, passed without the authorities submitting the report or seeking an extension from the court.

“The matter concerns the qualifications of doctors treating critically ill newborns. The NMC, being the statutory regulator, is duty-bound to ensure transparency and accountability, and its continued failure to place a clear and conclusive report before this Court raises serious questions regarding its fairness and credibility and that of its officers. The DGHS has likewise failed to discharge the joint duty cast upon it by this Court,” the plea said.
The court has posted the case for hearing on December 16.

articles.title: Oocyte racket in Telangana: Women paid ₹20,000 as operators made around ₹3 lakh per cycle
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Police probe alleged exploitation of 43 women, including possible forged consent documents and illegal commissions, while examining recruitment networks, payment trails and the role of IVF and fertility centres in Hyderabad

Women recruited from economically weaker sections were being offered ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 for an egg donation cycle, while those operating the alleged racket made an average of about ₹3 lakh from each cycle.
Malkajgiri police widened their investigation into the exploitation of women, falsification of records and the role of IVF and fertility establishments.

The 43 women rescued during simultaneous raids in Hyderabad have undergone medical examinations, including blood-group and fitness tests. Police are now verifying their medical histories with IVF centres to establish their treatment records.

The investigation has raised concerns over how the women were recruited and whether they gave informed consent for the procedures. Police said women from economically weaker sections were targeted and that, in some cases, intermediaries allegedly even completed their signatures on documents. Investigators are examining possible falsification of records and whether the women fully understood the procedures they were being recruited for.
Police are tracing the payments and commissions involving organisers, recruiters and intermediaries who connected the women with fertility-related establishments.

The investigation is now expanding to medical establishments. Police are preparing to serve notices to the District Medical and Health Officer (DMHO) and conduct searches at ART and fertility centres. Some hospitals have also approached police and informed them that employees found to have been involved had been removed.

Investigators are examining how women from West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and other states were recruited, transported and accommodated in Hyderabad before being referred for egg retrieval procedures. Their medical records, consent documents and the procedures they underwent are also being scrutinised.
All eight accused arrested in connection with the Hyderabad cases have been remanded to judicial custody. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: What India’s leaky exam system can learn from Soviet shoe factories
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Unless we treat the exams as the complex economic product they are, with knowledge dispersed among specialised professionals and each player acting in their own self-interest, and restructure the financial incentives at play, we will keep having protests and Cabinet reshuffles and Committee appointments

While the protests in New Delhi, the Centre relenting, and the petitions at the Supreme Court bent the arc of justice towards the lakhs of students who had suffered from leaked examination papers, neither the Cockroach Janta Party-led opposition nor the ruling dispensation have offered any concrete steps to prevent future leaks, beyond administrative reshuffles and legislative amendments. Neither seems wiser than the other.

The operations of the National Testing Agency (NTA) bear an uncanny resemblance to those of state-owned shoe factories in Soviet Russia. articles.title: SC disposes of Ram Temple embezzlement petitions after Uttar Pradesh says charge sheet filed
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court allowed petitioners, including Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Case Trust, Ajay Kumar Rai, Narendra Kumar Goswami and Sudhakar Singh, to assist the trial court in further proceedings

The Supreme Court on Monday (November 2, 2026) closed multiple pleas seeking Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the Ram Temple donations’ embezzlement case after the State of Uttar Pradesh informed it that a charge sheet has already been filed by its Special Investigation Team (SIT).

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India bowed out of any further judicial scrutiny even as Solicitor-General Tushar Mehta submitted that the misappropriations had occurred during the counting of the money, which was allegedly invested in property by the accused persons.

In its order, the apex court allowed petitioners, which include Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Case Trust, Ajay Kumar Rai, Narendra Kumar Goswami and Sudhakar Singh, among others, to assist the trial court in further proceedings.
The Bench reasoned that they could assist in the capacity of “victims of crime” as the case involved issues of public interest.

“Courts have allowed victims of crimes to assist, similarly you also assist the court… If there is an element of public interest involved, law enables victims to assist the court,” Chief Justice Kant told the petitioners.

Besides a common plea for a CBI probe, the petitioners had variously sought the immediate preservation of evidence, records, CCTV footage, and digital logs relating to donations and offerings at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir.
They had also sought an independent forensic audit of donations, offerings, and valuable items received by the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust from its inception till date.

The petitioners wanted the apex court to constitute or direct constitution of an expert committee comprising representatives of the Union and State authorities, audit/accounting experts, digital-payment/cyber-forensic experts and temple-administration experts to frame a ‘National Minimum Temple Donation Transparency Framework’ for public temples and religious endowments of national importance and temples receiving substantial annual donations, including but not limited to Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir, Ayodhya and Shri Krishna Janmasthan at Mathura.

In the previous hearing, the Uttar Pradesh government’s SIT report had said 105 instances of unauthorised currency removal were captured on CCTV in the temple donations’ misappropriation case. Mr. Mehta, on November 2, said initial investigations could only grab 48 hours of CCTV footage. However, the probe team had traced back to find out how and where the purloined money was used.
The status report had noted the estimated amount misappropriated by each accused individual.

It had said that receipts generated by the TCS software for 803 valuable articles were verified, and their relevant records were found to be with the Temple Trust. These articles were stored in a State Bank of India locker, which was physically checked.

In so far as these articles were concerned, no discrepancies were found during the verification. However, there were 86 valuable articles in respect of which receipts have not been issued. These articles had been separately identified and physically verified.

fullParagraphs: Palnadu District Collector Kritika Shukla has announced holiday for all government and private schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres on Tuesday (November 2) in view of Cyclone Murasu.
The Collector, in a press release here on Sunday, informed that the district administration has made all necessary arrangements to effectively deal with Cyclone Murasu.

A special control room has been set up at the Collectorate to ensure that people do not face any inconvenience due to the cyclone and to facilitate immediate relief measures. The control room will function round-the-clock. Staff have been deployed to provide necessary information to the public and coordinate relief operations.
People can contact the control room for emergency assistance or information on the number 08647 252999
In view of the cyclone warnings, the District Collector urged people to remain alert and avoid going outdoors unless absolutely necessary.

articles.title: Andhra goes ahead with Kotia local body polls despite Odisha’s plea in Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The YSRCP and the TDP both claim the disputed border villages will vote for them on November 5

The Andhra Pradesh government and the State Election Commission are making all arrangements to conduct local body elections in the Kotia group of villages on the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border, despite strong objections from Odisha. The neighbouring State has approached the Supreme Court to stop the election process in the disputed region.

Both the States have been at odds over the jurisdiction of the Kotia group of villages for about seven decades. Both have also been holding local body elections there for many decades. Odisha has objected before: it filed contempt petitions when Andhra Pradesh held polls in the villages in 2021. This time, it filed a fresh contempt petition last month, alleging that the poll notification violates the Supreme Court’s 2006 order directing both States to maintain the status quo. The villages are located 35 km from Salur town of Parvathipuram Manyam district.

Since the court has not passed any order on Odisha’s petition, the Parvathipuram Manyam district administration is making all arrangements to hold elections in places like Ganjai Bhadra, Pagalu Chennuru, Pattu Chennuru, Kurukutti, Sarika, Kotia and other villages on November 5, 2026. The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which won the Salur Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency and all four Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies in 2021, is keen to win them again with its spirited campaign in all Kotia villages.

Former Deputy Chief Minister and YSRCP senior leader Peedika Rajanna Dora on Monday alleged that the TDP, JSP and BJP alliance parties colluded with the ruling BJP leaders of Odisha to stop the election process in the Kotia group of villages as they were fearful of defeat there. “Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy government had won the hearts of Kotia people with its welfare schemes with an aim to get complete jurisdiction rights for AP over Kotia group of villages. The people who benefited from the welfare schemes of Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy will vote for us,” said Mr. Rajanna Dora while speaking to the media in Salur.

The Telugu Desam Party rejected the YSRCP’s allegations and said the TDP and its alliance partners would get an absolute majority in the Kotia villages this time, as was evident from the spectacular response to the TDP’s campaign in those villages. “In spite of the strong objection from Odisha officials, TDP has been campaigning vigorously in all villages. Recently, Odisha officials seized our campaign vehicle. In spite of all hurdles, we are continuing the campaign in those villages,” said TDP Salur president A. Parameswara Rao.

Meanwhile, Parvathipuram Manyam Collector N. Prabhakara Reddy and Superintendent of Police S.V. Madhav Reddy directed all political leaders to be cautious while campaigning in sensitive areas of the AP-Odisha border. They also asked polling officials to take care of ballot boxes, ballots and other polling material while conducting the election process in the Kotia group of villages. The police department is expected to send additional security forces to the Kotia villages to ensure free and fair elections. According to them, there may not be any untoward incidents on polling day as the local body elections were conducted smoothly in 2021.

articles.title: KEA to go ahead with written examination for recruitment of PU college principals in Karnataka on November 20, 22
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The lecturers’ association had submitted a representation seeking postponement of the examination by one month citing lack of time for preparation

The Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA) has decided to go ahead with the written examination for direct recruitment to the post of principal of government PU colleges as scheduled on November 20 and 22. The lecturers’ association had submitted a representation seeking postponement of the examination by one month.

The KEA is conducting the examination for direct recruitment of government PU college lecturers to 216 vacant posts of Grade A government PU college principal. Lecturers who have served in a college for more than 10 years are qualified to appear for the examination.

A lecturer from a government PU college in Mangaluru, who has served more than 15 years and is slated to appear for the exam, said not much time has been given to aspirants for preparation. They have to write papers on Kannada, General Studies, and Karnataka Civil Services Rules (KCSR).

The KCSR paper is a lengthy one and a minimum of one month is required for preparation. With lecturers being involved in SIR and other non-academic work, they hardly had time for preparation, since issuance of notification of the examination by the KEA on September 3.

Ninge Gowda, President of Karnataka State PU College Lecturers’ Association, told The Hindu that the last date for filing application was October 30. Like other recruitment examinations , the KEA should have scheduled the examination after a period of 90 days from the last date. He said representations seeking postponement were made to Additional Chief Secretary, School Education and Literacy, Rashmi Mahesh, and KEA Director H. Prasanna.

An office-bearer of the association, however, said there are no minimum marks, and top scoring aspirants will be selected for the vacant posts. After a long time, the government is conducting selection process for direct recruitment to the post of principal. Of the total 870 vacant posts of principal, 216 posts were being filled through direct recruitment.
“The situation is the same for all lecturers. It is better for aspirants to appear for the examination as per the schedule than seek postponement,” the office-bearer said.
Mr. Prasanna said the KEA will go ahead with the written examination as scheduled with 2,839 candidates expected to appear for the exam.

articles.title: Iran says considering two-day plan to reopen Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: “The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said

Iran's Foreign Ministry on Monday (November 2, 2026) said it was considering a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. agrees to its conditions, having previously proposed a one-week timeline.

"The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach. We have stated that, if Iran's demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period," said Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei, adding that the "exchange of messages is still ongoing" via mediators.

articles.title: Over 8,000 police personnel deployed to protect polio teams in Pakistan's Karachi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The development comes a day after the National Emergency Operations Centre for Polio Eradication confirmed that the new case was reported from Khyber district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province

More than 8,000 police personnel have been deployed in Pakistan's port city, Karachi, to provide security to vaccination teams during a week-long anti-polio campaign, an official said on Monday (November 2, 2026).

The campaign, conducted from November 2 to 8, has also begun in other parts of Pakistan, including Balochistan province, where vaccination teams are operating in 31 districts under heightened security measures.
The development comes a day after the National Emergency Operations Centre for Polio Eradication confirmed that the new case was reported from Khyber district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
Karachi Commissioner Syed Hassan Naqvi said safeguarding vaccination teams has been heavily prioritised following past security incidents and attacks during immunisation drives.
Additional police personnel have been deployed in sensitive areas, while snap checking and mobile and motorcycle patrols have been increased to strengthen security, he said.
Anti-polio campaigns in Pakistan are regularly marred by violence.
Despite global efforts to eradicate the virus, challenges such as safety issues, vaccine hesitancy, and misinformation remain in eliminating it.

Vaccination efforts continue to face resistance from community members amid misinformation and religious concerns surrounding the vaccine, including false claims that it causes infertility or impotence.
In September, militants killed two policemen deployed to protect a polio vaccination team in Balochistan's Nushki district.
During the 2025 anti-polio campaigns in Karachi, the provincial health department documented approximately 41,000 instances where parents or guardians refused to vaccinate their children.
Pakistan and Afghanistan are the only countries in the world where polio remains endemic, according to the World Health Organisation.

articles.title: Trump and Republicans in for a drubbing in mid-terms
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A forecasting model suggests the Democrats could win 230 of 435 seats in the House and 18 of 35 seats being contested in the Senate

On Tuesday, Americans vote in mid-term elections , halfway through Donald Trump ’s second term. Since January 2025, Republicans have controlled both chambers of Congress, though by thin margins. In the House of Representatives, they hold 218 of the 435 seats against 214 for the Democrats, with one independent and two vacancies. In the Senate, the Republicans hold 53 seats to the Democrats’ 45, with two independents caucusing with the Democrats. Polls suggest the Republicans are on the verge of losing both.
House members serve two-year terms, so all 435 seats are up for election. Senators serve staggered six-year terms, with a third renewed every two years. This year, 35 Senate seats are going to polls.

articles.title: Naftali Bennett’s ‘B’Yachad’ faction throws support behind Gadi Eisenkot to form next Israeli government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The development comes as Israeli President Isaac Herzog has urged political leaders to accept the election results and find creative solutions to prevent another election

Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's 'B’Yachad' faction has thrown its support behind Yashar party chief Gadi Eisenkot, announcing that it will recommend him to President Isaac Herzog to form the next government amid a political deadlock following Tuesday's (October 27, 2026) Knesset elections.
Mr. Bennett announced the decision in a post on X, saying he had promised throughout the election campaign to respect the voters' decision and was now acting accordingly.
לאורך כל מערכת הבחירות הבטחתי לכבד את הכרעת הבוחר, וכך אני עושה כעת. על כן החלטתי שסיעת ״ביחד״ תמליץ לנשיא להטיל את מלאכת הרכבת הממשלה על גדי איזנקוט. בהצלחה גדי!

"Throughout the entire election campaign, I promised to respect the decision of the voter, and that is what I am doing now. Therefore, I have decided that the 'Together' faction will recommend to the president to entrust the task of forming the government to Gadi Eizenkot. Good luck, Gadi!" Mr. Bennett said.
Responding to Mr. Bennett, Mr. Eisenkot thanked him for the support and said, "Together, we will bring Israel back to the right path!"

The development comes as Israeli President Isaac Herzog has urged political leaders to accept the election results and find creative solutions to prevent another election, with neither of the main political blocs securing a clear majority in the 120-member Knesset.

According to The Times of Israel , Herzog said he would receive the official election results on November 4 before beginning consultations with representatives of political factions at the President's Residence.

The election results gave the opposition 67 seats against 53 for the incumbent coalition. However, the Opposition bloc comprises 48 seats held by Zionist factions and 19 secured by Arab non-Zionist parties, presenting a challenge to coalition formation.
Mr. Herzog urged party leaders to "stop climbing up trees and face the reality" of the election outcome, calling for flexibility to break the political deadlock.
The newly elected Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on November 10.

Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's 'B’Yachad' faction has thrown its support behind Yashar party chief Gadi Eisenkot, announcing that it will recommend him to President Isaac Herzog to form the next government amid a political deadlock following Tuesday's (October 27, 2026) Knesset elections.

The development comes as Israeli President Isaac Herzog has urged political leaders to accept the election results and find creative solutions to prevent another election, with neither of the main political blocs securing a clear majority in the 120-member Knesset.

According to The Times of Israel , Herzog said he would receive the official election results on November 4 before beginning consultations with representatives of political factions at the President's Residence.

The election results gave the opposition 67 seats against 53 for the incumbent coalition. However, the Opposition bloc comprises 48 seats held by Zionist factions and 19 secured by Arab non-Zionist parties, presenting a challenge to coalition formation.

Mr. Herzog urged party leaders to "stop climbing up trees and face the reality" of the election outcome, calling for flexibility to break the political deadlock.

The newly elected Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on November 10.

articles.title: Is there an alternative to corticosteroids to control vomiting during chemotherapy? A new study attempts to find out
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: An Indian multicentre phase III trial found that an olanzapine-based regimen, which is non-steroidal, was not inferior to the standard dexamethasone-based prophylaxis, which is a steroid, for vomiting control. More research, however, is needed to establish the findings widely

Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting are among the most distressing side effects of cancer treatment in children. Preventing them is essential not only to improve quality of life, but also to help patients complete treatment. Yet the medicines used to prevent vomiting can themselves cause adverse effects, making the search for safe alternatives an important challenge in paediatric oncology.

An Indian multicentre clinical trial suggests that olanzapine may offer an alternative to dexamethasone, a corticosteroid routinely used to prevent chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in children receiving highly emetogenic chemotherapy — treatment with a high risk of inducing vomiting. The current regimen using dexamethasone is a guideline that is used regularly, but dexamethasone is a corticosteroid. The study was aimed at finding a comparable, non-corticosteroid option.
