articles.title: Apple's new CEO John Ternus to face first earnings test as memory costs surge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Apple ⁠has been trying to position its AI offerings differently than rivals such as Meta ⁠Platforms’ Muse agent

John Ternus will host his first earnings call as ‌Apple’s CEO on Monday, with investors looking to the company’s forecast to determine whether ​a blitz of new products can help offset rising costs for memory chips.

Ternus, ⁠who took the reins from Tim Cook in September, has overseen the introduction of Apple’s first foldable phone, smart home hub and Apple’s first touch-screen laptops. All of those products began shipping during the company’s current fiscal first quarter, amid ‌what Cook had called a “100-year flood” of rising memory costs.

Apple will face scrutiny over three key issues: its crucial holiday-quarter outlook, Ternus’ remarks on AI and the revamped Siri, and ‌rising memory-chip costs that analysts expect to drag quarterly profit growth to its weakest in six ‌quarters.
Apple ⁠has been trying to position its AI offerings differently than rivals such as Meta ⁠Platforms’ Muse agent, which took App Store rankings by storm in recent weeks.

Rivals such as OpenAI, which Apple is suing over alleged trade-secret theft, are also developing devices aimed at displacing the iPhone as the central device in people’s lives. How Apple ​embraces AI could also have large implications ‌for the future of its services business, whose slowing growth has worried investors after years of rapid expansion.

“Recent agentic innovation far outpaces our experience with Siri AI, but Apple has acknowledged that Siri AI ... is far more focused on trust/privacy,” said Dan Morgan, portfolio manager at Synovus Trust, which owns ‌Apple shares.
Apple is marketing Apple’s AI systems toward “everyday people” rather than Silicon Valley insiders, who ​are big users of frontier AI models from the likes of OpenAI.
Morgan added that investors want to know whether Apple could profit by distributing third-party AI agents through ⁠its App Store and taking a cut of the business they generate.

For now, Apple’s reluctance to join the massive AI spending race has worked in its favour. Its shares have risen about 27% this year, ‌outperforming tech giants such as Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Amazon as investors seek shelter from mounting concerns over the cost of building AI infrastructure.

Analysts expect Apple to report a nearly 11% rise in revenue to $113.39 billion for the July-September period, the company’s fiscal fourth quarter, according to LSEG data. Net profit is expected to rise about 6% to $29.04 billion.
Apple’s services business is expected to grow almost 10% to $31.56 billion, its slowest pace in more than three years.

IPhone sales are projected to climb about 15% to $56.54 billion, ‌slowing from growth of about 22% in the previous three months. The results will capture just nine days of sales ​of the new iPhone 18 Pro models, while the iPhone Duo, the firm’s first foldable, came out on October 23, which will benefit the holiday quarter.

articles.title: Can India’s heritage produce find a place on the global food map?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Agri-food thinktank Vrihi Foundation’s new report explores how indigenous agricultural and forest produce such as turmeric, jamun, and mahua can gain stronger value chains, markets and policy support

Over the last few years, the farm-to-table trend has put a lot of variety on our plates. Think indigenous ingredients such as native greens and nuts, different ways of cooking, and a deeper understanding of India’s vast agricultural ecosystem that extends into our forests and villages.

Having said that, how often do these ingredients make their way into the mainstream culinary ecosystem? Om Routray, founder of agri-food thinktank Indian Culinary Agenda and its parent organisation, Vrihi Foundation, aims to change this with a policy report on India’s heritage produce that launched recently.
A close-up shot capturing the ripening clusters of Carissa carandas, commonly known as Karonda or Bengal currant | Photo Credit: Jayantibhai Movaliya

Covering both agriculture and forest produce, the report — created alongside The Asia Foundation and social enterprise Ekgaon — aims to not only spotlight India’s vast agricultural heritage but also proposes an operational framework with GI tagged commodity value chains, and awareness among policy makers and consumers. Elaborating on the stakeholders and researchers involved in the project, Om says that the team studied producers, processors, retailers, culinary schools, and Government agencies.

Om, who has been working on digital technologies in agriculture for a decade, talks about how the startup he worked for operated in 37 countries, but never really took off in India. “The realisation came that no matter how much we work on the agriculture side, unless we work on the complete value chain, commodity ecosystems will not be elevated as a whole. The subsequent onslaught of ingredients such as California almonds , Australian lamb, etc. also demonstrated that we are not being fair with the agro-forest heritage that we have,” he says.

The report makes a case for Indian produce such as turmeric , jamun, mahua that are ‘uniquely Indian and most are rare outside the subcontinent’. While some are GI-tagged , there is a lot that needs to be done to fully tap their potential as ‘the impact of the certification has not been uniformly beneficial and, in many instances, not equally distributed’. “Kandhamal turmeric is a great example,” says Om. “Both individual farmers and Kandhamal as a district have not benefited much from the GI tag and the constant spotlight that the commodity has brought. For instance, there are no upmarket retail stores nor any processing capacity built in the district.”

The report also spotlights the fact that most commodities are facing climate-related challenges. For instance, jamuns from Jambhulgaon in Maharashtra are facing yield and harvest issues due to unseasonal rains shifting flowering. Also, women majorly collect and process most heritage commodities and there have been very few technological interventions to remove drudgery.
Jamuns at a street market in New Delhi | Photo Credit: MelanieMaya

So, how can things change? The report makes a case for import substitution by increased utilisation of indigenous commodities by promoting them better, and bringing in a strong supply chain. Take, for instance, nuts. “We have floated the idea of a Himalayan Nuts Association that promotes indigenous nuts on the lines of California almonds. Many chefs are using jamuns instead of blueberries in cheesecakes. We have not even scratched the surface when it comes to indigenous mushrooms,” explains Om, while sharing the example of mahua syrup. “It is already seeing early adoption as a replacement for maple syrup across bakeries and restaurants. Mahua resins are a great substitution for imported resins and a similar case can be made for indigenous dry fruits.”

The report also highlights the need for diversifying India’s export basket , the bulk of which comprises rice, wheat, etc. Om says that the team has recommended two paths. “One is to de-focus from generic exports. For example, there may not be much long-term value in exporting dragon fruits from Odisha as there is no reason why global markets will perceive it as a premium product. So, we must do a terroir-culture fit before introducing new commodities in productive regions,” says Om.
Indian farmer on a rice paddy field in Uttarakhand | Photo Credit: umesh negi

But how does one decide what counts as ‘heritage produce’, and how do we keep it from becoming a label that larger firms cash-in on. Om says, “We have created a definition of what should qualify as Heritage Produce. It is now for the funding agencies, Government departments, retailers and farmer coops to adopt. There is no harm in larger farms using the label so long as the producer communities receive the benefits.”

Om Routray, founder of agri-food thinktank Indian Culinary Agenda and its parent organisation, Vrihi Foundation, aims to change this with a policy report on India’s heritage produce that launched recently.

A close-up shot capturing the ripening clusters of Carissa carandas, commonly known as Karonda or Bengal currant | Photo Credit: Jayantibhai Movaliya

Covering both agriculture and forest produce, the report — created alongside The Asia Foundation and social enterprise Ekgaon — aims to not only spotlight India’s vast agricultural heritage but also proposes an operational framework with GI tagged commodity value chains, and awareness among policy makers and consumers. Elaborating on the stakeholders and researchers involved in the project, Om says that the team studied producers, processors, retailers, culinary schools, and Government agencies.

Om, who has been working on digital technologies in agriculture for a decade, talks about how the startup he worked for operated in 37 countries, but never really took off in India. “The realisation came that no matter how much we work on the agriculture side, unless we work on the complete value chain, commodity ecosystems will not be elevated as a whole. The subsequent onslaught of ingredients such as California almonds , Australian lamb, etc. also demonstrated that we are not being fair with the agro-forest heritage that we have,” he says.

The report makes a case for Indian produce such as turmeric , jamun, mahua that are ‘uniquely Indian and most are rare outside the subcontinent’. While some are GI-tagged , there is a lot that needs to be done to fully tap their potential as ‘the impact of the certification has not been uniformly beneficial and, in many instances, not equally distributed’. “Kandhamal turmeric is a great example,” says Om. “Both individual farmers and Kandhamal as a district have not benefited much from the GI tag and the constant spotlight that the commodity has brought. For instance, there are no upmarket retail stores nor any processing capacity built in the district.”

The report also spotlights the fact that most commodities are facing climate-related challenges. For instance, jamuns from Jambhulgaon in Maharashtra are facing yield and harvest issues due to unseasonal rains shifting flowering. Also, women majorly collect and process most heritage commodities and there have been very few technological interventions to remove drudgery.

Jamuns at a street market in New Delhi | Photo Credit: MelanieMaya

So, how can things change? The report makes a case for import substitution by increased utilisation of indigenous commodities by promoting them better, and bringing in a strong supply chain. Take, for instance, nuts. “We have floated the idea of a Himalayan Nuts Association that promotes indigenous nuts on the lines of California almonds. Many chefs are using jamuns instead of blueberries in cheesecakes. We have not even scratched the surface when it comes to indigenous mushrooms,” explains Om, while sharing the example of mahua syrup. “It is already seeing early adoption as a replacement for maple syrup across bakeries and restaurants. Mahua resins are a great substitution for imported resins and a similar case can be made for indigenous dry fruits.”

The report also highlights the need for diversifying India’s export basket , the bulk of which comprises rice, wheat, etc. Om says that the team has recommended two paths. “One is to de-focus from generic exports. For example, there may not be much long-term value in exporting dragon fruits from Odisha as there is no reason why global markets will perceive it as a premium product. So, we must do a terroir-culture fit before introducing new commodities in productive regions,” says Om.

Indian farmer on a rice paddy field in Uttarakhand | Photo Credit: umesh negi

But how does one decide what counts as ‘heritage produce’, and how do we keep it from becoming a label that larger firms cash-in on. Om says, “We have created a definition of what should qualify as Heritage Produce. It is now for the funding agencies, Government departments, retailers and farmer coops to adopt. There is no harm in larger farms using the label so long as the producer communities receive the benefits.”

1. Core Context & Background: Agri-food thinktank Vrihi Foundation’s new report explores how indigenous agricultural and forest produce such as turmeric, jamun, and mahua can gain stronger value chains, markets and policy support

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Over the last few years, the farm-to-table trend has put a lot of variety on our plates. Think indigenous ingredients such as native greens and nuts, different ways of cooking, and a deeper understanding of India’s vast agricultural ecosystem that extends into our forests and villages.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: But how does one decide what counts as ‘heritage produce’, and how do we keep it from becoming a label that larger firms cash-in on. Om says, “We have created a definition of what should qualify as Heritage Produce. It is now for the funding agencies, Government departments, retailers and farmer coops to adopt. There is no harm in larger farms using the label so long as the producer communities receive the benefits.”

articles.title: Who decides the cost of medicines in India?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: India’s separation of medicine licensing under CDSCO and pricing under NPPA presents a policy challenge. Stronger coordination,supported by pharmaceutical, clinical and health-economic expertise, could bridge this gap

A cancer medicine supplied to a retailer for ₹2,700 carries a maximum retail price (MRP) of ₹27,000. Who accounts for this tenfold difference? This was among the examples highlighted by the Supreme Court in September 2026, when it questioned the gap between the prices paid for medicines and what patients ultimately pay.

Subsequently, on October 17, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) announced a 30% cap on trade margins for 137 anti-cancer drugs, effective from November 9. This intervention could reduce prices substantially for some products. It also raises a broader question: how does India decide what medicines should cost?

articles.title: Citing GST revenue decline, Stalin says Tamil Nadu is ‘doomed’ under TVK government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The DMK president said the State’s growth rate in GST revenue had fallen below the national average

DMK president and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on Monday (November 2, 2026) said people should brace for difficult times as “Tamil Nadu was doomed” under the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government.

In a social media post, he said the State’s growth rate in Goods and Services Tax (GST) revenue had fallen below the national average under the TVK government. He also alleged that Korean investments worth ₹1,614 crore had been lost and gone to Andhra Pradesh because of the State government’s indifference.

“Guidance Tamil Nadu, which attracted investments, has been sacrificed because of the ego of individuals. One should learn from this government how to shift to reverse gear. But, the Chief Minister, who could not understand any of this, has gone to campaign in the byelections,” he said.

articles.title: Keralam govt. transfers 35 officers in major IAS reshufle
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prasanth N. has been posted as chairman and managing director, Kerala State Electricity Board, and T.V. Anupama as Secretary, Finance (Expenditure) department
The Keralam government has transferred 35 IAS officers in yet another major bureaucratic reshuffle.

K.R. Jyothilal, who was serving as Additional Chief Secretary of Finance, Taxes, and Public Procurement Advisory departments and as chief executive officer of the Rebuild Kerala Initiative in Planning and Economic Affairs department, has been posted as Additional Chief Secretary of the Home and Vigilance departments. He will also hold full additional charge of the Water Resources department, Housing department and Coir (Industries) department.

Puneet Kumar, who was serving as Resident Commissioner of Kerala House in New Delhi and Additional Chief Secretary of the Water Resources department (matters connected with inter-State water), has been posted as Additional Chief Secretary of the Power department. He will also hold full additional charge of Officer on Special Duty in Coordination and Programme Management Division in the office of the Chief Secretary. He will continue as Resident Commissioner of Kerala House in New Delhi.
Tinku Biswal has been relieved from the additional charge of Officer on Special Duty in Coordination and Programme Management Division in the office of the Chief Secretary.

Minhaj Alam, Additional Chief Secretary of Home and Vigilance departments and Agriculture department, has been posted as Additional Chief Secretary of the Finance department. The officer will also hold full additional charge of Taxes and Public Procurement Advisory departments, and as chief executive officer of the Rebuild Kerala Initiative and chairman of the Kerala Financial Corporation.

Mohammed Hanish A.P.M., Additional Chief Secretary of Industries, Revenue (Waqf) and External Co-operation departments, has been posted as Additional Chief Secretary of the Health and Family Welfare department. The officer will also hold full additional charge of Ayush, General Education, Revenue (Waqf), and Minority Welfare departments.

Sharmila Mary Joseph, Principal Secretary of Health and Family Welfare and Ayush departments, has been posted as Principal Secretary of the Transport department. The officer will hold full additional charge of the Women and Child Development department.

M. Beena, on return from Central deputation, has been posted as Principal Secretary of the Industries department. The officer will also hold full additional charge of matters related to External Co-operation.

Prasanth N., Special Secretary of Sports and Youth Affairs, Zoos and Museum, and Taxes departments, has been posted as chairman and managing director of the Kerala State Electricity Board Limited. The officer will continue to hold charge as Special Secretary of the Sports and Youth Affairs department.

M.G. Rajamanickam, chairman and managing director of the Kerala State Electricity Board Limited and Secretary of Power and Environment departments, has been posted as Secretary of the Local Self-Government department. The officer will continue to hold additional charge of Revenue (Devaswom) department and Commissioner, Guruvayur and Koodalmanikyam Devaswoms.

Anupama T.V., Secretary of Local Self-government and Transport (Aviation, Metro and Railway) departments, and chairman and managing director of the Kerala Transport Development Finance Corporation, has been posted as Secretary of the Finance (Expenditure) department. The officer will also hold additional charge of the Environment department.
Gokul G.R. has been relieved from the charge of Finance (Expenditure) department and Geromic George from the charge of Finance (Expenditure) department.

articles.title: Government notifies grievance redressal rules under VB-G RAM G Act; fixes 15-day deadline
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the Rural Development Ministry, grievances can be submitted in person, through speed post, a designated digital platform, telephone helplines or any other mode decided by state governments.

The Centre has notified rules for grievance redressal under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, mandating that complaints related to the implementation of the rural employment scheme be resolved within 15 days and providing for their escalation if they remain pending beyond the prescribed period.

Under the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Grievance Redressal Rules, 2026, notified by the Union Ministry of Rural Development, state governments will have to establish a three-tier mechanism at gram panchayat, block and district levels, the Ministry said in a statement issued on Monday (November 2, 2026).
The rules provide for designated grievance redressal officers at each level to receive, register, enquire into and dispose of complaints.
According to the Ministry, grievances can be submitted in person, through speed post, a designated digital platform, telephone helplines or any other mode decided by state governments.
No grievance can be refused registration on the grounds of its format, language, manner of submission or any procedural deficiency, the statement said.

All complaints received physically at gram panchayat, block or district level will have to be entered on the designated digital platform on the day of receipt or, if that is not feasible, by the next working day.
The complainant will receive an acknowledgement with a registration number, date of receipt and designation of the receiving authority.
The rules stipulate that an enquiry into a grievance must be completed within seven working days of its receipt, while the complaint must be resolved within 15 days.

The designated officer can call for relevant records, documents, reports and electronic data from the authorities concerned and provide the complainant an opportunity to be heard, either in person or electronically, wherever necessary.

Complaints not resolved within 15 days will be escalated to the next higher level under the mechanism established by the state government. Such cases will continue to be monitored electronically until their disposal.
A district programme coordinator will oversee grievance redressal at the district level and ensure that complaints are addressed through the designated mechanism and digital infrastructure.

The rules also provide for appeals against orders passed under the grievance redressal mechanism, in accordance with Schedule I of the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025.

fullParagraphs: The proposal, which seeks to replace the Breeding of and Experiments on Animals (Control and Supervision) Rule, if notified in their present form, could weaken existing safeguards for animals used in laboratory experiments, PETA India said

Several celebrities, politicians, scientists, veterinarians and animal welfare organisations have raised concerns over the proposed Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Control and Supervision of Experiment, Breeding and Trading of Laboratory Animals) Rules, 2026, with more than 18,000 people signing a petition seeking its withdrawal, according to People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) India.

Actors John Abraham, Tabu, Hema Malini, Raveena Tandon, Shilpa Shetty, Jacqueline Fernandez, Dia Mirza, Rupali Ganguly and Wamiqa Gabbi, among others, have signed the petition, while cricketer K.L. Rahul has also endorsed the appeal, PETA India said in a statement.

Several parliamentarians across political parties, including Lok Sabha MP Hema Malini, Rajya Sabha MP Sulata Deo, Lok Sabha MP Dr Mohammad Jawed and former Union Minister Renuka Chowdhury, have also signed the appeal, it added.

The appeal has also received support from more than 100 Indian and international scientists, over 100 veterinarians and more than 60 animal protection organisations, while over 18,000 people have signed a petition through PETA India's website, the statement said.
The proposal seeks to replace the Breeding of and Experiments on Animals (Control and Supervision) Rules, 1998.
It seeks to reduce bureaucratic delays and fast-track approvals of pharmaceutical, medical, and academic research through institutional self-regulation.

According to the Government, the draft rules actively strengthen animal welfare and ethical accountability while modernising scientific research. It has invited objections and suggestions till November 5.
But PETA India claims that the proposed rules, if notified in their present form, could weaken existing safeguards for animals used in laboratory experiments.
It added that the provisions could increase the capture and use of protected wildlife for experiments and allow community dogs and cats to be used in laboratories under specified circumstances.

The organisation also raised concerns over the continuation of experiments involving severe pain and distress, including inescapable electric shocks, induced tumours and toxicity tests in which death is an endpoint.

It further alleged that the draft rules would reduce oversight of the Central Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals (CCSEA) over several experiments and dilute existing safeguards relating to anaesthesia, euthanasia and rehabilitation.

"India has already demonstrated remarkable leadership in advancing non-animal science, and that is something every Indian can be proud of. We must build on this progress, not move backward," PETA India's science and research policy advisor Dr Noopur Jain said.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu Live updates: Heavy rain lashes Konaseema as cyclone Murasu nears Andhra coast
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: System intensifies into ‘Severe Cyclonic Storm’, likely to cross the south Andhra coast, between 11.30 p.m. today and 4 a.m. on November 3

P.L.N. Murthy, Head of the Cyclone Warning Centre, Visakhapatnam, said the cyclone is expected to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, between 11.30 p.m. on November 2 and 4 a.m. on November 3, 2026. The wind speed during landfall is likely to be 100-110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph. A storm surge of about 1.5-2 metres above the astronomical tide is very likely to inundate low-lying areas of South Coastal Andhra Pradesh. The maximum peak surge is expected in Bapatla and parts of Krishna and Prakasam districts.
He also warned that the storm surge could inundate low-lying areas even before landfall, as it is expected to begin three to four hours ahead of the cyclone’s landfall.
In the backdrop of the Murasu cyclone, the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) 10th Battalion has undertaken extensive preparations.
It has deployed a total of 14 NDRF teams—11 from Andhra Pradesh and 03 from Tamil Nadu—to areas likely to be affected by the cyclone.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to take all precautionary measures to prevent loss of life and property in Bapatla district in view of Cyclone Murasu , which has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm.
He reviewed the preparedness of district administrations through a video conference on Monday (November 2, 2026), attended by Bapatla Collector Vinod Kumar V.

Owing to waterlogging, several bus route roads in Chennai have started falling apart, as the northern and central regions of the city received widespread heavy rainfall due to Cyclone Murasu since Sunday (November 1, 2026) night.

A name rooted in Tamil’s cultural past is travelling across the Bay of Bengal as a weather warning. As the severe cyclonic storm advances towards the Indian coast, ‘Murasu ’ , a Tamil name suggested by the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), Chennai, has found its place in the region’s meteorological history.

With Cyclone Murasu likely to make landfall at Andhra Pradesh coast between evening of Monday (November 2, 2026) and early morning of Wednesday (November 3, 2026), the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for two Telangana districts and an orange alert in three districts for Tuesday (November 3, 2026).
Cyclone Murasu has brought heavy rain to Konaseema in Andhra Pradesh, flooding homes and leaving elderly residents struggling.
Farmers are still recovering from damage caused by Cyclone Arnab, while power restoration has also been delayed.

The IMD said Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rain today (November 2), with isolated very heavy rain, and isolated heavy rain again on November 3 and from November 5 to 7.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay inaugurates new bus stand at Pudukottai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Chief Minister, who was on his maiden visit to the district after assuming charge in May, distributed welfare assistance totalling ₹62.73 to 13,676 beneficiaries and inaugurated 44 completed works

On his maiden visit to Pudukottai after assuming office, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Monday distributed welfare assistance of ₹62.73 crore to 13,676 beneficiaries in the district and inaugurated the redeveloped new bus stand in the town.

Mr. Vijay inaugurated 44 completed projects worth ₹68.31 crore and laid the foundation for 70 new works worth ₹11.72 crore but did not address the gathering at the function organised by the district administration at the Collectorate.

The venue of the event, planned to be held at the District Armed Reserve grounds, was changed all of a sudden in the late hours on Sunday to the annexe building inside the sprawling District Collectorate premises where arrangements were made in a swift manner. Prior to that the Armed Reserve ground was being prepared on a feverish pace there to host the event.

Later, Mr. Vijay inaugurated the new bus stand that was redeveloped after the old structures were demolished and rebuilt at a cost of ₹23.25 crore. He went around the facility for about 15 minutes accompanied by his Cabinet colleagues, P. Madhusudhan Reddy, Director of Municipal Administration, and other officials.

Constructed by the Municipal Administration and Water Supply department on an area measuring 20,077 square metres, the new bus stand has 60 bays, 74 shops, a couple of restaurants, passenger waiting hall, and toilets. It has a police control room, a feeding room, and a reverse osmosis plant among other facilities.

The other projects inaugurated by the Chief Minister include the Arivusaar Maiyam (Knowledge Centre) constructed at Santhaipettai in Alangudi town panchayat and a seed storage godown at Vamban in Thiruvarankulam taluk.

Earlier, the Chief Minister, who arrived by a special flight at the Tiruchi International Airport from Chennai in the morning reached Pudukottai by road. Public and partymen lined up and cheered the Chief Minister at various points along the nearly 50-km Tiruchi-Pudukottai national highway stretch.

The Chief Minister reached the Pudukottai District Collectorate around 11.40 a.m. He was received by the Minister for Labour Welfare and Skill Development J. Mohamed Farvas and District Collector M. Aruna at the entrance of the annexe building. After receiving a guard of honour, Mr. Vijay had a look at the farm equipment kept on display and proceeded to the function venue.

Minister for Rural Development and Water Resources N. Anand, Lok Sabha MPs Durai Vaiko, S. Jothimani, and K. Navas Kani, Gandharvakottai MLA N. Subramanian and senior officials participated. After distributing welfare assistance to beneficiaries, Mr. Vijay received petitions from a few members of the public.

Thereafter, the Chief Minister proceeded on board his customised vehicle to the new bus stand in the town with crowds cheering him along the stretch braving the intense heat. A few of them standing near the bus stand fainted and were immediately shifted from the spot by the police personnel and given first aid.

​China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi said ‌on Monday (November 2, 2026) that all parties ​in the West Asia conflict ⁠should focus on political solutions rather than resorting to arms again, in a ‌meeting with an Iranian national security official in Beijing.

Dialogue ‌and negotiation are the way ‌to ⁠resolve West Asia conflicts, Mr. Wang ⁠told Ali Bagheri Kani, the Deputy Secretary of the Iran Supreme National Security Council, ​according to ‌Chinese state news agency Xinhua .
Mr. Wang also said China supports Iran in safeguarding its sovereignty and security.

Earlier on ‌Monday (November 2, 2026), Chinese President Xi Jinping ​told Omani leader Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said that ⁠the West Asia and Gulf region should not become a battleground for ‌great-power rivalry.
BRICS parliamentary forum expresses ‘deep concern’ about West Asian hostilities

In a China-Oman joint statement that followed, Muscat said it supports the Chinese peace proposals for West Asia, and looks forward to a "greater role" by ‌Beijing in achieving lasting stability in the ​region.
China, which is pressing for a bigger diplomatic role ⁠in West Asia, also announced that ⁠its special envoy to West Asia, would visit Iran, ‌Oman and Saudi Arabia this month.

fullParagraphs: The U.S. midterm elections on November 3 determine control of Congress, with all 435 House seats, about one-third of the 100 Senate seats, and numerous state governorships up for grabs, in a nationwide vote that weakens or strengthens the President’s agenda depending on which party prevails.

Every four years, halfway through a sitting president’s four-year term, the U.S. holds a nationwide poll known as the midterm elections. Although the White House occupant is not directly up for re-election in this vote, the outcome serves as a de facto referendum on the current administration’s leadership and political agenda.
The legislative branch, the U.S. Congress, is entirely at stake, as voters elect representatives to all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, who serve two-year terms.

At the same time, 35 of the 100 U.S. Senate seats which carry six-year terms are up for grabs (33 regular elections and two special elections in Florida and Ohio) alongside the state gubernatorial seats that decide chief executives across numerous states. articles.title: What a new global study on pain reveals about women’s experiences
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The study’s findings about women having a higher prevalence of pain across anatomical sites, resonate with observations from India, say experts, noting that even so, women’s pain has historically been under-recognised, misunderstood, or inadequately treated

Women are more likely than men to report pain across every one of the 11 anatomical sites examined in a global study involving more than 6.1 million people across 118 countries. The study found that differences were particularly pronounced for facial pain, headaches and abdominal pain.

Published in Nature Medicine , the study found that women had 83% higher relative prevalence of facial pain, 74% higher prevalence of headaches and 60% higher prevalence of stomach or abdominal pain than men. Women were also more likely to report high-intensity and widespread pain, highlighting a disparity that extends beyond the occurrence of pain to its severity and distribution.

Scientific & Technical Core: Innovations led by ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, and national research institutes are advancing India's capabilities in space exploration, quantum computing, biotechnology, and clean energy.

articles.title: Shock and regret: scientists react to AI roiling life’s work
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: OpenAI and Anthropic each said last week that one of their AI models had disproved the exponential time hypothesis
For decades, three computer scientists built their careers around an idea about the limits of what computers can do.
Artificial intelligence may now have shown it to be wrong: OpenAI and Anthropic each said last week that one of their AI models had disproved the exponential time hypothesis (ETH).
The hypothesis holds that some problems are so hard that computers can solve them only by trying nearly every possible answer. Hundreds of studies in computer science and biology rely on it.

The claim is the latest in a string of AI results that have shaken academia, setting off soul-searching, most notably among mathematicians, over the value of human expertise and the future of their profession.

Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi of the University of California San Diego first proposed the hypothesis around 25 years ago. Ryan Williams of MIT, a leading researcher in the field, had long publicly doubted it. The three are now helping organise an independent review of the claims from the AI companies.
Q: How did you feel when you learned that a machine may have overturned this hypothesis?
Ryan Williams: I did not fully believe the hypothesis, and I’m on the record as a prominent sceptic. So I felt vindicated.

Russell Impagliazzo: I’m afraid I am less cheerful about this than the others. I would have much preferred it to be discovered by a human who could explain their thought process. And I’d like to have shaken the (actual) hand of the person who disproved ETH.
Q: What is left for human researchers facing the machine? What would you tell a student?

Paturi: These breakthroughs extend the frontier of research, but I believe shaping that frontier and moving it forward remain within human capacity and creativity. I would encourage young students to join. They should learn to use these tools while developing their own judgment.

Williams: I think we’re starting to experience a major revolution in the field, and it is absolutely worth going into. Some people may not want to work in the field anymore; others may now feel motivated to.

Impagliazzo: I’m less confident. The rate of change is amazing. Until now, the same researchers mostly did both the glamorous part of research, solving, and the less glamorous part, verifying and explaining. Now it looks like much or most of the first will be done by AI, leaving humans the second -- until next year, when AI progresses further. I have no idea what research will be like next year.

articles.title: Clinging on: On Netanyahu and the Israel elections
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Netanyahu’s continuance will be bad news for Israel and the region

Benjamin Netanyahu was at the centre of Israel’s October 27 elections. For Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw a genocidal war in Gaza following Hamas’s October 7 attack , the election was the biggest test of his political career. For the Opposition, which promised to hold him accountable for the failures of October 7 and end the country’s “forever wars”, the election offered an opportunity to oust him from power. The results, however, sent a mixed message. With 85.6% of the votes counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has lost its majority but is still the largest bloc . His Likud party is projected to win 26 seats, while its main rival Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to secure 21. Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, the far-right extremist parties in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, demonstrated their continued strength, winning 13 seats between them. The dark horse, however, could be the Arab parties — the Joint List is projected to win 12 seats while the United Arab List (Ra’am) could secure seven seats. With neither bloc commanding a majority, the Arab parties could propel the opposition coalition to power. But the big question is whether the anti-Netanyahu coalition is ready to join hands with the Arab parties, which have historically been kept on the margins of Israel’ s power politics.

Mr. Netanyahu’s central promise has been that only he can guarantee Israel’s security. Yet, the October 7 attack took place on his watch and he has refused to take responsibility for the failures that led to it. A wanted man by the International Criminal Court, he has repeated, before and after October 7, that a Palestine state would not be formed while he is in power. His war on Gaza has killed over 70,000 Palestinians, including 20,000 children, and displaced the region’s population. Israel’s brutal occupation machinery has also expanded and tightened its control of the West Bank, while settler terrorists have unleashed violence on Palestinian households. His war on Iran has been a disaster, with global economic consequences. Mr. Netanyahu has sought to portray his wars as bold, necessary moves to protect Israel, while exploiting Israelis’ security concerns for political gain. He may not be voted out immediately, but his failure to secure a majority and the decline in his party’s popularity are significant. The Opposition should take its cue from the results and form a broad coalition with the Arab parties. It should restore accountability in governance, revisit his unchecked militarism and rebuild ties with the world. If Mr. Netanyahu continues to cling to power, it would be bad news for Israel and the region.

articles.title: Hunker down: On Cyclone Arnab, its landfall
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Proactive governance kept the casualties low after Cyclone Arnab

Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.

Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

articles.title: Devotees worried over conduct of Kandasashti festival at Kandakottam temple
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Devotees of the Sri Muthukumaraswamy Temple, popularly known as Kandhakottam in Rattan Bazaar in Park Town, are worried about the conduct of the Kandasashthi festival this year.

"Usually, tickets for the Laksharcharnai during the annual festival are sold just after Vijayadasami. Till date, the administration has not started selling tickets. Every year around 35,000 tickets each priced at ₹300 are sold to devotees who want to participate in the archanai that is slated to start on November 10. There is no sign of the conduct of the festival so far," said A. B. Srinivasan, a 65-year-old devotee.

Saravanan, another devotee, said that this year would be the 99 th consecutive year of the Kandasashthi festival during which grand concerts would be held. "Participants of the archanai would be given prasadam including a bucket. Tenders for procuring various items such as pandals, coconuts, bags, and flowers are yet to be called for. We hear that the executive officer has gone on leave and another person has taken charge," he said.

The over 500-year-old shrine, is a scheme temple, meaning it belongs to a particular community - in this case, the Berri Chettis. A five-member team was chosen from the community as trustees last year and they have also been in charge of the daily running of the temple.

Sendilvellan, one of the trustees, said that the executive officer had taken away cheque signatory powers from the trustees and the trustees were unable to pay salaries even. "He has gone to the bank and taken signatory powers without informing us. We seem to have absolutely no powers in the day-to-day running of the temple. The court had directed the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments department to interfere only if there was any problem relating to the conduct of the temple. From last year, we have been managing the temple without any problems," he said.

Another trustee said that with just a few days left for the festival they have been running from pillar to post trying to get the powers back and conduct it. Sources in the HR&CE Department said they will look into the matter.

articles.title: Rajasthan IPS officer removed after ACB probe ordered against IAS husband
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Rajasthan government on Saturday placed an Indian Police Service (IPS) officer, Prashakha Mathur, on awaiting posting order (APO) after an investigation by the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) was approved against her husband and senior Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Shikhar Agrawal.

Mr. Agrawal, who was also sent on APO earlier this week, is facing charges along with his family members of purchasing 40 villas in luxury resorts operated by a private firm in Udaipur and Alwar districts by allegedly abusing his position and influence and extending “undue benefits” to the firm.

While Mr. Agrawal was serving as the Additional Chief Secretary (Industries) and additionally held charge of four public sector corporations, his wife Ms. Mathur, a 1995-batch IPS officer, was posted as Additional Director General in charge of Planning, Modernisation and Welfare.

The ACB has alleged that Mr. Agrawal gave benefits such as relaxations in resort construction conditions, approvals without verification of certificates and special concessional packages to the firm. The alleged purchases of villas were made in the names of Mr. Agrawal and Ms. Mathur, their two sons, and Mr. Agrawal’s parents-in-law.

The ACB has registered a Preliminary Enquiry (PE) and launched an investigation into the allegations of abuse of official position, conflict of interest, and extending undue benefits to the firm in question.

ACB Director General Govind Gupta said the properties were allegedly purchased at prices substantially below their market value. The ACB’s probe will examine whether the alleged benefits caused substantial financial losses to the State government and whether Mr. Agrawal and his family members acquired assets disproportionate to their known sources of income.

Mr. Agrawal was appointed Additional Chief Secretary in the Chief Minister’s Office in February 2024, shortly after Bhajan Lal Sharma took oath as the CM, and served in that position till November 2025. Former CM Ashok Gehlot has demanded investigation by Central agencies into the matter, describing it as the “biggest scandal” under the Bharatiya Janata Party government.

articles.title: At CEC’s ‘public impeachment’, voters question deletion of names from rolls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Student leaders and activists also spoke at the event, which was held at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence in New Delhi

The Indian National Developmental, Inclusive Alliance’s symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday (October 31, 2026) featured accounts from voters who alleged that their names had been deleted from electoral rolls during the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise.
Among them was Anita Jaiswal, who moved from Kolkata to Delhi. She said she had voted in every election between 2012 and 2025 but was now being asked to establish her citizenship.
ALSO WATCH Watch: INDIA bloc leaders present united front against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, holds mock impeachment

“I am a single mother. They told me to get an Aadhaar card, saying it would prove that I am a citizen. Who gave you the right to remove my voter ID? My daughter gets a scholarship, has a bank account and an Aadhaar card, and now you are deleting our names. Who gave you the right?” she asked, adding, “Prove which country I am from.”

Iftikar Ahmed, another voter from Kolkata, said he had voted in the same Chowrangee constituency for 20 years but received a notice during the SIR hearing seeking documents because of a mapping discrepancy. His father, too, had been voting from the same address for two decades, he said. “Our names have been removed in a planned manner,” he alleged.

Nikhil Dey, founder of Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan, who has been working with affected voters, introduced Kanta Prasad, who had been declared dead in the exercise. “He spoke very convincingly for a corpse! The deprivation of the right to vote is a crime against the Constitution and a blot on our democracy. There must be accountability,” Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said in a post on X.
ALSO WATCH Rahul Gandhi: Deletion of 1 in 7 voters makes 2024 election ‘illegitimate’ | INDIA bloc

RTI activist Anjali Bharadwaj said that in response to an application seeking copies of files recording the decision-making process behind the SIR, the Election Commission of India (ECI) had replied that no such file existed.
“T.C. Kom, who is a Principal Secretary, said the ECI had not taken any decision to conduct an SIR,” Ms. Bharadwaj claimed.
Swaraj Abhiyan chief Yogendra Yadav described Mr. Kumar as the “Mukhya Chunav Abhiyukt (Chief Election Culprit)” rather than the “Mukhya Chunav Ayukt (Chief Election Commissioner)”.

All India Students’ Association (AISA) national president Neha Bora alleged that the SIR was a deliberate attempt to disenfranchise young voters and undermine democracy. Questioning the functioning of electoral registration officers (EROs), she said their statutory authority was being overridden through the use of software to exclude eligible voters. “You have abused your public office and favoured one political party,” she alleged.

The programme was held in the garden of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence in New Delhi. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the proceedings, while Mr. Kharge moved the motion.

articles.title: Two persons held for possession of country-made guns, explosives
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two persons, including a farmer, were arrested for possession of two country made guns and crude bombs near Pallikonda and Pernambut towns in Vellore on Saturday.
Forest officials identified the arrested persons as U. Chandru, 21, a tribal from Irular community, and G. Srinivasan, 39, a farmer.

Initial inquiry revealed that Srinivasan has been cultivating paddy and groundnuts on his two acre farmland. Forest officials said that, based on a tip-off, a special team conducted searches at his house and farmland, and found country made guns, explosives, nets, torchlights, and batteries.
Forest officials said that Srinivasan procured guns from his contacts in Kerala. He used pellets to hunt monkeys, rabbits, and spotted deer in forests surrounding Jawadhu Hills.

In a separate incident, forest officials arrested Chandru, who was allegedly loitering with a country-made gun in the area. The team nabbed him during a regular patrol and seized the country-made gun, pellets, and explosives.
Forest officials said both arrested persons were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. Further probe is under way.

articles.title: New bridge to be opened near Sholinghur to replace British-era structure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A new ₹3.85 crore high-level bridge across the Rendadi Water Supply Channel near Ponnai River, at Sekkadikuppam village near Sholinghur town in Ranipet will be opened for public use by December this year.

Officials of the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA), which executes the work, said that the new facility was a long-standing demand of at least eight surrounding farming villages across the water channel. The new bridge will replace the British-era causeway, which was damaged during 2021 floods in the water channel, fed by Ponnai river.

The new bridge will provide easy access to villagers in Ranipet and Thiruvallur districts. “The new bridge will help farmers to transport farm products to common markets in surrounding big towns. Buses will also be operated to reach remote villages,” S. Kannan, Assistant Engineer (AE), DRDA (Sholinghur), told The Hindu.

On Saturday, Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspected the under-construction bridge in the presence of S. Selvarani, Project Director (PD), DRDA (Ranipet), and Prabhakaran, Executive Engineer (EE), DRDA (Ranipet). “During monsoon, residents could not cross the water channel due to chest-deep water. The new bridge will be a lifeline for residents as ambulances and government buses can reach remote villages in the region,” said T. Perumal, a farmer.

DRDA officials said that the new bridge will replace the dilapidated causeway, which was demolished for the work, to connect surrounding villages with towns like Sholinghur, Arakkonam, Tiruvallur, and Tiruttani.

Funded under the State Special Assistance Scheme for 2025-26, the new bridge will be 38 metres long and 7.5 metres wide. It can discharge around 30,000 cusecs of water per second. The new facility has been built at least three metres above the water channel to prevent inundation during floods.

The new bridge will have tiled footpaths, LED lights, inlets to discharge rainwater into the river, reflectors, signboards and hand railings. Approach roads will also be laid to connect surrounding villages with the new facility.

For residents, the new bridges will end a detour of at least eight kms to reach the nearest towns in Ranipet and Thiruvallur districts. It will provide easy access to basic facilities like government schools, health centres, banks, ATMs, agricultural office, cooperative society and taluk office, residents said.

articles.title: Two arrested for attempting to determine sex of foetus in Tirupattur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two persons were arrested by Vaniyambadi Taluk police in Tirupattur district on Saturday for conducting a sex determination test and attempting abortion of a foetus.
Police identified the arrested persons as K. Indrarani, 60, and S. Geetha, 45. They are residents of Chittoor district in Andhra Pradesh.
Initial inquiry revealed that V. Jagadeesan, 34, and his wife J. Pavithra, 28, both wage labourers, have two daughters.

As Pavithra became pregnant again, the couple reportedly got in touch with Indrarani and Geetha through agents to conduct a sex determination test, and found that the fetus was a girl. As the couple did not want a third girl child, they allegedly sought help from Indrarani and Geetha to abort the foetus.

Subsequently, the accused came to Jagadeesan’s house in Girisamudiram village on Saturday. Based on a tip-off, a team of health officials led by N. Kalu Sivalingam, District Health Officer (DHO) and S. Aravind, health officer, inspected the house and found medical equipment.
Police said, along with police personnel from Vaniyambadi Taluk, the team conducted an inquiry with the suspects, who confessed that they were roped in by the couple to abort the foetus.
Police said a case was registered under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, 1971. Later, two suspects were lodged at a sub-jail in Tirupattur town. Further probe is under way.

articles.title: Coal India profit jumps 57% as higher offtake, prices weigh over costs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Cost of input materials increased 20% during the quarter.
Coal India’s net profit surged 57% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹6,547 crore in the second quarter, driven by higher offtake and improved price realisations that offset an increase in input costs.
The state-owned coal miner declared a second interim dividend of ₹10.25 per equity share.

Offtake during the quarter ended September increased 12% YoY to 186.34 million tonnes (MT), primarily driven by higher power demand. Average price realisation, covering fuel supply agreements, e-auctions, washed coal and other categories, rose 7% YoY to ₹2,346.21 per tonne.
The Kolkata-headquartered company’s overall production grew 4% YoY to 151.37 MT in the reported quarter, falling short of its target of 157.83 MT.
Revenue from the sale of products increased 21% YoY to ₹43,724 crore. Overall revenue also rose 21% to ₹44,179 crore.

The company’s cost of materials -- which primarily includes expenditure on explosives, oil and lubricants, heavy earth-moving machinery, spares and timber, among other items -- increased 20% YoY to ₹2,752 crore during the quarter.

articles.title: Deepavali sales expected to gain momentum in Coimbatore next week
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: With Deepavali falling in the first week of a month this year, people are likely to begin shopping after receiving their monthly salaries and festival bonuses; the last 5-6 days preceding the festival is likely to witness massive retail activity
Shopping for the Deepavali festival in Coimbatore city this year is expected to pick up next week across sectors.
President of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Coimbatore, C. Dorairaj, told The Hindu on Thursday (October 29) that several companies in Coimbatore will disburse bonuses next week.

With the festival coming in the first week of a month this year, people are likely to start purchases after getting the monthly salary and the festival bonus. So, the last 5-6 days preceding the festival is expected to see huge retail activity.
Be it textiles, FMCG, or household appliances, the retailers are expecting good sales this year.

All the products have seen a price hike, ranging between 10% and 30%, in the last few months, depending on the product. So, the retailers may see higher revenue though the volume of sales may remain the same as last year or slightly better in some sectors, he added.

In the case of textiles, while the large, multi brand retail outlets are already witnessing a pick up of sales, the smaller outlets are facing stiff competition from online sellers. Further, business at the small retail shops will go up in the last few days before the festival.

Though gold and silver prices saw a decline recently, jewellery retailers are yet to see business picking up. “We were hoping for better sales as the prices fell. But, consumers are waiting for further fall in prices,” said B. Sabarinath, president of the Coimbatore Jewellers Association.
The household appliances outlets are also expecting better sales only from next week.
In the case of sweets and savouries, most of the bulk buyers will purchase products for distribution just days before the festival, Mr. Dorairaj said.

articles.title: Rubio says U.S. not directly involved in Flavio Bolsonaro’s flight from Brazil
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Bolsonaro, who lost his bid to be president in the October 25 run-off vote, arrived with his family in the U.S. on October 28
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday (October 31, 2026) that Washington was not directly involved in Flavio Bolsonaro’s arrangements to leave Brazil after his election loss.

Mr. Bolsonaro, who lost his bid to be president in Sunday’s (October 25, 2026) run-off vote, arrived with his family in the U.S. on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) after a court ordered his passports be seized amid multiple investigations against him.

“He had previously held a visa, and the President made a decision to allow him to enter the country,” Mr. Rubio told a press conference in Atlanta, Georgia, where he hosted G20 Foreign Ministers for a two-day meeting.
But Mr. Rubio added that “the U.S. government was not involved directly” in arrangements Mr. Bolsonaro made to leave his country.

Following the vote, the 45-year-old bolted from Brazil via Argentina and Ecuador in a plane that some U.S. media, including The New York Times and The Wall Street Journa l, reported was chartered by Jason Miller, an adviser to U.S. President Donald Trump.
The plane that whisked the Mr. Bolsonaro family to the United States was paid for by an intermediary from a U.S. bank account, the head of the airline has told AFP .
The White House has not commented on the flight, but Mr. Trump has called the Brazilian election “disgraceful.”

A Brazilian diplomatic source, speaking on condition of anonymity, told AFP that Argentina’s diplomatic representative had been summoned for a “routine meeting” to “provide explanations” on the flight.
Argentina’s Foreign Minister later denied that Brazil had asked Buenos Aires to explain its role in the operation.
Since arriving in the U.S., Mr. Bolsonaro has claimed to be the true leader of Brazil and said that he left the country because he was a victim of “persecution.”
Flavio Bolsonaro’s father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for plotting a coup after his 2022 re-election loss.

articles.title: Andhra civic polls: TDP, YSRCP workers clash in Pulivendula; 22.08% turnout by 11 a.m. | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Fourteen vehicles were set on fire in Pulivendula, Kadapa district, Andhra Pradesh hours before polling began on Sunday

The YSRCP “seems to have come ‘well-prepared’ in Kadapa” while the rest of the State is voting peacefully, Minister Nara Lokesh said in a post on X on Sunday. The election authorities would deal with “criminal elements”, he said, urging voters to turn out in large numbers.

Turnout in Kadapa district’s urban bodies stood at 25.46% by 11 a.m., above the State average of 22.08%, according to the State Election Commission’s figures. Jammalamadugu recorded 60.92% and Pulivendula 35.17%. Kadapa city, the district’s only corporation, was at 18.54%.

YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy accused the State Election Commission of failing to ensure a level playing field in the municipal elections and of siding with the ruling NDA government. Speaking to reporters in Pulivendula on Sunday (November 1, 2026), he said the SEC should give every candidate a fair chance from nominations to counting. “Only then it will be termed as an election,” he said.

He alleged that journalists had been beaten up and their cameras destroyed in Pulivendula. Polling agents were not allowed into polling stations, he claimed. The Centre should step in even though the TDP is its ally, he said. “If today an NDA partner is permitted to do so and the central government chooses to ignore it, then democracy will not prevail.”

Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy flew into Pulivendula by helicopter on Sunday, in what was termed an “emergency landing”. He had reportedly been given permission to arrive on Saturday. The district administration, busy with the polls, had expressed difficulty in providing security.

Former Chief Minister and Pulivendula MLA Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy arrived in his constituency on Sunday morning, while voting was under way in the town’s municipal elections. He reportedly took out a roadshow, which TDP workers objected to. The TDP has accused him of violating the Model Code of Conduct. The YSRCP said he had come to cast his vote and that people walked alongside him in support.

Shaik Dastagiri, an accused-turned-approver in the Y.S. Vivekananda Reddy murder case, confronted Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy’s convoy on a busy road, causing tension. Mr. Dastagiri, known for his rivalry with the Y.S. family, reportedly shouted at him during the brief encounter.

Supporters of YSRCP Mayor candidate Varudu Kalyani got into an argument with TDP workers in Ward 29 of Visakhapatnam’s East Assembly constituency on Sunday. It happened while Ms. Kalyani was returning after casting her vote at a polling station in the area. The police stepped in quickly and asked both groups to leave. - Harish Gilai

About 21.40 lakh of Andhra Pradesh’s 96.89 lakh urban voters had cast their votes by 11 a.m. on Sunday, a turnout of 22.08%, according to the State Election Commission. Smaller towns are well ahead of cities. Jammalamadugu in Kadapa district leads the State at 60.92%, followed by Kuppam at 44.30% and Nagari at 40.46%. In Pulivendula, the scene of clashes this morning, 35.17% had voted.

The 13 municipal corporations are trailing: Chittoor leads them at 32.50%. Vijayawada was at 18.07% and Guntur at 17.82%. Visakhapatnam, the largest, was the lowest at 13.34%. 11 AM- Poll Percentage.pdf

YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy is on a visit to Pulivendula in Kadapa district on Sunday, where municipal polling is under way. The TDP has accused him of taking part in a roadshow in alleged violation of the Model Code of Conduct.​​ ​​

Polling picked up in Visakhapatnam through the morning. Turnout rose from 3.34% at 9 a.m. to 13.34% by 11 a.m. on Sunday, according to election officials. Of the city’s 18.37 lakh voters, 2,45,251 had voted by then.

articles.title: Anantapur chainsaw attack: A.P. Minister Nara Lokesh says Class 10 girl stable after bleeding controlled
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Minister said that the medical team at Manipal Hospital stabilised the girl’s condition with blood transfusions and supportive treatment

The Class 10 student from Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu, who was attacked with an electric chainsaw on Saturday (October 31, 2026), has been stabilised and receiving significant medical care at Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.

articles.title: Uttarakhand chopper crash: Mortal remains of all six victims recovered, sent to Rishikesh AIIMS
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Officials said that after completing the necessary formalities, the mortal remains were sent to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Rishikesh, by helicopter

The mortal remains of all six people who died in the helicopter crash near Joshimath in Uttarakhand were recovered and sent to AIIMS, Rishikesh, on Sunday (November 1, 2026) morning, the Chamoli district administration said.
On Friday (October 30), the chopper crashed on a hillside near Chai village in Joshimath while it was returning to Dehradun from the Badrinath shrine.

The mortal remains were brought to the Community Health Centre (CHC), Joshimath, by road. Officials said that after completing the necessary formalities, the mortal remains were sent to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Rishikesh, by helicopter.

The district administration said that teams of the Indian Army, ITBP, SDRF, NDRF, police, district administration and the Forest Department jointly conducted the search operation amidst challenging conditions in the inaccessible and high-altitude hilly area.
"The bodies of all six deceased were taken out by rescue teams on foot on difficult mountain paths," mentions a statement issued by the district administration on Sunday (November 1).
The operation started on Friday (October 30) after the chopper crashed, but due to the difficult terrain and remote location, it took over 24 hours for teams to complete the operation.

articles.title: ‘Chalo Delhi’ posters dominate as INDIA bloc prepares for mega rally at Ramlila Maidan | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: INDA bloc's 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar featured accounts from voters who alleged that their names had been deleted from electoral rolls
INDIA bloc leaders and supporters take part in the ‘Chalo Dilli’ march from the Minto Road–Connaught Place junction to Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on November 1.

The march precedes the Opposition’s mega rally against alleged vote theft and electoral irregularities. The parties are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over concerns surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Tribal communities from across the country performed a cultural dance in Connaught Place ahead of the INDIA bloc’s rally at Ramlila Ground.

Congress leader and Punjab Congress in-charge Sachin Pilot said the government wants to stop people through pressure and prevent them from voicing their opinions, but neither Rahul Gandhi nor “our people” would back down. He said “hundreds of thousands” would arrive from across the country today (November 1, 2026) and that traders would see “a lot of business”.

Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, speaking in Shimla, alleged that Mr. Gandhi was upset because the names of “infiltrators” had been removed through the SIR. He said the BJP stood with the Election Commission. He asked whether the elections in Himachal Pradesh, Kerala and Mr. Gandhi’s own Raebareli seat should be annulled by the same logic, and accused the Congress of “double standards” for claiming votes are “stolen” only where the BJP is in power. He also made an insulting personal remark against Mr. Gandhi.

Mr. Nadda called the Ramlila Maidan rally “a foolish, orchestrated drama”. He alleged that Mr. Gandhi’s politics works in four stages: spreading lies and rumours, inciting street anarchy, damaging the economy, and destabilising an elected government “at the behest of foreign powers”. He said the rally had four aims, among them to “rub salt into the wounds” of Sikhs and to rob Delhi traders of festive-season earnings.
Union Minister J.P. Nadda told Rahul Gandhi that India was “not some ‘banana republic’” where one could “incite arson, trigger riots, or push an agenda for ‘regime change’”.

He called November 1 the “darkest stain” in India’s democratic history, alleging that “goons nurtured by the Congress party” massacred Sikhs on this day in 1984, and said the Gandhi family had never offered a sincere apology. He accused Mr. Gandhi of insensitivity for holding the rally today (November 1, 2026).

Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said the message of the INDIA bloc’s mega protest was “very simple”: “Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao”. He added that it was “not about the Congress” but about the constitutional rights of the Indian people.

CPI(M) MP John Brittas on Sunday (November 1, 2026) described the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan as a landmark protest that would have a major impact on the country’s politics. He claimed that more than 10 lakh people would gather and said the ground was already packed before the event began.

Mr. Brittas said the rally would send a strong message to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, demanding the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He warned that the government should act on the demand or face further political consequences.

Congress leader Pawan Khera said “this is the calm before the storm”, adding that the “coming storm will sweep Gyanesh away” and that Amit Shah and Narendra Modi would also “not remain in their positions”.

articles.title: How were the States formed and how has the Indian map changed since 1947?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The last transformation of the Indian map happened in 2019 with the creation of the Union Territories of J&K and Ladakh

The story so far: On the “appointed day”, as Independence Day was referred to in the Indian Independence Act, 1947, British paramountcy lapsed in India, leading to the formation of two independent dominions- India and Pakistan. Pre-independence India consisted of state units, provinces and more than 550 scattered princely states. Nearly 114 of these, through the Instrument of Accession, had already joined India before August 15. The rest had the choice of joining either India or Pakistan, with most deciding to accede to the former.

From then to now, as India completes 79 years of independence and has 28 States and eight Union Territories, the internal boundaries of the country have undergone several changes with States being reorganised in multiple phases, with different factors behind the redrawing of the map.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu to set up 26 POCSO Act courts and four NDPS courts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: With the addition of these POCSO Act courts, there will be 52 special courts across 47 police districts

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has ordered the establishment of 26 courts under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, and four courts under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, to expedite the trial of cases registered under these laws.

A State government press release issued on Sunday (November 1, 2026) said during a review meeting on cases registered under the POCSO Act, the Chief Minister had stressed the need to ensure justice for victims by speeding up trials. He had also sought details on the need for additional courts. Accordingly, the government had decided to establish more courts.

Already, 22 courts dealing with POCSO Act cases and four special courts will start functioning soon. The government said the Chief Minister had ordered the establishment of 12 special courts and 14 additional courts at a cost of ₹46.59 crore, taking into account the volume of cases registered under the Act.

With the addition of these courts, there will be 52 special courts across 47 police districts. They are expected to expedite the delivery of justice and help prevent the recurrence of sexual offences against children, the government said.

The release said, 11 special courts were already functioning to deal with cases registered under the NDPS Act. Four more courts will be established, one each in Kancheepuram, Tiruvallur and Vellore, and an additional court in Chennai.

articles.title: GST mop-up grows 23% to over ₹2.31 lakh cr. in October
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore

Gross GST collections increased 23% to over ₹2.31 lakh crore in October, driven by strong mop-up from domestic activities and imports, according to government data released on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore.
The ₹2.31 lakh crore collection includes Central GST mop-up of ₹42,935 crore, State GST of ₹51,340 crore and Integrated GST of over ₹1.37 lakh crore, data showed.
Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds increased 6.5% year-on-year to ₹27,934 crore in October.
After adjusting for refunds, net GST collections rose 26% to over ₹2.03 lakh crore in October.

GST mop-up grows 23% to over ₹2.31 lakh cr. in October

Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore

Gross GST collections increased 23% to over ₹2.31 lakh crore in October, driven by strong mop-up from domestic activities and imports, according to government data released on Sunday (November 1, 2026).

Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore.

The ₹2.31 lakh crore collection includes Central GST mop-up of ₹42,935 crore, State GST of ₹51,340 crore and Integrated GST of over ₹1.37 lakh crore, data showed.

Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds increased 6.5% year-on-year to ₹27,934 crore in October.

After adjusting for refunds, net GST collections rose 26% to over ₹2.03 lakh crore in October.

During April-October, gross GST collection grew 13.2% to over ₹14.77 lakh crore. Net collections rose 13% to over ₹12.69 lakh crore.
