fullParagraphs: The development followed a series of defections that saw eight of the UDP MLAs merge with the BJP in September and three others with the NPP, the Chief Minister's party, earlier this month

United Democratic Party president Metbah Lyngdoh resigned as a Minister in the Meghalaya Cabinet on Saturday (October 31, 2026), days after 11 of the party's 12 MLAs joined the BJP and the NPP, leaving him as the UDP's sole legislator in the State Assembly.
Mr. Lyngdoh said that he had submitted his resignation letter to Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma after assessing the prevailing political situation and recent developments within the party.

The development followed a series of defections that saw eight of the UDP MLAs merge with the BJP in September and three others with the NPP, the Chief Minister's party, earlier this month. The Speaker recognised both mergers, reducing the UDP's strength from 12 to one. Both BJP and UDP are constituents of the NPP-led Meghalaya Democratic Alliance.
Mr. Lyngdoh said the UDP's Central Executive Committee would deliberate on the developments and decide on the future course of action in consultation with party leaders and office-bearers.
Rejecting speculation that he was forced to resign, the UDP president maintained that the decision was voluntary.
He was in charge of the departments of power, textiles, water resources and taxation.

The political upheaval in the UDP came amid reported discontent within the party over leadership and organisational issues. The developments also followed a cabinet reshuffle in September 2025, when Metbah Lyngdoh and Lahkmen Rymbui replaced senior UDP leaders Paul Lyngdoh and Kyrmen Shylla as the party's representatives in the state cabinet.

The eight legislators who joined the BJP were Lahkmen Rymbui, Kyrmen Shylla, Pius Marwein, Mayralborn Syiem, Matthew Beyondstar Kurbah, Ollan Singh Suin, Balajied Kupar Synrem and Synshar Kupar Roy Lyngdoh Thabah.
The three who merged with the NPP were Paul Lyngdoh, Renikton Lyngdoh Tongkhar and Nujorki Sungoh.
The moves took the NPP's strength in the 60-member Assembly to 36, while the BJP's tally rose to 10.
The UDP had emerged as the second-largest party in the 2023 Meghalaya Assembly elections with 12 seats.

articles.title: Postponement of college exam for CM’s visit in Pudukottai triggers row
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: With Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay scheduled to visit Pudukottai on November 2, to inaugurate the new bus stand and distribute welfare measure, semester examinations scheduled for the day at the Kalaignar Karunanidhi Government Arts College for Women, an autonomous institution in the town, has been postponed, triggering a row.

The examinations in the college started on October 30 and are to conclude on November 19. However, the examinations scheduled on November 2 have been postponed apparently “keeping in mind the difficulty the students of the college may face in reaching the institution from the bus stand,” said the college authorities.

The exam scheduled on November 2 would be held on a later day. The college office would work as usual on November 2, the college authorities said. Several students of the college hail from the rural areas of the district.

Information about the postponement of the examination on November 2 was conveyed to the faculty members in the college group on a mobile messaging platform a couple of days ago and communicated to the students.
The Tamizhaga Vazhvurimai Katchi leader, T. Velmurugan, in a social media post expressed shock over the postponement of the examination at the college in view of the Chief Minister’s visit.

He condemned the postponement and wondered whether the Chief Minister’s visit was more important than the future of students. “It was the government’s responsibility to make arrangements for security and transportation for the official function. But, action affecting the education and examination of students could not be accepted,” he said.
Meanwhile, arrangements are under way for the Chief Minister’s programme in Pudukottai.

Minister for Labour Welfare and Skill Development J. Mohamed Farvas on Saturday said that the Chief Minister would inaugurate the new bus stand in Pudukottai and distribute welfare assistance to the beneficiaries. The function is to be held at the District Armed Reserve ground during which welfare assistance would be provided to 2,000 beneficiaries. Welfare assistance to the tune of Rs. 100 crore is to be given to 14,000 beneficiaries of Pudukottai district on that day, the Minister told reporters in Pudukottai.

articles.title: ‘You can break a stick, not a bundle’: From an IT couple to a hospital patient, citizens turn up for INDIA bloc rally
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Citizens, youth groups, farmers and political party workers gather ahead of the Ramlila Maidan rally, saying a united movement is needed to fight alleged vote theft and electoral roll irregularities

Thousands of protesters from across the country, representing political parties, youth organisations, women’s groups and farmers’ bodies, gathered at Minto Road in Delhi on Sunday (November 1, 2026) ahead of the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, seeking to strengthen the campaign against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Chalo Dilli protests: Follow LIVE updates from the Opposition rally on November 1, 2026

Ahead of the arrival of Opposition leaders, including Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, protesters raised slogans of “vote chori” and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the rollback of the SIR exercise.

Among those assembling at Minto Road were members of the Indian Youth Congress, Samajwadi Party, Rashtriya Janata Dal, National Students’ Union of India, Krantikari Yuva Sangathan and the All India Students’ Federation, among other groups.

The gathering also drew citizens (independent of parties) who said the coming together of various parties and the public had given the protests greater strength after several demonstrations against the SIR in recent weeks.

“You can break one stick easily, but if you bundle 10 sticks together, they cannot be broken. Today’s protest symbolises that bundle of sticks,” said Tejender, an IT employee who had arrived with his wife from Gurugram.

When asked why he had joined the demonstration on a Sunday afternoon, he said, “We are doing this for a better future for our children. The education system is in a bad state, healthcare facilities are lacking, and there are concerns over the misappropriation of votes. Our country has so many problems that need to be addressed. It is high time we all came together,” he said.
Mr. Tejender said the SIR exercise has disproportionately affected people who lacked the resources or awareness to navigate the documentation process.

“I am educated and was able to produce all the required documents, but a large section of the population is either uneducated or unaware of the process and is being targeted by the SIR of electoral rolls. Who will fight for them?” he asked.
Participants also said that the past protests ensured that fear of demonstrations was gradually receding.

“The earlier protests were a struggle by the youth and they have helped remove the fear of the police from people’s minds. I was scared earlier, many political parties were scared too. But after a series of consistent protests, that fear is no longer there,” said Anil S. Raj, an advocate who had attended previous demonstrations against the SIR.

Participants said earlier demonstrations had largely taken place in silos, with different groups raising concerns over the SIR separately. The INDIA bloc rally, they said, offered an opportunity to bring these voices together and build a broader movement.

articles.title: Polling ends peacefully across Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu districts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Municipal elections in Guntur, Bapatla and Palnadu districts concluded largely peacefully on Sunday. Election authorities said some complaints were received in Palnadu and Bapatla districts, but the issues were promptly addressed. District Collectors inspected polling stations and reviewed arrangements to ensure smooth voting.

In Guntur district, the Guntur Municipal Corporation (GMC), with 76 wards, 596 polling booths and 6,18,714 voters, recorded 3,18,009 votes, a turnout of 51.40%, by 5 p.m. Tenali Municipality, comprising 52 wards and 185 polling stations, registered 88,764 votes from 1,57,089 voters, recording 56.51%.

District Collector and District Election Officer C.M. Saikanth Varma inspected polling arrangements in Guntur. He directed officials to assist voters through help desks and prioritise senior citizens, pregnant women, nursing mothers and those who were unwell. He also instructed staff to arrange tricycles for persons with disabilities when required.

In Bapatla district, Repalle Municipality recorded 25,776 votes from 37,008 voters across 44 polling stations, registering 69.65% turnout by 5 p.m. Chirala, with 88 polling stations and 69,557 voters, recorded 50,558 votes, or 72.69%. These included 24,247 male and 26,311 female voters. Bapatla District Collector Vinod Kumar V. said complaints received during polling were attended immediately and the elections concluded peacefully.

Palnadu district recorded its highest turnout in Sattenapalli at 76.17%, with 36,712 votes polled from 48,196 voters across 36 wards. Vinukonda, also with 36 wards, recorded 35,012 votes from 47,186 voters, a turnout of 74.20%. Macherla registered 31,145 votes from 46,520 voters, or 66.95%, across 36 wards. Chilakaluripeta, with 48 wards and 86,554 voters, recorded 56,606 votes, translating to 65.40%.

Palnadu District Collector Kritika Shukla inspected polling stations in Macherla and said polling was peaceful across the district, with good voter participation and essential facilities provided. She said webcasting was arranged at every polling station, while strong rooms were secured with CCTV cameras. Contesting candidates were also permitted to inspect strong rooms to address their concerns, ensuring transparency in the electoral process.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Steps taken to restore live power using alternating current supply

The solar-powered electric fence along the perimeter wall of the Puzhal prison complex, one of the largest prisons in the country, has remained defunct for three years, official sources said on Sunday.

With no contract for annual maintenance, the solar-powered fence failed about three years ago. When a Nepal national inmate scaled the perimeter wall and escaped from the prison recently and later captured, it was reported the power supply in the fence was not functional due to rains.

However, the sources said the electric fence had no power supply for a long time. Confirming this to ‘The Hindu’, a senior official in the prison department said steps had been taken to restore power using Alternating Current (AC) like in other central prisons.

The Puzhal prison complex built on a sprawling 212 acres of land houses the Central Prison-I (Convicts), Central Prison-II (Remand Prisoners) and Special Prison for Women. The complex built by the Tamil Nadu Police Housing Corporation was inaugurated by the then Chief Minister in 2006.
In a related development, the Tamil Nadu Prison Department has suspended out-gang duties preventing convicts from going out for managing fuel stations, prison bazaar stores etc.

Additional Director-General of Police, Prisons, K. Shankar said the decision was taken as a precautionary measure. About 100 convicts were deployed in fuel stations located close to 11 central prisons across Tamil Nadu and other small business establishments like ‘Freedom Bazaar’ that sell products manufactured by inmates in the prison industry.

“There are chances that they (the convicts on out-gang duties) might escape. The decision to suspend the deployment of convicts on duties outside the prison is a temporary measure. The fuel stations will continue to be operated by the Indian Oil Corporation,” the ADGP said.

Mr. Shankar took charge as the ADGP, Prisons, a couple of days ago after DGP Sandeep Rai Rathore was transferred following the sensational jailbreak in Theni where 17 inmates escaped from the district jail after overpowering the prison warders on duty. All the escapees were recaptured by the Tamil Nadu police who launched a massive combing operation and also flew drones over forest areas abutting Theni and neighbouring Keralam.

articles.title: Tirupati municipal elections see low voter turnout
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tirupati registered the lowest poll share at 45.26%, while the district averaged 53.65%
The elections to the urban local bodies in Tirupati district concluded in a peaceful manner, with the poll percentage reportedly reflecting an urban apathy.

At 45.26 per cent, Tirupati registered the lowest poll percentage in the entire district, till about 5 p.m. With half a dozen universities, institutes such as IIT and IISER, and prominent industries, the city is known for its elite, educated and responsible citizen population comprising academicians, retired bureaucrats and technocrats.

However, the urban indifference was quite conspicuous in the polls held for the Tirupati Municipal Corporation (TMC), as evident from the abysmal figure. Of the 2,90,492 total voters, only 1,31,476 showed up at the polling stations to cast their vote.
The situation was slightly better in the other towns, where the polling percentages were higher — Sullurpeta (63.72%), Venkatagiri (67.04%), Naidupeta (69.99%) and Puttur (75.57%) respectively.
Voters arrive at a polling station to cast their vote in Tirupati on Sunday. | Photo Credit: K.V. Poornachandra Kumar
Overall, the district registered a total voting percentage of 53.65%, with 2,40,052 of the 4,47,461 voters exercising their franchise in the 202 wards across the five urban local bodies.
District Collector S. Venkateswar, along with District Revenue Officer G. Narasimhulu, monitored the developments at the various polling stations through webcasting.

The Election Expenditure Observer Mahaboob Basha visited several polling stations in Venkatagiri, Sullurpeta and Naidupeta municipalities and instructed the officials to adhere to the guidelines pertaining to monitoring the expenditure.

articles.title: Oocyte extraction racket: Women paid ₹20,000 as operators made around ₹3 lakh per cycle
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police probe alleged exploitation of 43 women, including possible forged consent documents and illegal commissions, while examining recruitment networks, payment trails and the role of IVF and fertility centres in Hyderabad

Women recruited from economically weaker sections were being offered ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 for an egg donation cycle, while those operating the alleged racket made an average of about ₹3 lakh from each cycle.
Malkajgiri police widened their investigation into the exploitation of women, falsification of records and the role of IVF and fertility establishments.

The 43 women rescued during simultaneous raids in Hyderabad have undergone medical examinations, including blood-group and fitness tests. Police are now verifying their medical histories with IVF centres to establish their treatment records.

The investigation has raised concerns over how the women were recruited and whether they gave informed consent for the procedures. Police said women from economically weaker sections were targeted and that, in some cases, intermediaries allegedly even completed their signatures on documents. Investigators are examining possible falsification of records and whether the women fully understood the procedures they were being recruited for.
Police are tracing the payments and commissions involving organisers, recruiters and intermediaries who connected the women with fertility-related establishments.

The investigation is now expanding to medical establishments. Police are preparing to serve notices to the District Medical and Health Officer (DMHO) and conduct searches at ART and fertility centres. Some hospitals have also approached police and informed them that employees found to have been involved had been removed.

Investigators are examining how women from West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and other states were recruited, transported and accommodated in Hyderabad before being referred for egg retrieval procedures. Their medical records, consent documents and the procedures they underwent are also being scrutinised.
All eight accused arrested in connection with the Hyderabad cases have been remanded to judicial custody. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Rajyotsava celebrated in Raichur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Minister recalls the century-long struggle to bring Kannada-speaking regions under a unified State

​Minister for Minor Irrigation, Science and Technology and Raichur district in-charge Ajay Singh praised the immense contribution made by leaders and freedom fighters who spearheaded the Karnataka unification movement, highlighting the State’s rich cultural heritage and religious tolerance.

​Addressing a gathering after unfurling the national flag during the 71st Kannada Rajyotsava celebrations at the Mahatma Gandhi District Stadium in Raichur on Sunday, Dr. Singh recalled the century-long struggle to bring Kannada-speaking regions under a unified State as they lay scattered under the British administration.

​”Deputy Chennabasappa initiated the movement for unification as early as 1856. The century-long agitation culminated in the creation of the unified Mysore State on November 1, 1956, which was subsequently renamed Karnataka by the then Chief Minister D. Devaraj Urs on November 1, 1973,” Dr. Singh said.

​He remembered the invaluable contribution of prominent stalwarts, including Alur Venkataraya (Kannada Kulapurohita), Acharya B.M. Srikanthaiah, A.N. Krishnarao, Hardekar Manjappa, Kuvempu, S. Nijalingappa, H.S. Doreswamy, Bellary Siddamma and Patil Puttappa, among others.
​Highlighting the State’s literary and cultural achievements, the Minister noted that Karnataka remains a sanctuary of religious tolerance, moral conduct and peaceful coexistence.
He added that it is a matter of immense pride that Kannada literature has been honoured with eight Jnanpith awards.

​Explaining about the administrative and developmental measures, Dr. Singh stated that the State government has responded effectively to the severe drought situation, declaring 226 taluks State-wide, including all taluks in Raichur district, as drought affected.

​He noted that Raichur district faced a 49% rainfall deficit receiving only 222.5 mm of rainfall during the monsoon season (June to September) against the normal average of 439.6 mm. Deficits across individual taluks ranged between 35% and 62%.
​Under the Kalyana Karnataka Region Development Board (KKRDB), an action plan involving 890 development works worth ₹622.35 crore has been approved for Raichur district for 2025-26.
Out of these, 61 works have been completed, 394 are in progress, while an expenditure of ₹178.03 crore has been incurred so far.

​To address water scarcity and boost groundwater levels, the Minor Irrigation and Groundwater Development Department has executed 1,890 works, including check dams, lift irrigation projects, lake developments and borewell drilling, at an estimated cost of ₹874.09 crore over the last three financial years (2023-24 to 2025-26).

Of these, 1,274 works have been completed, while 616 works, including the rejuvenation of Mavinakere, Neerabhavikuntakere and Rampur lakes in Raichur city, are in progress. A total of ₹547.88 crore released by the State government has been fully utilized to date.

articles.title: Search on for eight missing trekkers in Uttarakhand’s Kedartal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Heavy snowfall and adverse conditions affect operations; SDRF resorts to aerial reconnaissance through a helicopter

The State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) initiated a search and rescue operation on Sunday for seven trekkers and one guide who went missing after being stranded on the Kedartal trek in Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand .

On October 27, a group of 13 people, consisting of seven trekkers and six support staff, set out from Gangotri for the Kedartal trek. They were scheduled to return on October 29, but adverse weather conditions, including glaciers and snowfall, blocked their route and prevented their timely return.

A team from Gangotri had already reached the Kedartal area for an initial assessment. However, heavy snowfall and adverse conditions hindered their progress. As a result, the SDRF has decided to conduct aerial reconnaissance and search the region using a helicopter.
Officials said that under the directives of SDRF Commandant Arpan Yaduvanshi, a specialised mountaineering team had been deployed to locate the missing individuals.

Two SDRF personnel, head constable Ravi Chauhan and constable Deepak Pant, reached Harsil by helicopter on Sunday, from where they conducted two thorough aerial reconnaissance flights over the Kedartal area. No clear signs of the missing trekkers or their tents were spotted during these flights, officials said.

Another team from the SDRF battalion headquarters has been sent out, equipped with essential rescue and mountaineering gear, to ensure that the search and rescue operation can continue as soon as conditions improve.
Officials said a future action plan was being developed in coordination with the relevant agencies as part of the ongoing search operation.

Rescue teams departed for Gangotri on Saturday to assist the group of trekkers and support staff stranded on the Kedartal trek due to inclement weather. According to officials, one of the stranded trekkers has also sustained a head injury.

articles.title: German ministers pledge tough action after rioters damage stores in Frankfurt
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Frankfurt became the hot spot for ⁠violent protests after tens of thousands of demonstrators took to the streets of dozens of German cities during the day to demand better education ‌and lower living costs

German ministers threatened tough penalties for looters and rioters ​who damaged stores and injured more than 100 police officers in ‌Frankfurt overnight, still praising public forces for preventing larger-scale violence.

Frankfurt ​late on Saturday (October 31, 2026) became the hot spot for ⁠violent protests after tens of thousands of demonstrators took to the streets of dozens of German cities during the day to demand better education ‌and lower living costs in protests led by the campaign group “Gen Z regelt” — “Gen Z takes charge”.

In the ‌financial hub Frankfurt, hooded rioters damaged 17 shops and ‌stores, ⁠of which five were looted, Roman Poseck, interior minister ⁠of the state of Hesse, told a press conference on Sunday (November 1).
He said police deployed 1,300 officers, with more than 100 injured in clashes. Police arrested ​54 people aged between ‌13 and 29.
“I am shocked by what I have seen, and there is no point in sugar-coating it. Let me make this very clear: Things cannot go on like this,” ‌Mr. Poseck said.
Mr. Poseck said most of those arrested were ​German nationals, adding that many of those involved in the disturbances were of a migrant background, citing information ⁠from the police.
“Police currently estimate that they are dealing with between 1,000 and 1,500 violent troublemakers, predominantly from a migrant background,” ‌he added.
Frankfurt police reported violent disturbances including windows being smashed and petrol bombs being thrown at the emergency services.

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt was quoted as telling the Bild tabloid on Sunday (November 1), “The rioters and looters will be identified and held accountable. This breach of the peace must be followed by tough penalties.”
He ‌accused “violent left-wing groups and troublemakers from the migrant community” of hijacking the ​otherwise peaceful protests, without elaborating.
Mr. Dobrindt said the police strategy of maintaining a large presence while deploying officers across ⁠multiple locations had worked.
“Excesses of violence like those in Paris were ⁠prevented thanks to our highly committed police forces,” Mr. Dobrindt, a member of the conservative Christian Social Union, said.

articles.title: Somali pirates seize Iranian fishing vessel, raising fears of attacks on cargo ships
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Azini was hijacked on October 29 between the coastal towns of Bandar Bayla and Hafun in northeastern Somalia, a maritime security officer with the Puntland Maritime Police Force said

Somali pirates have seized an Iranian fishing vessel carrying 23 people, the Maritime Security Centre Indian Ocean said, warning that the ship was approaching a commercial shipping lane and could become a floating base for further attacks.

The Azini was hijacked on Thursday (October 29, 2026) between the coastal towns of Bandar Bayla and Hafun in northeastern Somalia, a maritime security officer with the Puntland Maritime Police Force said on Sunday (November 1, 2026).

The officer told The Associated Press that 12 pirates seized the vessel, which was carrying 21 Iranian crew members and two Somali security guards. He spoke on condition of anonymity because he wasn't authorised to speak with the media.

The crew's safety was unknown, the centre said in an alert dated on Saturday (October 31, 2026). In an updated warning, it said that pirates could use the vessel as a “mother ship” to support attacks on commercial vessels.
The European Union's naval Operation Atalanta was investigating. The centre urged ships in the area to remain vigilant and report suspicious activity.

The seizure follows a resurgence of Somali piracy across the Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean. By August, pirates had hijacked six commercial vessels since April, with some attacks taking place far from Somalia's coastline. The captures included the oil products tanker Sibu 1, seized about 136 nautical miles (252 kilometres) east of al-Mukalla, Yemen.

In September, Puntland authorities said pirates killed five crew members of the tanker MT Honour 25 before security forces recovered the vessel. The tanker had been held since April. Authorities said that 16 suspected pirates were detained.

The renewed piracy adds another danger for shipping in a region already disrupted by the Iran war. Attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and threats by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels against Saudi-linked shipping through Bab el-Mandeb have complicated routes used to move oil to world markets.

Those disruptions have lengthened voyages and driven up tanker costs. The AP reported in September that some oil shipments diverted around Africa faced journeys up to a month longer, while daily spot charter rates for tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz had reached $1 million.

International naval patrols and improved maritime security sharply reduced Somali piracy over the past decade. The latest seizures have renewed concerns about the threat to vessels off the country's long coastline.

articles.title: S. Jaishankar meets Russian, Polish, South Korean counterparts; discusses Ukraine, West Asia
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The External Affairs Minister also met Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held separate meetings with his Russian, Polish and South Korean counterparts in the U.S., discussing the Ukraine conflict, the situation in West Asia, bilateral ties and multilateral issues.
The meetings took place on Saturday (October 31, 2026) on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta.
In a social media post, Mr. Jaishankar said he "discussed the Ukraine conflict, Gulf situation and multilateral issues" with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.
The External Affairs Minister also met Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, with discussions focusing on the Ukraine conflict, India-EU ties and the G20.
Poland is attending this year's G20 meetings as a full participant following an invitation from the U.S. It has also expressed interest in securing permanent membership of the grouping.
“My meeting with DPM & FM Radosław Sikorski @sikorskiradek of Poland focused on the Ukraine conflict, India-EU ties and the G20,” Mr. Jaishankar said.
Mr. Jaishankar also met South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and discussed bilateral cooperation and other multilateral issues.
“Appreciated the stocktaking with @FMChoHyun of the Republic of Korea of our bilateral cooperation, as also the discussion on G20 and multilateral issues,” he said.

After two days of brainstorming on global affairs, Jaishankar and fellow G20 foreign ministers attended the college football game between the Florida Gators and the Georgia Bulldogs at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta.

“Happy to introduce my fellow foreign ministers to the quintessential American sport of football and welcome them to #GatorNation,” Mr. Rubio posted on social media after escorting the visitors to the stands of the stadium.
Mr. Rubio's son Anthony plays as a running back for the Florida Gators and is in his fourth season with the team.

articles.title: India's flight disruptions to Saudi Arabia continue amid security concerns
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The flight disruptions have continued amid attacks on civilian and critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including airports

Flight disruptions between India and Saudi Arabia continue, with Akasa Air on Sunday (November 1, 2026) extending the suspension of its services to Jeddah until November 18 amid the prevailing security situation in the Gulf kingdom. The airline said flights to and from Riyadh would remain suspended until November 30.
The announcement came two days after Air India and Air India Express said their flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh, and Dammam would remain suspended until November 14.
The flight disruptions have continued amid attacks on civilian and critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including airports.

In a statement on October 22, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh said one Indian national was killed and two others injured in the October 21 attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam. Another Indian national was injured in an attack on Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field in the Eastern Province.
The Embassy said it was in contact with Saudi authorities and would provide all possible assistance to the affected Indians.
Earlier, India had condemned attacks targeting Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, saying the targeting of civilian infrastructure was unacceptable.

Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels have claimed responsibility for several attacks on Saudi targets, including airports and energy infrastructure. The group has carried out missile and drone attacks on the kingdom amid the wider regional conflict.

In its advisories, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh has asked Indian nationals to remain calm and vigilant, stay indoors in the event of an aerial attack and follow instructions issued by local authorities.
It also urged them not to circulate or repost videos or news related to the ongoing developments.

The Consulate General of India in Jeddah has been coordinating with airlines, local authorities, and community organisations to assist affected Indian nationals, particularly Umrah pilgrims, and facilitate alternative travel arrangements.

With the latest announcements, Air India, Air India Express, and IndiGo have suspended services to several Saudi destinations until November 14, while Akasa Air's suspensions extend until November 18 for Jeddah and November 30 for Riyadh.
However, Saudi carriers continue to operate some flights to India.

It also urged them not to circulate or repost videos or news related to the ongoing developments.

The Consulate General of India in Jeddah has been coordinating with airlines, local authorities, and community organisations to assist affected Indian nationals, particularly Umrah pilgrims, and facilitate alternative travel arrangements.

With the latest announcements, Air India, Air India Express, and IndiGo have suspended services to several Saudi destinations until November 14, while Akasa Air's suspensions extend until November 18 for Jeddah and November 30 for Riyadh.

articles.title: Six Indian tourists stranded in Nepal, rescue efforts under way
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Indian tourists had ventured into the area despite warnings from security personnel and the Nepali guide accompanying them, says an official

Security personnel are making efforts to rescue six Indian tourists, including two women, stranded due to heavy snowfall in the Shey-Phoksundo National Park area of Nepal since Saturday afternoon (October 31, 2026), officials said on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
The tourists had gone to the Dho area in Shey Phoksundo Rural Municipality’s Ward No. 8, which was covered in heavy snow, according to Dolpa Chief District Officer Junu Dhakal.
Shey Phoksundo Lake, located in the rural municipality, is Nepal’s deepest lake. It is situated at an altitude of 3,600 metres and has an estimated depth of 145 metres.
“We have located the area where they are stranded, and an Army helicopter is arriving to rescue them. We hope to rescue them soon,” Ms. Dhakal told PTI .
The Indian tourists had ventured into the area despite warnings from security personnel and the Nepali guide accompanying them, she said.
Ms. Dhakal said the tourists left the guide and proceeded towards the lake area despite heavy snowfall. Communication with them was disrupted on Saturday night (October 31, 2026).

The guide contacted the District Administration Office in Dolpa on Saturday evening (October 31, 2026), saying the tourists might have been stranded due to heavy snowfall, she said. However, communication was completely disrupted on Sunday morning (November 1, 2026).
“We cannot say they are missing, as we have located the area,” Ms. Dhakal clarified.

The tourists have been identified as Moumita Halder, Piyali Koley, Jajla Trivedi Kumar, Aditya Singha, Diplina Bishwas and Rajesh De, according to a press release issued by the District Administration Office, Dolpa.
Security personnel are being mobilised, and a rescue helicopter is expected to arrive soon, the press release said.

articles.title: Explained | What is the Gaia space mission and what has it revealed about the Milky Way?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The new data released by the European Space Agency’s Gaia mission has revealed the surprise phenomena of ‘starquakes’—massive tsunami-like movements on the surface of stars

The story so far: The third dataset released by the European Space Agency’s star-mapping Gaia probe, covering almost 1.8 billion stars in the Milky Way galaxy, has revealed an unexpected phenomena called ‘starquakes’, which are similar to earthquake-like movements but on the surface of stars.

The data has also revealed the largest chemical map of the entire Milky Way, showing the DNA of millions of stars, which includes their age, mass, chemical composition, colour, temperature, and metal content. Besides, the new data has also made discoveries about binary star systems, quasars, asteroids, and exoplanets.

articles.title: Is there an alternative to corticosteroids to control vomiting during chemotherapy? A new study attempts to find out
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: An Indian multicentre phase III trial found that an olanzapine-based regimen, which is non-steroidal, was not inferior to the standard dexamethasone-based prophylaxis, which is a steroid, for vomiting control. More research, however, is needed to establish the findings widely

Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting are among the most distressing side effects of cancer treatment in children. Preventing them is essential not only to improve quality of life, but also to help patients complete treatment. Yet the medicines used to prevent vomiting can themselves cause adverse effects, making the search for safe alternatives an important challenge in paediatric oncology.

An Indian multicentre clinical trial suggests that olanzapine may offer an alternative to dexamethasone, a corticosteroid routinely used to prevent chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in children receiving highly emetogenic chemotherapy — treatment with a high risk of inducing vomiting. The current regimen using dexamethasone is a guideline that is used regularly, but dexamethasone is a corticosteroid. The study was aimed at finding a comparable, non-corticosteroid option.

Science, Space & Environment Report: Is there an alternative to corticosteroids to control vomiting during chemotherapy? A new study attempts to find out. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Storm ‘Murasu’ to bring very heavy rain over north Tamil Nadu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Isolated places over Chennai, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Ranipet and Nilgiris districts are likely to get heavy rainfall on Monday, November 2; Chennai District Collector S. Malathi Helen announced holiday for schools on account of heavy rains

The cyclonic storm “Murasu” over Southwest and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal moved west-northwestwards with speed of 25 kmph during past six hours and lay centred at 5.30 p.m. on Sunday over the same region, at about 420 km east-southeast of Chennai, 490 km east-southeast of Nellore, 500 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 510 east-southeast of Kavali, 530 km southeast of Ongole and 560 km south-southeast of Vishakhapatnam.

It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm around Monday (November 2) morning. Thereafter, it is very likely to move northwestwards and cross south Andhra Pradesh coast as a severe cyclonic storm with wind speeds of 100 to 120 kmph between Nellore and Narsapur between Monday midnight and the early hours of Tuesday (11.30 p.m. and 4 a.m.).

As a result of the storm, during the 24-hour period ending 8.30 a.m. on Monday (November 2), the Regional Meteorological Centre here has forecast heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning likely over Tiruvallur district. At the same time, isolated places over Chennai, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Ranipet and Nilgiris districts are likely to get heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning.

Isolated places in districts including Vellore, Tiruvannamalai, Villupuram, Kallakurichi, Cuddalore, Erode, Tirupur, Salem, Namakkal, Karur, Tiruchi, Madurai, Tirunelveli, Kanniyakumari districts and rest of the Western Ghat districts and Puducherry are likely to get moderate rainfall. Light rain is likely to occur at isolated places over the rest of the State and Karaikal.

For the 24-hour period from 8.30 a.m. on Monday, heavy to very heavy rain is likely at isolated places over Chennai and Tiruvallur districts. The rains could be accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning with gusty wind speed reaching 40-50 kmph at one or two places.
Chennai District Collector S. Malathi Helen announced that Monday will be a holiday for schools alone on account of heavy rains.

Heavy rain is likely at isolated places with thunderstorm and lightning over Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Ranipet, Vellore and Nilgiris districts. Light to Moderate rain has been forecast at a few places with thunderstorms and lightning over rest of north Tamil Nadu and Western Ghat districts and Puducherry and Karaikal area.

For Tuesday (November 3), heavy rain at isolated places with thunderstorms and lightning is likely to occur over Nilgiris district. Moderate rain is likely to occur over isolated places in north Tamil Nadu and Western Ghat districts, Puducherry and Karaikal area. Light to moderate rain is likely to occur at a few places over the rest of the State.

articles.title: RJD and JSP call for disqualification of independent MLCs who ‘joined’ BJP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Bihar Bharatiya Janata Party issued a press statement saying both had joined the party; when a controversy erupted both MLCs said they have not joined the party but are supporting the BJP

Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) MP Manoj Jha called for the disqualification of two newly elected Independent MLCs (Rahul Raj and Banshidhar Brajwasi) on Sunday (November 1, 2026) for reportedly “joining the BJP”. He sought the urgent intervention of the Bihar Legislative Council chairman in the matter.

A day earlier, the Bihar Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) had issued a press statement saying both had joined the party, along with pictures that showed membership receipts. However, after a controversy erupted, both MLCs denied joining the party, claiming they had merely offered to back the BJP.

Mr. Jha said that under India’s Anti-Defection Law (Tenth Schedule of the Constitution), an independent Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) or Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) cannot join any political party after being elected.

Addressing the press at the state RJD headquarters Mr. Jha, Rajya Sabha MP and national chief spokesperson of the party, demanded that the acting Chairman of the Legislative Council, Ram Bachan Rai, disqualify the newly elected MLCs.
Presenting videos and photographs of both MLCs allegedly joining the BJP, Mr. Jha said that they have violated the anti-defection law and their memberships should be terminated.
“We will approach the Acting Chairman and demand the disqualification of these two Legislative Council members,”Mr. Jha said.
He said if no decision is taken regarding their disqualification, the controversy will snowball out of control.

Citing Paragraph 2(2) of the Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, Mr. Jha explained that if an individual is elected as an independent candidate without being fielded by any political party and subsequently joins a political party, they shall be deemed disqualified from membership of the House.
Mr. Jha described the situation not merely as “theft of votes”, but as a “robbery of the public mandate”.

Targeting Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, the RJD leader said that this serves as a test for all of them. He added if such activities are shielded or encouraged, the entire matter would be exposed before the public.

articles.title: Nadda terms INDIA bloc rally against CEC a ‘foolish and designed drama’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Health Minister says Rahul Gandhi was ‘rubbing salt into the wounds of the Sikhs’ on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots

Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda on Sunday (November 1, 2026) termed the Opposition INDIA bloc rally calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar a “foolish drama”, and accused the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi of “rubbing salt into the wounds of Sikhs” by holding the protest in Delhi on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.
The protest was part of a conspiracy to surrender democracy to anarchy and disorder, and would prove to be the final “nail in the coffin” of the Congress’s “political downfall”, Mr. Nadda claimed.

“Removing the democratically elected government by conspiring to spread riots and anarchy in Delhi, adversely impacting the earnings of shopkeepers and traders in Delhi during the festive season and defaming the country are other objectives of the rally,” Mr. Nadda told media persons.

“The day of November 1 is the ugliest and darkest blot on India’s democratic history. On this very day, goons patronised by the Congress massacred our innocent Sikh brothers. Thousands and lakhs of Sikh families became homeless overnight,” he said, in an apparent reference to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots following the assassination of then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
“This is a foolish and designed drama of people who have been defeated and repeatedly rejected by the public. The public understands this very well,” he said.

The Opposition alliance is holding the ‘Chalo Dilli’ protest in the national capital as part of its campaign against alleged electoral irregularities, and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The Congress and Mr. Gandhi “cannot hide the dark history of November 1. You cannot escape answering for the tears of Delhi’s traders”, the former Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president said.
Thousands of people had been killed in the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, but the Gandhi family had not apologised to the Sikh community to this day for “their great sin”, Mr. Nadda said.

“And look at Congress’s insensitivity and Rahul Gandhi’s petty mindset. On this dark day today, when the country should have remembered those martyrs and victims, Rahul Gandhi is standing at Ramlila Maidan polishing his politics. Rahul Gandhi has rubbed salt into the wounds of the Sikhs,” Mr. Nadda alleged.

The Congress leader’s “model of politics” involved “lying and spreading rumours” in its first stage, creating anarchy and unrest as the second, harming the economy in the third, and destabilising the elected government of the country at the behest of foreign powers as the fourth stage, Mr. Nadda claimed.

“It is the festive season. It is Dhanteras, Diwali, Chhath Puja. Throughout the year, our small traders, street vendors, shopkeepers wait for it for some earnings during these festivals. But Rahul Gandhi does not care about the stoves burning in traders’ homes. He only wants to ignite the fire of his politics,” he added.

“Due to previous protests, Delhi’s traders have already suffered a loss of nearly ₹3,000 crore. And due to today’s political spectacle, according to an estimate, our shopkeepers are likely to suffer a hit of more than ₹10,000 crore. Rahul Gandhi’s stubbornness has completely shut down their business today,” Mr. Nadda said.

articles.title: Punjab polls: Two MLAs, including former Minister, quit AAP ahead of Assembly polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The MLAs say they quit as the party failed to fulfil its promises; AAP smells foul, alleges BJP is attempting to bring leaders into its fold

Ahead of the Assembly election in Punjab, due in 2027, two legislators, one of whom was a former Minister of the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), on Sunday (November 1, 2026) resigned from the party’s primary membership.

Chetan Singh Jouramajra from the Samana Assembly constituency and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra from Sanour in Patiala district, said, they were quitting as the party has failed to fulfil its promises made during the 2022 Assembly polls.

At a press conference, both MLAs said various guarantees extended by the party regarding eradicating drugs, minimum support price on crops, better education and health in Punjab have not been fulfilled.
“In Punjab, people are continuously losing their lives to drug menace,” said Mr. Jouramajra, who was a Cabinet Minister and held portfolios including Health, among others.
Mr. Pathanmajra, meanwhile, is facing rape charges and a police case is registered against him in Punjab. He was granted regular bail by the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

Meanwhile, the AAP hit out at the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) over its attempts to induct leaders who have left or been expelled by other parties. AAP’s Punjab Chief Spokesperson and MLA Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal said that while the AAP had consistently put Punjab’s interests first and taken action against its own ministers and MLAs over corruption, the BJP was attempting to bring in leaders facing serious allegations.

“The BJP in Punjab is no longer a political party but has become a scrap shop and has no support base in Punjab. They are collecting rejected leaders and discarded material from other parties, whether they are Congress leaders, or those surviving on the mercy of the Shiromani Akali Dal, or tainted faces expelled from the AAP,” he alleged.

articles.title: Four workers die of suffocation in Ujjain hotel waste chamber; CM announces aid
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two workers collapsed after entering the food-waste tank at Shri Ganga Hotel on the Ujjain-Dewas road; two more entered to rescue them, and all four died
Four workers died after entering a waste chamber for cleaning at a private hotel in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, with officials suspecting suffocation caused by a poisonous gas leak.

According to officials, the incident took place around 10.30 p.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026) when two workers entered an overground chamber containing residual and leftover food at Shri Ganga Hotel on the Ujjain-Dewas road and collapsed. Two other workers then entered the chamber in an attempt to rescue them, resulting in the death of all four.

Ujjain Superintendent of Police Pradeep Sharma told The Hindu that all four workers had entered the tank without the required protective gear, adding that three had been hired externally for the cleaning work while one was a hotel staff. He said the bodies have been sent for post-mortem examinations and that an FIR will be registered based on the findings.

The incident is suspected to have been caused by slippery sludge in the chamber and a gas leak, though investigations are ongoing and the hotel management and staff are being questioned. Mr. Sharma added that the bodies were recovered after police personnel and hotel staff broke open the chamber, during which some people, including police officers, sustained minor injuries.
“There was an iron grill on the chamber so some people suffered injuries during the rescue efforts. Police also tried to revive them through CPR but we could not succeed,” he said.
The deceased have been identified as Wahid Khan, 29, Nitin Binarwan, 28, Kamlesh Tamboli, 30, all local residents, and the hotel supervisor Manoj Meena, 25, a resident of Rajasthan’s Jhalawar.

Ujjain Collector Roshan Kumar Singh told The Hindu that the Ujjain Police and the Ujjain Municipal Corporation are probing the case. Meanwhile, an Ujjain Municipal Corporation health department official said that the hotel had not gotten a mandatory receipt from the civic body for the cleaning.

Chief Minister Mohan Yadav condoled the deaths and announced financial assistance of ₹4 lakh to each to family of the deceased. “News of the tragic death of four people in an accident while cleaning a chamber at a private hotel in Ujjain is deeply painful. My condolences to the bereaved families. I have directed the state government to provide financial assistance of Rs4 lakh each to the families of the deceased,” he said on X.

articles.title: Coal India’s production increases 19% as mining recovers after monsoon slump
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: In a statement, the Coal India said, “The achievement assumes greater significance in view of the need to augment coal stocks at thermal power plants amid rising power demand.”

Coal India’s production increased about 19% to 67.2 million tonnes (MT)on a year-on-year basis in October, indicative of mining activity of the country’s largest producer picking up after being dampened because of monsoons.

The Kolkata-headquartered miner said that its supplies to the power sector also increased 19% to touch 57.1 MT. Overall supplies during the month surged 19% on a year-over-year basis to scale 70.3 MT. Both supplies to the power sector and overall supplies scaled record-highs in a single month, the company said.
About evacuation, it said that it loaded on an average 310 rakes per day — to the power sector — in October.

In a statement, the Coal India said, “The achievement assumes greater significance in view of the need to augment coal stocks at thermal power plants amid rising power demand, while disruptions caused by unseasonal rainfall, the Puja festivities and impact of a cyclone posed challenges to the operational performance.”

articles.title: GST mop-up surges 23% to second-highest level of ₹2.31 lakh crore in October on festive demand boost
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore

GST collections jumped 23% year-on-year to the second-highest level of over ₹2.31 lakh crore in October as festive buying boosted domestic demand, according to government data released on Sunday (November 1, , 2026).
October is the second consecutive month when monthly gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) crossed ₹2 lakh crore, and second only to the record about ₹2.43 lakh crore mop-up in April.
Also, the 22.9% year-on-year growth clocked during the month is the fastest recorded pace of gross mop-up in the current fiscal year.
Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore.
The ₹2.31 lakh crore collection includes Central GST mop-up of 42,935 crore, State GST of ₹51,340 crore and Integrated GST of over ₹1.37 lakh crore, data showed.
Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds increased 6.5% year-on-year to ₹27,934 crore in October.
After adjusting for refunds, net GST collections rose 26% to over ₹2.03 lakh crore in October.
In April-October, gross GST collection grew 13.2% to over ₹14.77 lakh crore. Net collections rose 13% to over ₹12.69 lakh crore.

Grant Thornton Bharat, Partner and Tax Controversy Management Leader, Manoj Mishra, said October collections capture the festive-season demand cycle, which typically brings higher consumer spending, retail activity and movement of goods across sectors.
The performance across key states, including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, also points to continued strength in GST collections across major economic centres.

“The focus now should be on sustaining domestic revenue growth and ensuring that the benefits of GST 2.0 translate into stronger compliance, smoother input tax credit flows and faster refunds for businesses,” Mr. Mishra said.

EY India Tax Partner, Saurabh Agarwal, said the GST collections for October 2026 reflect the continued resilience of the Indian economy, despite persistent global headwinds. The steady month-on-month rise in revenue indicates strong underlying consumption and improving compliance.

articles.title: Historic win, humongous challenges
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Lula tweaked his campaign’s message, speaking more about reducing working hours, relief for indebted families and higher welfare payments under the Bolsa Familia scheme

At the end of the first round of Brazil’s presidential elections, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva looked like a leader on his way out after a record third term. He trailed Flavio Bolsonaro by 45.2% to 47%, hurt by an abstention rate of 21%, the highest since 1998, as many of his supporters stayed home.

In the three weeks that followed, Mr. Lula managed a remarkable turnaround, helped by several factors. First, the day after the first round, thousands of students from the Fluminense Federal University marched through the streets of Niteroi to stand against Bolsonarism. Days later, thousands more young people occupied Candelaria Square in Rio de Janeiro. Similar student, youth and workers’ marches soon spread across urban Brazil. The protesters gathered without party banners, united less by support for Mr. Lula than by opposition to Bolsonarism, a far-right movement opposed to institutions, supportive of high-handed actions against crime and eager to curtail civil liberties. The newspaper O Globo described the marches as the Left’s return to the streets after more than a decade of absence.
Global & Diplomatic Brief: Historic win, humongous challenges. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

articles.title: Bhutan builds 108 stupas in 9 hours, dedicates No. 76 to PM Modi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuk says gesture recognises India’s steadfast support for realisation of Gelephu Mindfulness City

Bhutan King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuk on Sunday (November 1, 2026) dedicated one of the 108 Buddhist stupas erected in a nine-hour construction feat to Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a mark of appreciation for India’s support for the country’s ambitious Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC) project.
About 40,000 trained volunteers built the 108 Jangchub Chortens in what could be a potentially record-breaking royal initiative to lay the spiritual foundation of the planned city.
About 240 km south-southeast of Bhutan’s capital, Thimphu, Gelephu borders Assam’s Chirang district. King Wangchuk envisions the city as a spirituality-driven global economic hub.

The King, other members of the royal family, top officials and foreign dignitaries faced Chorten Number 79 from the ceremonial ground as thousands of people around chanted a six-syllable Tibetan Buddhist mantra a billion times while the volunteers completed the mission between 3 a.m. and 12 noon.

About two hours later, the focus shifted to Chorten Number 76, which the King dedicated to Mr. Modi “as an enduring symbol” of his “profound appreciation” for the latter’s “unwavering commitment and India’s steadfast support for the realisation” of GMC. Bhutanese officials said the number was chosen because Mr. Modi turned 76 more than a month ago.

Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju, who represented India for ‘Project 108’, thanked the King for dedicating Chorten 76 to Mr. Modi. “This remarkable milestone is an enduring symbol of the deep spiritual and civilisational bonds between our two nations,” he said, congratulating Bhutan on the achievement.

Each 15 metres tall and 108 metres apart, the Jangchub Chortens, or Buddhist stupas, stand in a single meandering file along the Mau Chhu River, Gelephu’s lifeline. Built with steel and other improvised building materials, they mark a departure from the traditional use of stone and earth.

Addressing the people after the completion of Project 108, King Wangchuk said he had been worried that the construction of 108 stupas in a single day might not succeed. “People from every walk of life and every generation came together to make this possible,” he said, underscoring the Bhutanese collective spirit and ability to achieve “anything impossible”.

He said the same spirit would help Bhutan overcome natural calamities, economic crises, and other challenges. The King also expressed gratitude to Bhutan’s patrons, sponsors, supporters, and well-wishers. “Prime Minister Modi and the government of India have been enormously supportive of Bhutan and of the vision of Gelephu Mindfulness City,” he said.

He said the same spirit would help Bhutan overcome natural calamities, economic crises, and other challenges. The King also expressed gratitude to Bhutan’s patrons, sponsors, supporters, and well-wishers. “Prime Minister Modi and the government of India have been enormously supportive of Bhutan and of the vision of Gelephu Mindfulness City,” he said.

articles.title: Bangladesh forms wage board as garment workers keep up protests
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The garment sector is the backbone of Bangladesh's export-driven economy, employing millions of workers and generating the bulk of the country's foreign earnings

Bangladesh formed a new board on Sunday (November 1, 2026) to review the minimum wage for garment workers, as authorities sought to quell protests that have disrupted key industrial hubs around Dhaka.
Despite the move, thousands of workers continued demonstrations in industrial areas around Dhaka on Sunday (November 1, 2026), leading to clashes with police who fired tear gas and sound grenades.
The garment sector is the backbone of Bangladesh's export-driven economy, employing millions of workers and generating the bulk of the country's foreign earnings.
The new wage board includes representatives of the government, workers, and factory owners.
"For the last three days, we have been discussing this issue with labour leaders and factory owners," Labour Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury said at a news conference in Dhaka.
"A coterie seeking to destabilise the government and cause public suffering has been exploiting our workers," he added, as he announced the new Board and urged workers to return to factories.
Labour leaders said their grievances extended beyond the creation of the Board, citing inflation and rising household expenses.
Workers currently earn about 13,000 taka ($106) a month, according to Kalpona Akhter of the Bangladesh Centre for Workers Solidarity.
"This time we are demanding a bit more than 30,000 taka, considering inflation and the rising cost of living," Mr. Akhter told AFP .
Thousands of factories across the country produce clothing including T-shirts, jeans, and sweaters for major retailers in Europe and the United States.

The industry is also seeking to expand beyond its traditional markets, having recently secured greater access to Japan while exploring new export destinations as it competes with regional rivals such as Vietnam.

articles.title: North Korea tests cluster-bomb warheads in latest weapons drill
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: It also came against the backdrop of growing tensions over a landmine explosion along the heavily fortified border between the two Koreas that saw three South Korean soldiers wounded
North Korea test-fired cluster-bomb warheads, its state media reported on Sunday (November 1, 2026), the latest in a slew of weapons drills aimed at training its military units on using them.

The test, conducted on Saturday (October 31, 2026), came after the nuclear-armed North recently trialled a range of weaponry including attack drones, a new precision-guided torpedo system, and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile.
It also came against the backdrop of growing tensions over a landmine explosion along the heavily fortified border between the two Koreas that saw three South Korean soldiers wounded.
The North has denied responsibility and vowed to further fortify its border areas and resume its loudspeaker campaign.

Saturday's (October 31, 2026) test was conducted to "assess adaptation to combat and power of a cluster-bomb warhead to be tipped on tactical ballistic missiles", the official Korean Central News Agency reported on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
Officials said it confirmed the weapon "is capable of turning into ashes a target area of 12 to 13 hectares with its highest-density power".

"Within this year we will enable units to select and use all those types according to operational aims and specific features of targets," said the general director of the North's Missile Administration.
Photos released by KCNA showed a projectile firing from a mobile launcher, with an orange exhaust plume. Another image showed multiple cluster-bomb impacts on an island target.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un was not present on Saturday (October 31, 2026), although he had overseen a test-launch of cluster-bomb warheads mounted on a ballistic missile in April, accompanied by his daughter Ju Ae.

articles.title: Iran warns new war could last longer after Trump threatens strikes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Diplomatic efforts to end the West Asia war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the U.S. and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections

Iran warned on Sunday (November 1, 2026) that any renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous round of fighting, after President Donald Trump said he still had to "take care" of more targets.
Diplomatic efforts to end the West Asia war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the U.S. and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections.

"A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion," said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television.

In the most intense phase of the war, which began on February 28 with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran retaliated with missile and drone attacks across the region. Iran-aligned armed groups joined the fighting in Lebanon and Yemen.
Mr. Akraminia's remarks followed Mr. Trump's suggestion that the U.S. could swiftly strike its remaining targets in Iran.
"We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes," Mr. Trump told reporters at his Florida residence.
"You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex.
Top military and political officials in Iran have warned against any new attack.
Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebbi on Sunday (November 1, 2026) echoed a warning issued a day earlier in a written message by Iran's new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei.
"In a conflict with America, there are no geographical limitations; a vast theatre has been defined for inflicting damage upon the enemy," Mr. Mohebbi said, according to state television.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said "we hope the other side will exercise rationality and choose diplomacy", adding that Iran "remains prepared for both defence and diplomacy", according to the official IRNA news agency.
The warnings came as Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei disclosed on Saturday (October 31, 2026) that he had received a letter from U.S. Vice President J. D. Vance seeking to revive talks.

articles.title: GVMC polls: smooth polling experience for senior citizens, first-time voters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Arrangements made by the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) enabled senior citizens, persons with disabilities and first-time voters to exercise their franchise in the urban local body elections, which passed off largely smoothly across the city on Sunday.

Most senior citizens said that the process was trouble free and that the staff guided them well. One of them, who did not wish to be named, said finding the right station was initially a problem after wards rose from 98 to 120, but the staff quickly helped.

Polling stations had drinking water, help desks, medicine counters, toilets, shamianas and ventilation, with ramps, handrails and chairs for senior citizens. Police personnel managed the crowds, and food was arranged for the staff.
At Yendada in Ward 11, around 300 voters turned up in the first hour after polling began at 7 a.m., said Booth Level Officers (BLOs) S. Srinivas and N. Nageswarao.

They added that residents of long-settled localities turned out in larger numbers than those living in apartment complexes. A similar pattern was seen later at other stations in the city. At Ward 3 in Bheemunipatnam, N. Narendra, BLO, said voting went on without hiccups, while Auxiliary Nurse Midwife N.V. Padma and ASHA worker G. Konda said they had all essential medicines, including oral rehydration salts (ORS) sachets, paracetamol and a blood pressure monitor.
First time voter show her inked finger after casting her vote at the at a polling booth in KDPM High School in the East Assembly Constituency in Visakhapatnam on Sunday | Photo Credit: V RAJU

Elisha Paul K, 21, a first-time voter pursuing an MBA at Andhra University, voted in Ward 31, Maharanipeta. He had expected a rush and lengthy queues, he said, but the process took less than 15 minutes, and the staff explained how a ballot is cast.

Patnala Papayyamma, 86, who makes it a point to vote in every election despite the hardship of travelling, her family said, voted in Ward 4 at the office of the Superintendent of Central Tax, Bheemunipatnam. Her family helped her onto a scooter allowed near the station.
First time voter shows her inked finger at a polling booth in Peda Jalaripeta, in the East Assembly Constituency on Sunday. | Photo Credit: V RAJU

At Chepala Thimmapuram in Ward 5, one of the exceptions, voting took time, with long queues continuing past noon. Jaya Kumar, 66, a senior citizen with ailments, found the ramp occupied by voters in the queue and a wheelchair lying unused beside the wall. The staff on duty told him to walk around the building and use the stairs at the other end.

District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore asked officials to ensure voters faced no inconvenience and to report the polling trend every two hours, while GVMC Commissioner Ketan Garg, noticing long queues at several stations, directed that ballot paper distribution be speeded up. Election Observer A. Bhargav Tej and Election Expenditure Observer P.V. Sandeep Reddy toured all 10 zones between them, and Mr. Sandeep Reddy expressed satisfaction over the smooth and peaceful polling.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Arrangements made by the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) enabled senior citizens, persons with disabilities and first-time voters to exercise their franchise in the urban local body elections, which passed off largely smoothly across the city on Sunday.

Most senior citizens said that the process was trouble free and that the staff guided them well. One of them, who did not wish to be named, said finding the right station was initially a problem after wards rose from 98 to 120, but the staff quickly helped.

Polling stations had drinking water, help desks, medicine counters, toilets, shamianas and ventilation, with ramps, handrails and chairs for senior citizens. Police personnel managed the crowds, and food was arranged for the staff.

At Yendada in Ward 11, around 300 voters turned up in the first hour after polling began at 7 a.m., said Booth Level Officers (BLOs) S. Srinivas and N. Nageswarao.

They added that residents of long-settled localities turned out in larger numbers than those living in apartment complexes. A similar pattern was seen later at other stations in the city. At Ward 3 in Bheemunipatnam, N. Narendra, BLO, said voting went on without hiccups, while Auxiliary Nurse Midwife N.V. Padma and ASHA worker G. Konda said they had all essential medicines, including oral rehydration salts (ORS) sachets, paracetamol and a blood pressure monitor.

First time voter show her inked finger after casting her vote at the at a polling booth in KDPM High School in the East Assembly Constituency in Visakhapatnam on Sunday | Photo Credit: V RAJU

Elisha Paul K, 21, a first-time voter pursuing an MBA at Andhra University, voted in Ward 31, Maharanipeta. He had expected a rush and lengthy queues, he said, but the process took less than 15 minutes, and the staff explained how a ballot is cast.

Patnala Papayyamma, 86, who makes it a point to vote in every election despite the hardship of travelling, her family said, voted in Ward 4 at the office of the Superintendent of Central Tax, Bheemunipatnam. Her family helped her onto a scooter allowed near the station.

First time voter shows her inked finger at a polling booth in Peda Jalaripeta, in the East Assembly Constituency on Sunday. | Photo Credit: V RAJU

At Chepala Thimmapuram in Ward 5, one of the exceptions, voting took time, with long queues continuing past noon. Jaya Kumar, 66, a senior citizen with ailments, found the ramp occupied by voters in the queue and a wheelchair lying unused beside the wall. The staff on duty told him to walk around the building and use the stairs at the other end.

District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore asked officials to ensure voters faced no inconvenience and to report the polling trend every two hours, while GVMC Commissioner Ketan Garg, noticing long queues at several stations, directed that ballot paper distribution be speeded up. Election Observer A. Bhargav Tej and Election Expenditure Observer P.V. Sandeep Reddy toured all 10 zones between them, and Mr. Sandeep Reddy expressed satisfaction over the smooth and peaceful polling.

articles.title: Aadhav Arjuna calls for a separate flag for Tamil Nadu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: He says a law should be enacted to provide for the flag, and Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay should hoist it on November 1 and July 18
Public Works Minister Aadhav Arjuna said on Sunday (November 1, 2026) that Tamil Nadu should have its own flag, along the lines of those of other States, with the Tamil language given prominence.

Addressing a meeting organised to honour Tamil scholars on the occasion of Tamil Nadu Day, he said a law should be enacted to provide for the flag, and Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay should hoist it on November 1 and July 18.
“It should be hoisted at every house. We are in a position to create a flag with a status equal to that of the national flag to proclaim the greatness of Tamils and the Tamil language,” he said.

The Minister said a message about the importance of the Tamil language should reach children in the State, as schools were promoting the idea that only English could provide employment opportunities. “We should change this perception. We should also change the attitude of taking pride in speaking English. In China, people speak Chinese, and in France, they speak French. They are not giving up their mother tongue,” he said.

Reiterating the advocacy of the two-language policy, Mr. Arjuna said English was a language of business and was necessary for commerce and trade. “A child born in Tamil Nadu should learn Tamil. Children of MLAs and Ministers should study in the Tamil medium, and the children of all IAS and IPS officers should also opt for the Tamil medium,” he added.

fullParagraphs: Palnadu District Collector Kritika Shukla has announced holiday for all government and private schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres on Tuesday (November 2) in view of Cyclone Murasu.
The Collector, in a press release here on Sunday, informed that the district administration has made all necessary arrangements to effectively deal with Cyclone Murasu.

A special control room has been set up at the Collectorate to ensure that people do not face any inconvenience due to the cyclone and to facilitate immediate relief measures. The control room will function round-the-clock. Staff have been deployed to provide necessary information to the public and coordinate relief operations.
People can contact the control room for emergency assistance or information on the number 08647 252999
In view of the cyclone warnings, the District Collector urged people to remain alert and avoid going outdoors unless absolutely necessary.
