articles.title: Andhra Pradesh civic polls largely peaceful; Jagan demands repoll in Pulivendula after clashes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Polling across 13 municipal corporations and 79 municipalities and nagar panchayats ends amid sporadic violence. The SEC puts the overall polling percentage at 48.03 by 3 p.m., reports 275 FIRs in connection with 40 incidents and says repolling, if required, will be held on November 2

Elections to 13 municipal corporations and 79 municipalities and nagar panchayats in Andhra Pradesh ended at 5 p.m. on Sunday without major law and order problems, barring incidents of stone-pelting by cadres of the TDP and the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) and the torching of several vehicles in Pulivendula.

The overall polling percentage across the urban local bodies stood at 48.03 at 3 p.m., according to information furnished by the State Election Commission (SEC), compared with 63.30 in the 2021 elections.

YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy and Kadapa MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy staged a protest in Pulivendula over alleged electoral malpractices and the prevention of YSRCP agents from entering several polling stations.

The SEC extended polling by two-and-a-half hours, until 7.30 p.m., in Ward No. 55 of the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation to rectify an error in the printing of election symbols allotted to two candidates.

In Pulivendula, Mr. Jagan demanded a repoll across the municipality, alleging that election authorities had turned a blind eye to violations that undermined the electoral process. He left without casting his vote.
Independent candidate A.B. Venkateswara Rao stages a protest at Polling Station No. 73 in New RR Peta, Vijayawada, on Sunday, demanding a repoll at the booth. | Photo Credit: G.N. Rao

Reacting to Mr. Jagan’s demand at a press conference in Vijayawada, State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha said he had sought a report from the District Collector. A decision on repolling would be taken based on formal requests from the Collector or the Superintendent of Police, supported by evidence, he said.

Meanwhile, mild tension prevailed when Mr. Jagan was on his way to the Returning Officer’s office in Pulivendula, as Sk. Dastagiri, an accused in the murder of former MP Y.S. Vivekananda Reddy, reportedly confronted the YSRCP chief over issues he had faced.
Sporadic incidents were also reported from some other places in the Rayalaseema and Palnadu regions. The respective District Collectors and District Election Authorities were inquiring into them.
State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha visiting a polling station in DAV Public School at Ibrahimpatnam near Vijayawada on Sunday.

Mr. Punetha told the media that he had spoken to the Collectors of Nandyal, Kadapa, Palnadu, Markapuram, Nellore, Prakasam, Tirupati, Chittoor, Anantapur, Kurnool, Annamayya and Sri Sathya Sai districts in the evening. Polling was by and large peaceful, he said.

He added that the incidents reported from Palnadu and Anantapur districts and Pulivendula were being investigated. A decision on whether repolling was necessary would be taken after examining field reports, as the Commission’s orders had to withstand judicial scrutiny.

articles.title: NLCIL, CISF hold fire safety awareness programme ahead of Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: CISF Fire Wing personnel demonstrated how to handle LPG leaks, tackle fires involving domestic LPG cylinders and electrical equipment, and use fire extinguishers

NLC India Limited (NLCIL) and the Fire Wing of the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) conducted a fire prevention and safety awareness programme for shopkeepers and residents at Main Bazaar in Neyveli Township recently, ahead of Deepavali.

CISF Fire Wing personnel demonstrated how to handle LPG leaks, tackle fires involving domestic LPG cylinders and electrical equipment, and use fire extinguishers. They also explained the precautions to be followed at firecracker shops.

Shopkeepers received hands-on training in operating fire extinguishers and basic firefighting techniques through live demonstrations. The programme aimed to improve preparedness and prevent fire accidents during the festive season.
B. Vaidyanathan, chief general manager, Township Administration, NLCIL and CISF officials were present.

articles.title: BJP leader questions Vijay’s silence over Mekedatu dam issue
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: BJP State president Nainar Nagenthran on Sunday questioned Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s alleged ‘silence’ over the efforts being made by the Karnataka government to construct a dam across the Cauvery at Mekedatu.

Referring to a statement by Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar that efforts were being made to acquire land for the construction of the Mekedatu dam, Mr. Nagenthran criticised both the Karnataka government’s actions and the Vijay-led TVK government’s silence on the issue.

“Karnataka is being ruled by the Congress, which is an ally of the TVK. Despite the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s directive, it [Karnataka] has not released water to Tamil Nadu... it intends to destroy the livelihood of the farmers of Tamil Nadu. Why is Mr. Vijay not opposing the Congress in Karnataka?” he asked.

articles.title: No-cost EMI: a loan that is portrayed as free
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: A ₹60,000 phone, 6 easy instalments of ₹10,000, no interest. It feels as if the shopkeeper has done you a favour. He has not. Nobody lends money for free and nobody sells at a loss. Someone pays.

Every festive season, the same board greets you at the electronics shop: “No-cost EMI”. TVs, washing machines and appliances are available at no-cost EMI. A ₹60,000 phone, 6 easy instalments of ₹10,000, no interest. It feels as if the shopkeeper has done you a favour. He has not. Nobody lends money for free and nobody sells at a loss. Someone pays. Lets see who.

A bank or finance firm funds the purchase and charges interest. The shop agrees to bear interest but it will recover it in one of two ways. Either the price quoted to you is higher, or you lose the discount a cash buyer would have got Take the same phone. A cash buyer gets it for ₹57,000. The EMI buyer pays ₹60,000. The ₹3,000 gap is the interest.

Macroeconomic & Financial Update: No-cost EMI: a loan that is portrayed as free. This development reflects key trends in India's fiscal roadmap, monetary policy transmission, and financial sector resilience.

RBI & Fiscal Dynamics: In the context of inflation targeting by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), credit growth, capital expenditure (Capex), and external balance of payments remain vital indicators for economic stability.

articles.title: Small fish: On Operation Trident
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: While carriers of narcotics are caught in the net, big sharks operate freely

Operation Trident , a multi-agency crackdown on an international syndicate operating across the India-Myanmar-Bangladesh corridor, marks a significant step-up in the government’s campaign against drug trafficking. The Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has set December 31, 2029, as the deadline to eradicate drug networks across the country. The October 23 raids, which led to 18 people being arrested , were based on NCB investigations following the arrest of an alleged Myanmar-based kingpin in Delhi this May. However, the dismantling of the entire network would require identification of all suppliers in Myanmar and their successful prosecution. The government’s strategy, involving States and Union Territories, over 40 Ministries, central agencies and the pharmaceutical sector, is outlined in the Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029), launched by Mr. Shah at the Narco-Coordination Centre meeting on June 26, 2026. It envisages dismantling 100 major cartels and improving prosecution outcomes. The broad strategy reflects the complexity of the problem and signals a more focused approach. Data for 2025 also show an increase of over 50% in arrests and a nearly 53% rise in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act compared with 2024.

However, the government’s action-plan will depend on consistent implementation and efficient coordination among agencies, and striking at the real brains behind it all. In several cases, foreign-based key operatives still remain at large and big sharks often do not fall in the net. The 2021 Mundra port case in Gujarat, involving the seizure of about 3,000 kg of heroin, is a case in point wherein the principal Afghanistan-based suppliers have yet to be brought to book. Also, the quantity of drugs seized does not, by itself, indicate whether drug availability or consumption has declined. Punjab remains a prominent example of the continuing public health challenges associated with drug abuse. The alleged drug-related killings of anti-drug activists in Mansa and Gurdaspur, along with the alleged death by suicide of a father in Sangrur who had raised concerns about the easy availability of synthetic drugs in his locality, underscore the human cost of the problem. These incidents also raise questions about the protection of those who speak out against drug trafficking and networks. These concerns lend urgency to the objective of dismantling entire networks and apprehending the “big sharks”, rather than concentrating disproportionately on individual carriers. The key is to identify the ultimate beneficiaries by meticulously following the money trail and ensuring their conviction.

articles.title: Fouled waters: On Rajasthan’s river pollution
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: River pollution from industrial effluents indicates state failure

The Supreme Court has pulled up, once again, the Rajasthan government over industrial effluents flowing into the Jojari river and the deadly risk it poses for the people depending on it. The problem is decades old — public interest litigation in the Rajasthan High Court alerted State machinery to the problem in 2011 — indicating an oversight by the State bordering on the systematic. The Jojari, the Luni, and the Bandi are seasonal rivers in the State’s arid western region, flowing through Jodhpur, Balotra, and Pali districts. This region has also evolved as a textile-dyeing and steelworking hub, and untreated or insufficiently treated effluents from these factories have run directly into the rivers and soil, endangering the health of around 20 lakh local residents. The region also suffers rampant illegal sand mining in riverbeds. The sewage treatment plants have been able to accommodate only around half of the sewage generated in the three urban centres, according to the State’s submissions to the Court in 2025, even as the Court recorded substantial underutilisation at common effluent treatment plants. The combination is suggestive of industrial sources bypassing treatment facilities, poor connections between the sources and the facilities, and/or insufficient capacity at particular sites or in specific periods.

The Court initiated a suo motu writ petition in 2025 and constituted a High-level Ecosystem Oversight Committee chaired by Justice Sangeet Lodha to audit the plants and draft a plan to restore the rivers. Based on the committee’s scathing status reports, Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta banned construction within 100 metres of the rivers’ edges and hazardous industries within 500 m of the present path, or of the flood lines where available. The Court has also upbraided local authorities for failing to enforce pollution norms by citing the Court’s own stay of a 2022 National Green Tribunal order imposing a compensation on the Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation and the local administration in Jodhpur and Barmer. The State regulatory apparatus has been dysfunctional: officials were aware of illegal mining operations in some areas, yet they regularised leases in those areas. Given the dereliction in play, the Court is correct to treat the possibility of collusion between State officials and industrial mafias seriously. Justice Mehta’s observation that the State could be held liable under the ‘polluter pays’ principle is also a significant indictment of state failure, through negligence. Now, importantly, the State still has to restore the Jojari and attend to its wellbeing, which is relevant to a recent tendency by the Court to substitute itself for regulators rather than disciplining them into discharging their functions. This needs to change.

articles.title: GSLV-F18 carrying NVS-03 lifts off from Satish Dhawan Space Centre | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: NVS-03 satellite is equipped with an indigenous atomic clock alongside procured atomic clocks

The GSLV rocket carrying the next-gen navigation satellite NVS-03 lifts off from Sriharikota Spaceport. 18.46 minutes later, the GSLV-F18 is expected to place the NVS-03 satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit. Cryo-stage performance of GSLV rocket normal
ISRO’s live coverage of the GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission will begin at 11:20 pm IST on October 30, ahead of the scheduled 11:51 pm launch from Sriharikota.

ISRO’s NVS satellite launch programme has seen considerable gaps between missions. NVS-01 was launched in May 2023, followed by NVS-02 in January 2025, a gap of 19 months. The next satellite, NVS-03, is scheduled for launch in October 2026, nearly 20 months after its predecessor.

The pace of launches has also been affected by setbacks in ISRO’s broader mission programme. The space agency recorded three failures in six missions launched from Indian soil between January 2025 and January 2026, adding to the challenges of maintaining a steady launch schedule.

Sriharikota [Andhra Pradesh], Oct 29 (ANI): A view of the NVS-03 satellite, which will enter the Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit in the 20th GSLV-F18 flight from Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR), in Sriharikota on Thursday. The launch is scheduled for October 30. (@isro X/ANI Photo)

The United States operates the Global Positioning System (GPS), a satellite network that underpins a vast range of civilian, commercial and military activities across the world. While 24 satellites are considered sufficient to provide global coverage and optimal performance, the US maintains a larger constellation of at least 30 satellites. This additional capacity acts as a safety net, ensuring uninterrupted and reliable services even if some satellites malfunction or go out of service.

China, meanwhile, runs its own satellite-based navigation network, BeiDou, as an alternative to GPS and to meet its domestic and global positioning requirements. BeiDou’s global navigation services are designed around a constellation of 30 satellites, with estimates suggesting that approximately 35 satellites are currently in orbit.

Restoring NavIC to its minimum operational capacity would require ISRO to launch at least two more NVS-series satellites, NVS-04 and NVS-05, in addition to the existing NVS-01 and the upcoming NVS-03. These four satellites would form the minimum constellation needed to resume the system’s core navigation services. The launches would need to be carried out within a relatively short timeframe to ensure continuity.

However, four satellites would only meet the basic requirement. For greater reliability, stronger coverage and uninterrupted services, India would need additional backup satellites in orbit. This would mean building and maintaining a constellation of around six to seven NVS-series satellites to ensure the long-term stability of a regional navigation system like NavIC.

For NavIC’s core services to function effectively, at least four satellites are theoretically required. However, information shared by the Indian government indicates that only three of the constellation’s 11 satellites are currently capable of performing their primary functions.

These include first-generation satellites IRNSS-1B and IRNSS-1I, along with second-generation satellite NVS-01. IRNSS-1B has already exceeded its designed 10-year lifespan, making its continued operation uncertain, while IRNSS-1I could remain functional until around 2028. NVS-01, if it performs as intended, has at least another decade of service ahead. Meanwhile, NVS-02, launched in January 2025, was unable to raise its orbit after its onboard engines failed to fire, severely limiting its utility. As a result, NVS-01 is currently the only satellite that can be considered reliably operational over the long term.
ISRO’s NVS-03 launch could restore NavIC’s functionality, upgrading indigenous clocks and improving regional navigation amid recent launch setbacks.

articles.title: Man held for possession of 22 country-made explosives in Ranipet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: He was lodged in Central Prison in Vellore
A 20-year-old tribal, who belongs to the Irula community, was arrested by the Forest Department in Ranipet on Friday for possession of 22 country-made explosives.

Forest officials identified the arrested person as V. Devak Kumar, a resident of Irular colony near Arcot town. Initial inquiry revealed that a team of forest officials were on patrol in Pakkiri reserve forests near Kaveripakkam village, when they intercepted Kumar.
Upon inquiry, Kumar took the team to a hideout spot where he had stored country-made explosives for allegedly hunting small wild animals.
Based on a complaint by forest officials, a case was registered by Kaveripakkam police. Later, Kumar was lodged in Central Prison in Vellore. A probe is under way.

articles.title: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Bank measures can only limit damage from ‘digital arrest’ scams

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation , during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams , that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.

Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.
Editorial Context: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.summary: Bank measures can only limit damage from ‘digital arrest’ scams
articles.keyPoints:
• Bank measures can only limit damage from ‘digital arrest’ scams
• Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation , during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams , that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.
• Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.

articles.title: Suboptimal outcomes: On social security boards for unorganised, gig, platform workers
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Social security concerns of unorganised sector workers remain

One year after the implementation of the Code on Social Security , the Union Labour Ministry has constituted the National Social Security Boards for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers. The constitution of the boards, though delayed, is a welcome step. However, the highly centralised nature of this mechanism may hinder its optimal outcomes. By design, the Union Government controls both the Boards: they will be chaired by Union Minister for Labour Mansukh Mandaviya. The Board for Unorganised Sector Workers will have 40 members, nominated by the Union Government. They include seven members representing unorganised sector workers and seven members representing employers of the unorganised sector. Similarly, the Board for the welfare of gig and platform workers will have 22 members with five representatives each from the aggregators and the workers. But they have no significant representation of Central Trade Unions from the Opposition side or from the State Governments ruled by the Opposition. Labour is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and both the States and the Union must work together to improve the living standards of workers.

The International Labour Organization defines social security as the ‘protection that a society provides to individuals and households to ensure access to health care and to guarantee income security, particularly in cases of old age, unemployment, sickness, invalidity, work injury, maternity or loss of a breadwinner’. The Union Government claims that the country’s social security coverage has increased from 19% in 2015 to 64.3% in 2025, which is around 94 crore citizens. However, it is apparent that the unorganised and gig and platform workers, who make up more than 92% of the country’s total workforce, are far from enjoying any social security under this definition. Almost two decades ago, the National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector, headed by economist Arjun Sengupta, recommended a slew of measures to improve the social security of workers in the informal sector. The issues raised by the panel still remain unaddressed. A report prepared by Justice V. Gopala Gowda for the Keralam Government in March this year flagged certain anti-federal and anti-worker characteristics in the Social Security Code and suggested amendments. The Union Government should take the trade unions and the State Governments on board while creating new systems and mechanisms to address the social security concerns of the vast majority of workers.

articles.title: Bihar’s interests must be considered in the Ganga Water Treaty: Samrat Choudhary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The CM mentioned that Bihar’s rivers hold immense potential for the State, and through the proper management of their water and silt, new opportunities can be created in agriculture, industry, infrastructure, and employment

Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Friday (October 30, 2026) said that Bihar’s interests must be given top priority in matters concerning the Ganga Water and the Farakka Treaty. He said this during a one-day seminar organised by the State Water Resources Department titled ‘Ganga Water Treaty: Water Security of Bihar’.
He asserted that the availability of sufficient water is crucial for the holistic development of Bihar, the expansion of agriculture, and industrial progress.

“The State requires water for drinking, irrigation of farmlands, and the operation of industries. Bihar’s interests must be given top priority in matters concerning the Ganga water and the Farakka Treaty. The 25-year-old dispute between Bihar and Jharkhand over the sharing of Sone River water has been resolved with the assistance of the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, ensuring that Bihar receives three-fourths (3/4) of the water,”Mr. Choudhary said.

He added that it is a major achievement toward the better management of the State’s water resources. The Chief Minister also said that the State government has formulated a State-level policy for ‘Silt Management ', and a scientific approach will be adopted for the removal and utilisation of silt extracted from the Ganga and other rivers.

“Efforts will be made to make the silt and soil from the Ganga available for public use, as well as for construction projects such as roads and other infrastructure. An agreement will be signed between the Government of Bihar and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) in the near future. There is also a need to develop a silt management policy at the national level,”Mr. Choudhary said.

Emphasising the construction and strengthening of embankments along the Ganga, the Chief Minister called for the necessity of scientific understanding of the river’s flow and management, and acting accordingly.

He suggested that experts participating in the seminar should conduct an aerial survey of the Ganga to gain a direct assessment of the river’s current state, flow, and silt accumulation, enabling them to provide effective recommendations.

Mr. Choudhary mentioned that Bihar’s rivers hold immense potential for the State, and through the proper management of their water and silt, new opportunities can be created in agriculture, industry, infrastructure, and employment.
“The State government aims to generate employment and job opportunities for one crore people, a goal in which the optimal use of water resources will play a crucial role,”Mr. Choudhary said.

He reiterated the commitment to transform Bihar’s rivers into the foundation of the State’s economic prosperity. He suggested that through the scientific management of water resources, expert guidance, and the support of the Central Government, Bihar will be steered toward new heights of development.

articles.title: TNUHDB identifies 20 sites for reconstruction across State; appeals to residents of dilapidated tenements to vacate
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Tamil Nadu Urban Habitat Development Board (TNUHDB) has identified 20 locations across the State for reconstruction of ageing tenements during 2026-27 and plans to build greenfield resettlement sites in Perambur and Madurantakam.

TNUHDB Chairperson Ku. Pa. Krishnan, in an interaction with journalists on Friday, said that the reconstruction projects involve demolishing existing ageing tenements and constructing new housing units at the same locations. Residents can return after the work is completed. The Board has identified a total of 70 sites for reconstruction across the State, which will be taken up in phases, he said.

The TNUHDB also appealed to residents of 23 dilapidated sites to temporarily vacate their houses in view of the ongoing northeast monsoon. Of the 23 tenements identified in its safety advisory, 14 fell within the locations proposed for reconstruction this year, for which a Government Order is to be issued in the coming week. The remaining nine have been additionally prioritised for safety during the monsoon in view of their dilapidated condition.

The 23 tenements include Srinivasapuram, V.O.C. Nagar, Old Block Vyasarpadi, Nagooran Thottam, Annathai Kuppam, Nallankuppam (Old), N.V.N. Nagar (Phase-II), West Cemetery Road, Pallakumaniyam and Kabali Thottam, and Rukmani Nagar.

Mr. Krishnan said the Board was willing to undertake reconstruction of structurally weak buildings but residents’ cooperation in vacating the premises was essential. Citing Srinivasapuram, where tenements constructed in the 1970s had deteriorated over the years, he said the Board was ready to rebuild the houses and hand them back to the residents.

Two new settlement sites will come up in Perambur and Madurantakam, with Mullai Nagar identified as the location for the Perambur project. Both projects are expected to have over 450 housing units. A G.O. will be issued in the coming weeks, said Ramana Saraswathi, Managing Director, TNUHDB.

The constructions are proposed as ground-plus-six-floor buildings and are intended for eligible families living on vulnerable and objectionable poromboke land, including flood-prone areas lacking basic infrastructure.

Mr. Krishnan also spoke about the infrastructure challenges at two housing projects taken up during the previous DMK government in Dindigul district. At Oddanchatram, 480 housing units were constructed at a cost of ₹66.23 crore. “The Board is now spending an additional ₹7.14 crore to provide drinking water connectivity to the site. Nearly 90% of the work is over. But the site has poor road connectivity. We will have to look at the other amenities required to make such locations liveable,” he said.

He said a similar situation prevails at Keeranur in Dindigul district, where 432 houses were constructed at a cost of ₹57.04 crore. “Such housing projects across the State would be reviewed to assess their location, infrastructure facilities and suitability for habitation. Action will be initiated if any irregularities are found,” he said.

articles.title: Bengaluru needs long-term master plan for water, roads and sewerage: KBG

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 31 Oct 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Bengaluru needs long-term master plan for water, roads and sewerage: KBG

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda has directed officials to prepare a comprehensive, long-term master plan to provide drinking water, road connectivity, and underground drainage infrastructure across the Bengaluru Urban district, including areas beyond the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) limits.

Mr. Gowda chaired the fourth Executive Committee meeting of the Bengaluru Development Authority at Vikas Soudha on Friday. He said infrastructure projects must be taken up in phases with clearly defined timelines, keeping pace with the city’s rapid expansion.

The Minister said a uniform policy would hold agencies excavating roads accountable for restoration, with clear standards, cost recovery and penalties for violations.

He also stressed the need to prioritise scientific treatment and reuse of sewage to improve water security. He cited the KC Valley, HN Valley, and Vrishabhavathi Valley projects, which supply treated wastewater to lakes across neighbouring districts.

Further, he directed the BMTC to introduce GPS-enabled feeder buses within a 2 to 3 km radius of Metro stations, with fixed routes. Plans are also under way to integrate private auto-rickshaw and taxi services with the BMTC 2.0 app, which already facilitates combined ticket bookings for Metro and BMTC services.

The government has also approved nine additional fire stations across the five municipal corporations under the GBA, taking the proposed network beyond the existing 20, he said.

articles.title: Seven packaged drinking water units closed for violations in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: 102 units inspected in two days; 69 water samples collected for laboratory analysis

Karnataka’s Food Safety and Drug Administration has closed seven packaged drinking water units across Karnataka for major violations, including severe unhygienic conditions, operating without mandatory licences and non-cooperation with inspection teams, as part of a Statewide special inspection drive.

Officials also seized 82 cases of one-litre packaged drinking water bottles, valued at ₹7,380, from M.S. Food and Beverages in Devanahalli taluk of Bengaluru Rural district after detecting labelling defects.

As many as 102 packaged drinking water units were inspected between October 29 and 30, 69 water samples collected for laboratory analysis and issued notices to 53 food business operators (FBOs) for various violations.

On the second day of the drive, officials inspected 57 units and collected 37 samples for testing. Notices were issued to 29 units for violations, including unhygienic conditions, absence of medical certificates for food handlers, labelling defects, non-availability of water analysis reports and lack of mandatory pest control certificates.
Among the units closed were S.P. Food and Beverages in Hassan district, Avanti Industries in Bengaluru Urban district and Sai Ram Food Beverages in Bidar district for severe unhygienic conditions.

Om Shakthi Minerals in Bengaluru Urban, Nandi Food and Beverages in Kalaburagi and Dalia Beverages in Mysuru Rural were shut down for operating without the mandatory Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) licence. Nandi Food and Beverages was also found to be maintaining unhygienic conditions.
Aqua Refresh Packaged Drinking Water Unit in Kalaburagi district was closed following non-cooperation during inspection and investigation.
The samples collected during the inspections have been sent to government food laboratories to assess their quality and compliance with prescribed food safety standards.

The department said the special inspection drive would continue across the State and warned that stringent legal action would be initiated against packaged drinking water units found violating the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the rules framed under it.

articles.title: Karnataka High Court to nominate new head for SIT to probe KPSC irregularities on Monday
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: State government issues notification declaring SIT as police station

The State government on Friday issued a notification declaring the Special Investigation Team (SIT), which has been constituted by the High Court of Karnataka to probe cases related to alleged irregularity and corruption in recruitment process in the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC), to be a police station under Section 2(1)(u) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).

The notification was issued as the High Court on October 28 questioned the inaction on the part of the State government in not declaring the SIT as a police station in terms of High Court’s September 21 direction even 15 days after the Supreme Court on October 13 upheld the order of the High Court in constituting a SIT by the High Court.

The investigation officers appointed to the SIT are authorised under Section 193 of the BNSS to file police reports before the competent courts after investigation into the two cases related to the KPSC irregularities, it has been stated in the notification, a copy of which has been submitted to the High Court on Friday.

Justice M. Nagaprasanna, who took on record the notification, said that the court would pass orders on head of the SIT by considering the names of four senior officers suggested by the State government in terms of the order passed by the apex court on an appeal filed by the government.

The government had filed appeal before the apex court against the High Court’s September 21 order of constituting the SIT, appointing Director-General of Police Alok Kumar as its head, along with four other IPS officers, and directing the SIT to conduct investigation afresh.

However, as the apex court had observed that “...having regard to the seriousness of the allegations and possibility of the involvement of functionaries in the KPSC, the case requires investigation by a SIT comprising high ranking officers, therefore, we do not find a good reason to interfere with the impugned order (of the High Court) insofar as it directs for investigation by an SIT.”

As the apex court found the SIT a necessity, the government had confined its challenge “only to the composition of the SIT and the direction to conduct investigation afresh by pointing out certain reservation about Mr. Kumar heading it.
Besides, the government had pointed out possible conflict of interest in the inclusion of IPS officer Divya Gopinath, Director of Forensic Sciences Laboratory, in the SIT.

Though the apex court set aside the High Court’s order for conducting probe afresh, it left it to the High Court to appoint/substitute the head/member in the SIT constituted earlier, while giving liberty to the State government to suggest names of senior police officers to the SIT.

Now, the State government has suggested Additional Directors General of Police, R. Hitendra, B.K. Singh, S. Murugan, and Soumendu Mukherjee to head the SIT, and the advocates for the petitioners, Basanagouda R. Patil Yatnal, MLA, All Karnataka State Students’ Association, and Manjunath, who had sought probe by independent investigation for the KPSC irregularities, have filed their objections/responses for nominating among these officers to the SIT.

articles.title: Japan’s Omron Healthcare opens first India manufacturing facility near Chennai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Japan’s Omron Healthcare on Friday formally inaugurated its first India production facility in Gummidipoondi near Chennai. The new unit, spread over an area of 258,333 square feet at Origins by Mahindra industrial estate in Puduvoyal, has been built within three years of the Japanese firm signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Tamil Nadu government in 2023.

Designed to produce about 300,000 blood pressure monitors annually, the company plans to increase its production capacity tenfold to make 30 lakh units annually in the next two years. Omron will manufacture three models of blood pressure monitors at the new facility. The firm is also looking at exporting blood pressure monitors manufactured at the new factory to the European market by next year. “We plan to make Chennai a base not just for the Indian market but also develop it as a base for exports,” Ayumu Okada, president and CEO, Omron Healthcare Company Limited, said.

Muneo Takahashi, Consul General of Japan in Chennai said: “Tamil Nadu has become an important destination for Japanese investment, supported by its strong industrial base, skilled human resources and excellent infrastructure.”

Deepak Jacob, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Guidance said: “In 1972, Omron‘s founder joined hands with Dr. Yutaka Nakamura — a doctor known as the father of Japan’s Paralympic movement — to open Omron Taiyo in Beppu. It was Japan’s first welfare factory run and staffed by people with disabilities. People called it “the factory with wheelchairs.” And a second such factory followed in Kyoto in 1985.” Omron‘s commitment to employing persons with disabilities in this plant (Chennai) reflects exactly that value. It will inspire industries across our State to see ability first, he added.

Approximately 300 million people nationwide are estimated to be living with hypertension, while the World Health Organization (WHO) identifies cardiovascular diseases like stroke and heart failure among the country’s leading causes of death. As India’s economy continues to grow at approximately 7% annually, lifestyle changes mean that the prevalence of hypertension is expected to rise further, adding to such challenges and increasing the need for preventive healthcare. Yet fewer than 5% of households have a home blood pressure monitor in regular use, while access to healthcare services also remains limited in many regions. By strengthening the domestic supply of blood pressure monitors, Omron Healthcare aims to support more widespread home monitoring, earlier identification of cardiovascular risks, and improved hypertension management, the company said.

articles.title: NVS-03 launched successfully; satellite placed in intended orbit | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: NVS-03 satellite is equipped with an indigenous atomic clock alongside procured atomic clocks

The GSLV rocket carrying the next-gen navigation satellite NVS-03 lifts off from Sriharikota Spaceport. 18.46 minutes later, the GSLV-F18 is expected to place the NVS-03 satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit. Cryo-stage performance of GSLV rocket normal
ISRO’s live coverage of the GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission will begin at 11:20 pm IST on October 30, ahead of the scheduled 11:51 pm launch from Sriharikota.

ISRO’s NVS satellite launch programme has seen considerable gaps between missions. NVS-01 was launched in May 2023, followed by NVS-02 in January 2025, a gap of 19 months. The next satellite, NVS-03, is scheduled for launch in October 2026, nearly 20 months after its predecessor.

The pace of launches has also been affected by setbacks in ISRO’s broader mission programme. The space agency recorded three failures in six missions launched from Indian soil between January 2025 and January 2026, adding to the challenges of maintaining a steady launch schedule.

As a result, NVS-01 is currently the only satellite that can be considered reliably operational over the long term.

articles.title: NVS-03 satellite launch successful: ISRO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The 2250 kg NVS-03 is the third satellite in the next-generation navigation satellite system envisaged for providing continuity of navigation services for the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System series

The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-F18) on Friday (October 30, 2026) successfully launched the NVS-03 satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, according to the ISRO.
The GSLV-F18 with the NVS-03 satellite lifted off from the second launch pad of the spaceport and, 18 minutes later placed the satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit.

“The GSLV-F18 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the NVS-03 satellite weighing 2250 kg in the intended elliptical orbit. Let me congratulate each and every team member of ISRO, industrial partners, academia for this outstanding accomplishment,” ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan said.
He added that the vehicle systems have performed as predicted and as expected.

The 2250 kg NVS-03 is the third satellite in the next-generation navigation satellite system envisaged for providing continuity of navigation services for the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS) series or the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC).
According to the ISRO, the satellite carries an indigenous atomic clock, along with procured atomic clocks.
“It also includes L1 signal in addition to existing L5/S signals with coverage over India landmass and a region extending 1,500 km around Indian geopolitical boundary,” the ISRO said.

NavIC is India’s independent regional navigation satellite system designed to provide accurate position, navigation, and Timing (PNT) services to users in India as well as the region extending about 1,500 km beyond the Indian landmass, which is its primary service area.

The successful launch of the NVS-03, which will have a mission life of 12 years, is expected to restore the functioning of the NavIC constellation, which has been weakened due to repeated failures of atomic clocks and the ISRO’s inability to place its previous replacement satellite, NVS-02, in its intended orbit.
It can be recalled that earlier this year, on March 13, the last functioning atomic clock aboard IRNSS-1F had stopped working.
The ISRO Chairman said that with the success of the mission, the NavIC constellation is restored to the minimum operational configuration with four satellites.

“Already three satellites are successfully working in orbit, with this satellite we will have four satellites and restore the PNT services of the country. As you know, the NavIC constellation is a strategic national asset that provides the nation independent access to PNT services. It is also used for civilian applications like real-time tracking of trains along with tracking of vehicles and shipping vessels. It is an important component of the One Nation One Time Project,” the ISRO Chairman said.

articles.title: KTR questions proposed sale of IDBI Bank, asks if its valuable real estate assets were factored in valuation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: BRS working president sought to know why the concerns raised by IDBI Bank employees over the proposed disinvestment were not being addressed

Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president K.T. Rama Rao has questioned the Union government’s proposed sale of IDBI Bank to a private player , raising concerns over the bank’s valuation, changes in bidding norms and the treatment of its real estate assets.

In a post on X, KTR said public sector undertakings (PSUs) and public sector banks were national assets that needed to be safeguarded. He said reports about the alleged undervaluation of IDBI Bank were a matter of concern and sought to know why the rules and valuation methodology were changed after bids fell below the reserve price.
He also questioned whether the bank’s valuable real estate assets, including prime land in Hyderabad, were adequately factored into the valuation.
KTR sought to know why the concerns raised by IDBI Bank employees over the proposed disinvestment were not being addressed.

Before selling a reputed public sector bank to a private entity, the Union government owed the country clear answers on the valuation and the process being followed, he said. Questioning the urgency behind the proposed sale, the BRS leader asked: “What’s the hurry?”.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Congress, VCK mobilise cadres for Nov. 1 INDIA bloc protest in New Delhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “We expect more than five lakh Congress cadres to participate. From Tamil Nadu, we are expecting at least 100 party workers to reach New Delhi from each district,” says MP R. Sudha

Demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) have activated their respective party machineries to mobilise cadres for the INDIA bloc protest to be held on November 1, 2026, in New Delhi.

While the bulk of the heavy lifting would be done by the Indian National Congress, which is much stronger in and around New Delhi, the TNCC leaders, on their part, are expected to mobilise at least 150 people from every district in Tamil Nadu.
Mayiladuthurai MP R. Sudha said that the party’s rank and file are enthusiastic and have heeded the call of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, who is expected to lead the protest.

“We expect more than five lakh Congress cadres to participate. From Tamil Nadu, we are expecting at least 100 party workers to reach New Delhi from each district. Apart from them, the office-bearers of the Mahila Congress, Youth Congress, and other party wings will also participate,” she said.

While the Congress party is mobilising people from across the country, Ms. Sudha alleged that the BJP-led Centre was trying to curtail the privileges of Members of Parliament by not allowing Emergency Quotas in trains and not providing accommodation to their guests.

“EQ is not being released. Family members are not being given accommodation, which we are usually allotted. Congress MPs, in particular, are being singled out. They are curtailing our privileges and our movement. This is an undeclared emergency,” she said.

A senior VCK leader said that the party has asked its organs in Tamil Nadu and across southern States such as Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Keralam to mobilise a modest number of party cadres for the protest in New Delhi.

Rescue work started at 5 a.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026) but the recovery from the remote area would be difficult, they said. The operation had been halted on Friday (October 30, 2026) due to darkness, the presence of wild bears and other animals and difficult terrain.

On Friday (October 30, 2026), officials had informed that after recovery, the bodies will be brought to Joshimath town where post-mortem will be conducted on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

articles.title: ABVP holds ‘Save Democracy’ march in Patna amid SIR row
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ABVP National Secretary Abhay Pratap Singh said that in a democracy, governments change through ballots, not mob rule. He added that attempts to pressurise constitutional institutions are unacceptable

Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) members on Friday (October 30, 2026) took out a protest march in Bihar’s Patna under the campaign ‘ Loktantra Bachao Arajakta Hatao’ (Save Democracy, End Anarchy).

Hitting out at the Congress party, the ABVP members gathered at Kargil Chowk to convey the message of unity against alleged attempts to weaken democracy and democratic institutions. Despite continuous rainfall, a large number of students and activists from various districts of north Bihar and south Bihar participated in the programme.

Holding the national flag and ABVP flag, the protesters crossed the police barricades and marched towards Dak Bungalow Chauraha, where the rally concluded. ABVP National Secretary Abhay Pratap Singh and newly elected Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) President Yash Dabas were leading the march.
The protesters also broke the police barricading near JP Golambar before reaching Dak Bungalow and attempted to stand on the barricading.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Singh said, “India is a democratic country where governments are formed and changed through the people’s votes, not through demonstrations of strength on the streets. Anarchy aimed at changing governments in India, inspired by political developments in Bangladesh and Nepal, is unacceptable.”

“Amid questions surrounding the role of external forces, it is clear that India’s political direction will be determined by Indian citizens. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is a regular administrative process, and allegations of irregularities in it should be raised before constitutional forums with supporting evidence,” he added.

Mr. Singh pointed out that raising questions about the credibility of institutions like the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the Supreme Court for political interests, and attempting to bring them under pressure, goes against democratic principles.

“Those who are dreaming to bring a change of Government in India through anarchy, must understand that India’s democracy is strong and the future of Governments here is decided by the people,”Mr. Singh said.

ABVP called upon the youth of the country to remain vigilant in protecting the dignity of constitutional institutions, democratic values and national interest, and to oppose the politics of anarchy and mobocracy through democratic means.

“The roots of India’s youth lie in its rich cultural heritage, civilisational consciousness and sense of duty towards the nation. India’s youth take pride in their cultural identity and believe in positive, constructive and democratic approaches to resolve the country’s challenges,’ Mr. Dabas said.

He also said that through the student march in Patna, students have made it clear that the energy of Indian youth will be channelled towards nation-building, social harmony and strengthening the country’s cultural heritage.

articles.title: Two militants held for 'involvement' in kidnapping of woman in Manipur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: "They have been suspected of being involved in the kidnapping of a woman from Top Awang Leikai in Imphal East district on September 3," says police
Two members of a proscribed outfit were arrested for allegedly being involved in the kidnapping of a woman in Manipur's Imphal East district, police said on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

A joint team of police commandos and 31st Assam Rifles personnel apprehended the two militants, who belong to the banned Kangleipak Communist Party (Nongdrenkhomba), on Thursday (October 29), a police statement said.
"They have been suspected of being involved in the kidnapping of a woman from Top Awang Leikai in Imphal East district on September 3," police said.
A firearm along with ammunition and a car were seized from their possession, it said.
Security forces have been conducting search operations in Manipur since ethnic violence broke out in the State three years ago.

The ethnic conflict that erupted in May 2023 between the valley-based Meitei and hill-based Kuki communities has claimed at least 306 lives, while 49 people remain missing and thousands have been left homeless. In recent months, clashes between Kuki and Naga communities have also been reported.

articles.title: Jadu, lone rhino at Thiruvananthapuram zoo, dead
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The rhino, affectionately called Shambhu by zoo staff, was 39
Jadu, the lone one-horned rhinoceros at the Thiruvananthapuram zoo in Keralam and one of the main attractions of the facility for some three decades, died on Friday night.
The rhino, affectionately called Shambhu by the zoo staff, was 39. He was under treatment for old-age related ailments. The average lifespan of rhinoceros is around 35-40 years.
A ‘veteran’ of the zoo, Jadu was transported from the State Zoological Park, Guwahati, Assam, on May 19, 1993, by incurring an expenditure of ₹6.5 lakh. He was five then.
It was a lonely life for him though since Rita, a female rhino, was gored to death by Ramu, a male rhino, in 2004. Ramu too died of illness later.
A post-mortem examination is set to be conducted under the leadership of zoo veterinary surgeon Nikesh Kiran and State Institute for Animal Diseases, Palode, pathologist Harish.

articles.title: G20 foreign ministers to end Atlanta meeting without consensus on key issues
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Divisions over Russia’s war with Ukraine overshadowed the talks, with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio set to release a chairman’s statement instead of a joint communique

Top diplomats from the Group of 20 (G20) largest world economies will wrap up two days of talks in Atlanta on Saturday (October 31, 2026) without reaching consensus on several critical global security issues, after divisions, notably over Russia’s war with Ukraine, overshadowed the start of the meeting.

As a result, the group will not release a joint communique, but will rely on a chairman’s statement summarising the talks, which U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will release at the conclusion, according to diplomats who attended.

Mr. Rubio, who opened the talks with an appeal for unity, cancelled the traditional group photograph of the foreign ministers on Friday (October 30, 2026), after European diplomats objected to the inclusion of Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and threatened to boycott or walk out of the photograph that often kicks off such gatherings.

Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, who was representing his country for the first time as a guest at a G20 meeting, said on Friday he was not surprised by the failure to reach consensus. “We have wars going on, and we have participants in those wars around the table, so it’s very difficult to agree on a common line,” he told reporters.

Other participants, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the closed-door talks, said all had agreed to try to overcome their differences despite the long odds, and to work to make next month’s G20 leaders’ summit, hosted by President Donald Trump in Florida, a success.

These diplomats said a chairman’s statement had long been the plan, given the deep differences among the attendees, including over the Russia-Ukraine conflict, the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, U.S. tariffs and Chinese actions in the South China Sea.

All have contributed to spikes in the global cost of fuel, as well as uncertainty about trade. They described the opening session as cordial, but said Russia’s position on Ukraine is unyielding — as is its opposition to Poland’s membership in the G20. The disagreements also include the Trump administration’s decision not to invite G20 member South Africa, over the objections of others.

Some G20 countries had already expressed concern that the U.S. invited Russia during its heightened attacks on Ukraine, especially after Mr. Trump pushed ties with Ukraine to new lows by waiving fresh sanctions on Moscow and temporarily limiting logistical and intelligence assistance. However, the State Department announced on Friday that it had approved a proposed $2.1 billion sale of Patriot air defence interceptors for Ukraine.
Mr. Lavrov said Moscow would not allow a situation in which Ukraine poses a “military threat to legitimate security interests of the Russian Federation.”

He has travelled only infrequently to NATO member countries since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and severe sanctions were imposed on Moscow, and it is unclear if Russian President Vladimir Putin will accept Mr. Trump’s invitation to attend the leaders’ summit at his Miami golf club in December 2026.

The U.S. has said a top priority for the meeting is resolving differences over issues related to freedom of navigation, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, the Black Sea and the South China Sea. The topic will include discussions on Iran, Russia-Ukraine and China and its smaller neighbours.

But hanging over the meeting is the prospect of new U.S. military intervention in Iran, which has put the region, including G20 member Saudi Arabia, on edge. Mr. Rubio met on the sidelines with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan, as well as Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, whose country has been a key mediator.

Top diplomats from the Group of 20 (G20) largest world economies will wrap up two days of talks in Atlanta on Saturday (October 31, 2026) without reaching consensus on several critical global security issues, after divisions, notably over Russia’s war with Ukraine, overshadowed the start of the meeting.

As a result, the group will not release a joint communique, but will rely on a chairman’s statement summarising the talks, which U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will release at the conclusion, according to diplomats who attended.

Mr. Rubio, who opened the talks with an appeal for unity, cancelled the traditional group photograph of the foreign ministers on Friday (October 30, 2026), after European diplomats objected to the inclusion of Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and threatened to boycott or walk out of the photograph that often kicks off such gatherings.

Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, who was representing his country for the first time as a guest at a G20 meeting, said on Friday he was not surprised by the failure to reach consensus. “We have wars going on, and we have participants in those wars around the table, so it’s very difficult to agree on a common line,” he told reporters.

Other participants, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the closed-door talks, said all had agreed to try to overcome their differences despite the long odds, and to work to make next month’s G20 leaders’ summit, hosted by President Donald Trump in Florida, a success.

These diplomats said a chairman’s statement had long been the plan, given the deep differences among the attendees, including over the Russia-Ukraine conflict, the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, U.S. tariffs and Chinese actions in the South China Sea.

All have contributed to spikes in the global cost of fuel, as well as uncertainty about trade. They described the opening session as cordial, but said Russia’s position on Ukraine is unyielding — as is its opposition to Poland’s membership in the G20. The disagreements also include the Trump administration’s decision not to invite G20 member South Africa, over the objections of others.

Some G20 countries had already expressed concern that the U.S. invited Russia during its heightened attacks on Ukraine, especially after Mr. Trump pushed ties with Ukraine to new lows by waiving fresh sanctions on Moscow and temporarily limiting logistical and intelligence assistance. However, the State Department announced on Friday that it had approved a proposed $2.1 billion sale of Patriot air defence interceptors for Ukraine.

Mr. Lavrov said Moscow would not allow a situation in which Ukraine poses a “military threat to legitimate security interests of the Russian Federation.”

He has travelled only infrequently to NATO member countries since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and severe sanctions were imposed on Moscow, and it is unclear if Russian President Vladimir Putin will accept Mr. Trump’s invitation to attend the leaders’ summit at his Miami golf club in December 2026.

The U.S. has said a top priority for the meeting is resolving differences over issues related to freedom of navigation, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, the Black Sea and the South China Sea. The topic will include discussions on Iran, Russia-Ukraine and China and its smaller neighbours.

But hanging over the meeting is the prospect of new U.S. military intervention in Iran, which has put the region, including G20 member Saudi Arabia, on edge. Mr. Rubio met on the sidelines with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan, as well as Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, whose country has been a key mediator.

articles.title: Trump backtracks on rallies in turbulent end to midterms campaign
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The U.S. President reinstated two rallies in Kansas and Iowa a day after cancelling them, saying Republicans “have a shot” in the midterms as a record 47.9 million Americans have already voted

U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday (October 30, 2026) insisted Republicans “have a shot” at success in the U.S. midterms, despite a feverish end to the campaign for elections that will decide control of Congress.
Mr. Trump reversed course and reinstated two rallies in Kansas and Iowa a day after cancelling them, a move that had raised questions about his health and about the state of the race.

“There’s such love in these all over the country,” he said of his rallies, before rattling off a series of insults against Democratic candidates vying for House and Senate seats in the elections on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

Speaking late on Friday to a crowd in Daytona, Florida, Mr. Trump said the rallies were being held “for one very simple reason: to stop America-hating communists from taking over the United States Congress.”

He reiterated his promise to give every adult American citizen $5,000 if Republicans retain control of both chambers of Congress. Experts have questioned whether he has the legal authority to do that.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Trump acknowledged to reporters that a sitting President’s party often suffers in midterm elections. “I think we have a shot at doing well. Maybe very well, but you know, pretty well,” he said.

Republicans are defending their 53-47 majority in the Senate, while Democrats are seeking to capture at least one chamber of Congress and curb Mr. Trump’s legislative agenda during his final two years in office.

Mr. Trump has put himself at the centre of the Republicans’ midterm strategy, hoping it will fire up his MAGA (Make America Great Again) base. But his dismal approval ratings and public anger over the Iran war and the cost of living may be a drag on Republican chances.
Mr. Trump, who complained of losing his voice earlier this week, had lashed out on Thursday (October 29, 2026) when asked if he was scrapping the Kansas trip because he was “sick of traveling.”
“I feel perfect,” he snapped, saying he no longer needed to visit Kansas because Republican Senator Roger Marshall was “doing very well.”
But the about-face was likely the result of questions over the energy levels of America’s oldest-ever elected President, political strategist Mike Fahey told AFP .

“My suspicion is that Trump didn’t particularly like that narrative, and putting the events back on the calendar was the fastest way to kill it,” said Mr. Fahey, a veteran of multiple election campaigns. Both Kansas and Iowa voted comfortably for Mr. Trump in 2024, but have emerged as unexpected battlegrounds for Republicans.

articles.title: Jaishankar, Anita Anand agree that Modi’s Canada visit in December will be ‘another building block’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: External Affairs Minister Jaishankar met Canadian counterpart Anita Anand in Atlanta on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met his Canadian counterpart Anita Anand and agreed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Canada in December will be another “building block” in ties between the two countries.

Mr. Jaishankar met Ms. Anand in Atlanta on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting on Friday (October 30, 2026). Both the leaders also assessed the “steady growth” in India-Canada cooperation.
“Delighted to meet FM @AnitaAnandMP of Canada today. Assessed the steady growth of our cooperation,” Jaishankar said in a post on X on Friday (October 30, 2026).

According to an official statement, “the ministers agreed that Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Canada in December will be another building block in the two countries’ ambitious relationship.” They also “agreed” to stay in close contact ahead of the visit, it said.

Earlier this month, during her visit to India, Canadian Foreign Minister Anand met Prime Minister Modi, and she said they had a productive discussion on further strengthening India-Canada ties in trade, technology and energy.
On October 16, the Indian High Commission in Ottawa said Mr. Modi will visit Canada on December 11 and 12. The date of the visit was also confirmed by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.
Mr. Carney had said he spoke to Modi and the visit will take place in Toronto and Ottawa. “We’ll see if we can broaden it out,” he said earlier this month.
ALSO WATCH Falling short on Marco Rubio’s second visit to India | The Hindu Editorial
Mr. Jaishankar also met foreign ministers of Argentina, Mexico, Brazil, and Germany. “Glad to meet FM Pablo Quirno of Argentina on the sidelines of G20,” he said.
Mr. Jaishankar said he discussed trade, critical minerals, defence and nuclear cooperation, and multilateral issues with Quirno.
The Minister said his meeting with Mexico’s Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco Alvarez was focused on giving a new impetus to bilateral relations.
“A pleasure to sit down with FM Mauro Vieira of Brazil. Our conversation covered bilateral and global issues,” Mr. Jaishankar said.

articles.title: Oman rescues 25 from burning ship, Iran halts tankers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Tehran has restricted maritime traffic through the strait since the West Asia war erupted on February 28 with U.S.-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic
Oman said Friday (October 30, 2026) it had rescued 25 sailors from a merchant ship set ablaze in an attack, as Iran reported three oil tankers were halted while crossing the Strait of Hormuz.
Tehran has restricted maritime traffic through the strait since the West Asia war erupted on February 28 with U.S.-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic.
The narrow waterway, which normally carries about a fifth of global oil, has become a focal point of the conflict, with ships regularly coming under Iranian fire.

Muscat's navy "carried out an evacuation operation for 25 crew members of the merchant ship RITI, flying the Panamanian flag, after it was targeted, which led to a fire breaking out on board," Oman's Maritime Security Centre said in a statement.
The crew members were provided with medical care, the Omani statement said, without giving details.
The Marine Traffic ship-tracking website described the RITI as a crude oil tanker.

U.S. Central Command chief Brad Cooper said in a video released on Friday (October 30) that U.S. forces had "successfully cleared the strait's internationally recognised primary transit routes of Iranian sea mines".
U.S. forces remain "present to ensure that all primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear," he added.

Mr. Cooper said he visited some of the more than 50,000 U.S. service members in the region, repeating earlier statements that Washington has helped Gulf countries export more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude via the strait since summer.

British maritime security agency UKMTO said that a ship 40 nautical miles (74 kilometres) south of Lavan Island in Iran was struck on Friday (October 30) by an unknown projectile, which caused a fire onboard.
"The crew of the vessel have been reported as safe and there is no reported environmental impact at this time," the UKMTO said on X.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said earlier that three oil tankers had been halted after encountering unspecified "incidents" or hitting mines.

articles.title: Fears of violence as France braces for Halloween protests
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Around 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday (October 31, 2026), matching the number mobilised a week ago, as authorities seek to avert a repeat of the October 17 unrest

France on Saturday (October 31, 2026) braced for a third weekend of protests coinciding with Halloween, as shops boarded up and authorities scrambled to prevent a repeat of the street violence that swept the country two weeks ago.
The demonstrations come in an increasingly febrile political climate, with presidential elections six months away and far-right leader Marine Le Pen leading opinion polls.
President Emmanuel Macron this week said it was "not normal" for France to be in such a state of "turmoil" so close to a presidential election.
Around 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday (October 31, 2026), matching the number mobilised a week ago, as authorities seek to avert a repeat of the October 17 unrest.
More than 40 metro stations will be closed in the capital and tram services will also be disrupted.

An aide to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said they expected street violence on a scale "comparable" to the unrest two weeks ago, when images of clashes, looted shops and public buildings set ablaze were broadcast around the world.

The protest movement brings together Yellow Vest activists, trade unions, and high school and university students. It initially focused on the rising cost of living, inequality, and deteriorating learning conditions.
But following a security clampdown and serious injuries to some protesters, the movement broadened its demands to include greater protection of civil liberties and the right to protest.
A police source pointed to "considerable nervousness" among the authorities. "There is no reason to think this will go smoothly," the source said.
Alain Di Crescenzo, president of France's chamber of commerce, said business owners were worried.

"Shopkeepers can't wait for Saturday (October 31, 2026) to be over," Mr. Di Crescenzo told broadcaster France Inter . "The information we have is that Halloween is not helping matters, because we're going to have people wearing masks."
Ahead of the protests, some shops and other businesses across France boarded up their storefronts.

Former conservative presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said Friday (October 30, 2026) that he fled Brazil to the United States because he was a victim of "persecution" in his country.

articles.title: Lava to increase smartphone prices by up to ₹3,000
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Lava has been serving the sub-30k price category and is focused on budget and mid segment

As the rising memory shortages continue to hit smartphone makers, Lava has decided to revise its smartphone prices by up to ₹3,000. The homegrown smartphone brand said that the new prices will be effective November 15.
“In the current industry environment, ongoing memory shortages have necessitated a price revision of up to ₹3,000 across our smartphone portfolio, effective 15th November, 2026,” the company said.

Known to sell affordable smartphones in the country, Lava is the sole Indian smartphone brand in the country standing among Chinese and Korean players. During Q3 2026, the Indian brands, including Ai+, captured around 7% market share in India, as per Counterpoint.
Lava has been serving the sub-30k price category due to volume game and thinks that anything beyond that is vanity. It wants to focus on budget and mid segment and purely smartphone business.

Lava further added that consumers looking to upgrade their devices have a strong opportunity at this moment, as its products are currently available at festive prices across leading e-commerce platforms and offline retail network.
We would encourage customers to take advantage of the ongoing offers, before the revision comes into effect, added Lava.
