articles.title: All arrangements in place for municipal polls across south A.P.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: All arrangements have been completed for municipal polls across the southern districts of Andhra Pradesh on Sunday. The respective district administrations, police authorities, polling staff and and micro-observers are ready to conduct the elections in a peaceful, free, and fair manner.

Tirupati District Collector S. Venkateswar, along with by Municipal Commissioner M. Jayakrishna, inspected the election materials at the premises of S.V. Arts College on Saturday morning. They reviewed the process of distributing ballot boxes, ballot papers, and other supplies.

“Special facilities have been arranged for pregnant women, nursing mothers, persons with disabilities, the elderly, and female voters. NSS volunteers will assist with queue management. Nearly 2,500 police personnel have been deployed to ensure security,” the Collector said.

In SPSR Nellore district, Superintendent of Police (SP) Ajitha Vejendla said that stringent security arrangements were being implemented to ensure that citizens can exercise their right to vote in a free and peaceful environment.

Following her direction, the police officials conducted on-site inspections of polling stations. They examined the infrastructure and security arrangements available at the polling stations and the surrounding areas.

Similarly, under the directives of Kadapa district Superintendent of Police (SP) Shelke Nachiket Vishwanath, the police officials conducted route march in R.K. Nagar and field inspections of hyper-sensitive and sensitive polling stations within Jammalamadugu and Rajampet municipalities.

The SP warned that strict action will be taken against those engaging in activities that disrupt law and order or lead to untoward incidents. He ensured continuous monitoring and robust barricading at the polling stations.

As polling is set to take place for the Ongole Municipal Corporation, as well as Cheemakurthi and Addanki municipalities, Prakasam District Collector P. Raja Babu, SP V. Harshavardhan Raju and Joint Collector Kalpana Kumari jointly inspected the arrangements for the municipal elections.
Polling staff check the election materials for the municipal elections at RISE Engineering College in Ongole on Saturday. | Photo Credit: KOMMURI SRINIVAS

“Of the 303 polling stations in the district, 100 have been categorised as hyper-sensitive and 107 as sensitive and based on the security scale determined for these respective categories, sufficient personnel have been deployed at all locations,” Mr. Harshavardhan said.

Markapuram district SP Pankaj Kumar Meena said that nearly 800 police personnel were deployed for election security duties to ensure the peaceful conduct of the elections in Markapuram, Giddalur, and Kanigiri municipalities.

articles.title: Minister to seek additional ₹300 crore for irrigation works in Kalyana Karnataka region
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Minor Irrigation Department plans to seek additional funds of ₹300 crore for development works in the Kalyana Karnataka region after discussions with the Finance Department, said Minister for Minor Irrigation Ajay Singh.

Speaking to presspersons here on Saturday, Dr. Singh said 13 minor irrigation projects worth ₹200 crore were taken up during the 2025-26 financial year through the Minor Irrigation Department and the Kalyana Karnataka Region Development Board.

Dr. Singh said a meeting with officials would be held within a week to assess water scarcity in rural areas and identify locations where borewells and open wells needed to be drilled to address the water shortage.
Defending the increase in the price of Nandini milk, the Minister said that the decision was taken to protect dairy farmers who are facing rising production costs and the impact of drought.
He said the cost of milk production, packaging and transportation had increased substantially, making it difficult for farmers to sustain dairy operations without adequate returns.
“Is it wrong to ensure that farmers receive fair compensation for their hard work? Should they continue selling milk at a loss?” he asked.
Of the additional ₹8 collected through the price revision, ₹7 would go directly to farmers, while the remaining ₹1 would be allocated to the milk producers’ cooperative, the Minister claimed.

Dr. Singh maintained that Nandini milk continued to be cheaper in Karnataka than in several other States. Even after the price revision, milk prices in Karnataka remained ₹4 to ₹10 lower than those in many States, he claimed.

Criticising the BJP-led Union government, the Minister said Karnataka was not receiving the financial assistance it was entitled to. Despite seeking at least ₹20,000 crore in assistance under the National Disaster Response Force to tackle the drought situation, the State had not received a favourable response, he said, accusing the Centre of adopting a “step-motherly approach” towards Karnataka.
He also pointed out that the rising prices of petrol, diesel and cooking gas had increased the financial burden on common people.
The Minister termed the protests organised by the BJP and Janta Dal (Secular) against the milk price revision as politically motivated.

articles.title: Jowar prices hit an all-time high in Karnataka amidst drought conditions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The price of the Maldandi variety of jowar has increased from ₹5,500 in September to ₹ 8,500 per quintal; Gundu Thene variety is priced at ₹8,200 per quintal, up from ₹5,000

On the heels of a rise in rice and toor dal prices, jowar prices too have surged in Karnataka amid drought conditions. Farmers, traders and agriculture experts say the current price of jowar, a staple in many north Karnataka districts, has hit its highest level in recent times.

According to APMC merchants in Vijayapura and Kalaburagi districts, the price of the famous Maldandi variety of jowar has increased from ₹5,500 per quintal in September to ₹8,500 per quintal at present. The Gundu Thene variety is priced at ₹8,200 per quintal, up from ₹5,000. Last week, the price had gone up to ₹9,200 per quintal for the Maldandi variety and ₹9,000 per quintal for the Gundu Thene variety.

While drought is the major reason behind the increase, department officials and experts from the university pointed out that the mechanisation of almost all other crops in the agriculture sector except jowar, and the fixed Minimum Support Price (MSP) from the Centre, are other reasons why jowar prices have increased compared with previous years.

Data from the Agriculture Department reveal that the sowing achieved in the kharif season was 0.42 lakh hectares against a target of 0.80 lakh hectares, or 53% of the target. Last year, in the same season, sowing was completed on 0.39 lakh hectares against a target of 0.54 lakh hectares.

Speaking to The Hindu , Santosh Budge, Assistant Director, APMC, Kalaburagi, said, “I have seen prices go up and down for more than a decade. But it is the first time that the price has increased to ₹9,000-9,200 per quintal. This week, it has reduced to ₹8,500 per quintal and I believe the price will keep hovering between ₹8,500 and ₹9,500. It might even shoot up to ₹10,000.”

Highlighting previous prices, Mr. Budge said, “In 2022-23, when there was a similar drought situation, the price had increased to ₹8,000 per quintal. Last year, in October, the price was around ₹6,500 per quintal and later decreased to ₹5,000.”

Vijay Hiremath, a jowar trader, said, “Currently, stocks in the market are also low for various reasons. Some farmers sell directly at the APMC, while others sell in the open market to traders of their choice for ₹10-15 more than the APMC price. Whether the prices will rise further or stabilise will be known only in mid-November, when the sowing of jowar for the rabi season will be completed across north Karnataka.”

Prof. Suresh K.B., an expert in post-harvest and engineering technology at the University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru (UAS-B), said, “Jowar is a kharif and rabi crop, but the Maldandi and Gundu Thene varieties are mostly cultivated in the rabi season. The sowing has begun now and will end by the second week of November. As a millet, jowar does not require much water. It is grown in rain-fed regions of Karnataka, including Vijayapura, Ballari, Raichur, Kalaburagi, Belagavi and Dharwad. Instead of depending on rain, many farmers adopt the residual moisture method. This means they sow jowar soon after paddy is harvested. The residual moisture present in the soil helps the cultivation of jowar. In the first 30 days, it does not require water.”

However, he pointed out that paddy cultivation had also reduced during the kharif season because of deficient rainfall and low water levels in major reservoirs. “We have to wait and watch the yield of jowar in the rabi season after the harvest,” he said. He predicted that prices might remain high until new rabi stocks arrive.

Shivanagouda Patil, Joint Director, Agriculture Department, Vijayapura district, said, “Vijayapura has the largest area under jowar cultivation, with 0.12 metric tonnes in kharif and 0.72 metric tonnes in rabi. But over a period of time, farmers have lost interest in cultivation due to the lack of mechanisation.” For instance, in contrast, toor cultivation is completely mechanised and offers better returns. While the Minimum Support Price for jowar is ₹4,073 per quintal, it is ₹8,450 per quintal for toor.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi claims 2024 Lok Sabha elections ‘illegal’ over voter deletions | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge lists six charges against Gyanesh Kumar, including facilitating vote theft, deleting 13.2 crore voter names and changing Form 6 without parliamentary oversight

After the INDIA bloc’s symbolic ‘public impeachment’ programme against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said discussions had been dignified and positive. He expressed confidence that the same spirit would continue at Sunday’s rally, adding that large numbers of people were expected to attend.

In a post on X, Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi alleged that the deletion of one in every seven voters from electoral rolls amounted to an admission that the 2024 Lok Sabha election was illegitimate. He accused Gyanesh Kumar and others of treason and warned of action against them.
Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi claimed the Opposition had enough evidence against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to ensure his removal, warning the BJP against retaining him in office.

BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad criticised Rahul Gandhi for holding a symbolic ‘mock Parliament’ programme, accusing the Congress of ridiculing constitutional institutions. He also alleged that Jawaharlal Nehru became Prime Minister through vote theft and challenged Gandhi to resign.

Speaking at the INDIA bloc’s symbolic public impeachment programme against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi, TMC MP Mahua Moitra accused the Modi government and the Election Commission of undermining voting rights, claiming that 71% of deleted voters in West Bengal were Muslims and 51% were women.

Speaking at the INDIA bloc’s public impeachment programme against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi alleged that the deletion of 13.3 crore voter names had undermined the legitimacy of the 2024 Lok Sabha election. He claimed the number of deleted voters far exceeded the 3% vote margin between the Opposition and the BJP-led alliance.

articles.title: Petrol export duty cut to nil, diesel levy raised by ₹3 a litre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The government’s fortnightly review raised the export levy on diesel to ₹11.5 per litre from ₹8.5 and on aviation turbine fuel to ₹11 per litre from ₹10.5, while India’s diesel exports touched 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025, according to Kpler

The government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) slashed the export duty on petrol to nil while hiking the levy on export of diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹3 per litre and 50 paise per litre respectively for the next 15-day period.
There was no change in the existing excise duty rates for petrol and diesel for domestic consumption.
Diesel exports would now draw a levy of ₹11.5 for every litre against ₹8.5 per litre it drew in the previous fortnight.
ATF would be subject to an export levy of ₹11 for every litre against ₹10.5 for every litre as mandated for the previous fortnight.
The revised levy on diesel assumes significance as India spiked its exports of the liquid vehicular fuel amid a global supply crunch, particularly in Europe.
According to data from real-time analytics provider Kpler, India’s diesel exports stood at 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025.

Sumit Ritolia, Manager for Modelling and Refining at Kpler, in a social media post on Friday (October 30, 2026) further observed, “India’s diesel exports are expected to ease to 500-550 kbd in Nov–Dec as seasonal domestic demand peaks before recovering to 550–600 kbd in Q1 2027. Higher maintenance in Q2-27 will constrain export, with new capacity contributing meaningfully only later in 2027.”

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

articles.title: Iran’s Supreme Leader warns U.S., Israel against new attacks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Saturday (October 31, 2026) warned the United States and Israel against returning to war, according to a written statement, following threats from the Islamic republic's foes of a possible resumption of strikes.

"If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for ending them," said a statement attributed to Mr. Khamenei posted on his website.

The remarks came during a reported meeting between Mr. Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi. It was the first reported meeting between them.
Mr. Khamenei has not been publicly seen since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's killing in U.S.-Israeli strikes at the start of the war in West Asia in February.
According to the statement, Mr. Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that "any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response".
It also said that Mr. Khamenei ordered the commanders to update Iran's target list to include "all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy".
The war began on February 28 with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran, which swiftly responded with attacks on countries around the region.
The supreme leader's statement came as fresh diplomatic efforts were under way to avert a resumption of fighting.
A Qatari delegation arrived in Tehran on Friday (October 30) for talks with Iranian officials, after Iran reportedly received a letter from U.S. Vice President JD Vance.
According to Iranian media, Tehran had yet to respond to the letter.

articles.title: Britain open to apologising for slavery, says U.K. PM Andy Burnham
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Mr. Burnham pushed back against the notion of financial reparations for victims of slavery saying that the British people could not be held responsible for historical wrongs; Burnham’s omission of colonialism ‘inexcusable’, said Tharoor
U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said his government is open to the idea of formally apologising for Britain’s historical role in the slave trade, although he ruled out financial reparations.

Mr. Burnham set out his position in an opinion piece in The Guardian on Friday (October 30, 2026), ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda, next week. There have, for long, been calls for Britain to apologise and offer reparations for slavery and its colonial past , including in India.

Some three million Africans were transported as slaves to work on plantations in Britian’s colonies in the Americas. Britain began abolishing the slave trade in its empire in 1807. Slavery was abolished in 1833 though not all slaves were freed until 1838. Britain “compensated” slave owners to a total sum of GBP 20 million or 40% of the government’s annual budget in 1833.
“Manchester’s cotton industry was built on the labour of enslaved people,” wrote Mr. Burnham, the former Mayor of Manchester.
Mr. Burnham acknowledged the calls from affected countries for a dialogue on slavery.

“By sticking our heads in the sand, we have damaged the ability of the Commonwealth to function,” he said, adding that it was necessary to have conversations on slavery to protect the future of the Commonwealth.
Mr. Burnham said the U.K. was “offering structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade”.
“Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process, and I am open to them,” he added.

Calls for Britain to make amends for its past have grown louder in recent days as Britain’s King Charles III tours the Caribbean on his way to the CHOGM. The King is the titular head of the Commonwealth.
In the Bahamas this week, Charles acknowledged the “great suffering and injustices of the past”, stopping short of an apology.
Bucking Palace has said that it was up to the U.K. government to decide whether or not to apologise.

Barbadian Prime Minister Mia Amor Mottley welcomed Mr. Burnham’s statement, even as she acknowledged that “views differ” on reparations. The British Monarch was the titular Head of State of Barbados until 2021, when the country became a republic. It is one of several countries asking Britain to go beyond an apology and make financial reparations for slavery.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics

Mr. Burnham pushed back against the notion of financial reparations for victims of slavery saying that the British people could not be held responsible for historical wrongs; Burnham’s omission of colonialism ‘inexcusable’, said Tharoor

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said his government is open to the idea of formally apologising for Britain’s historical role in the slave trade, although he ruled out financial reparations.

Mr. Burnham set out his position in an opinion piece in The Guardian on Friday (October 30, 2026), ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda, next week. There have, for long, been calls for Britain to apologise and offer reparations for slavery and its colonial past , including in India.

Some three million Africans were transported as slaves to work on plantations in Britian’s colonies in the Americas. Britain began abolishing the slave trade in its empire in 1807. Slavery was abolished in 1833 though not all slaves were freed until 1838. Britain “compensated” slave owners to a total sum of GBP 20 million or 40% of the government’s annual budget in 1833.

“Manchester’s cotton industry was built on the labour of enslaved people,” wrote Mr. Burnham, the former Mayor of Manchester.

Mr. Burnham acknowledged the calls from affected countries for a dialogue on slavery.

“By sticking our heads in the sand, we have damaged the ability of the Commonwealth to function,” he said, adding that it was necessary to have conversations on slavery to protect the future of the Commonwealth.

Mr. Burnham said the U.K. was “offering structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade”.

“Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process, and I am open to them,” he added.

Calls for Britain to make amends for its past have grown louder in recent days as Britain’s King Charles III tours the Caribbean on his way to the CHOGM. The King is the titular head of the Commonwealth.

In the Bahamas this week, Charles acknowledged the “great suffering and injustices of the past”, stopping short of an apology.

Bucking Palace has said that it was up to the U.K. government to decide whether or not to apologise.

Barbadian Prime Minister Mia Amor Mottley welcomed Mr. Burnham’s statement, even as she acknowledged that “views differ” on reparations. The British Monarch was the titular Head of State of Barbados until 2021, when the country became a republic. It is one of several countries asking Britain to go beyond an apology and make financial reparations for slavery.

The story so far: The U.S. midterm elections are just days away, and the results could prove to be a defining moment for the Trump administration and the Republican Party. The elections represent the first major electoral test for Donald Trump since his return to the Oval Office for a second term. The run-up to the polls has been marked by a series of high-stakes developments, including renewed scrutiny of Mr. Trump’s name appearing in the Epstein files, the U.S. military operation that led to the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January, the controversy surrounding the Nobel Peace Prize, and the escalating conflict in West Asia following the launch of U.S. and Israeli military operations against Iran — Operation Epic Fury and Operation Roaring Lion, respectively.

Against this backdrop, the Vatican has confirmed that Chicago-born Pope Leo XIV, formerly known as Robert Francis Prevost, has cast his vote in the U.S. midterm elections. “Pope Leo XIV has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen whenever he was eligible to do so,” the Holy See Press Office said in a statement. It further confirmed that, “in keeping with this long-standing practice of civic participation, he has submitted his mail-in ballot in Chicago.”

articles.title: France heads into third weekend of protests as youth-led rallies sweep Europe
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween

France prepared on Saturday (October 31, 2026) for a third consecutive weekend of protests over living costs and education, deploying 70,000 police and gendarmes and rerouting the Paris march to the capital's edge as youth-led demonstrations spread across Europe.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween.

Paris police banned union and “yellow vest” marches through the city centre, ordering demonstrations to follow a single route along the capital's outer boulevards, from Porte de Bagnolet to Porte de Charenton. Unions and student groups challenged the restrictions in court, but lost.
President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday (October 26, 2026) that marches would stay out of city centres to protect shops.
Police also barred entry to Place de la Republique and Les Halles, both hit by rioting and looting on October 17, from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026) and Sunday (November 1, 2026).

Unaccompanied minors face a separate 9 p.m. curfew around the Champs-Elysees. A Paris court on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) suspended an earlier curfew on minors as a serious and illegal infringement of freedom of movement.
The movement began with high school students protesting school conditions and broadened into anger over living costs.

Authorities counted about 550,000 protesters nationwide on October 17, when rioters looted hundreds of shops, and 410,000 last Saturday (October 31, 2026), when rallies were largely peaceful but police made more than 1,300 arrests.

In Germany, a youth initiative called “Gen Z regelt” — roughly “Gen Z's got this” — urged protests in some 30 cities “for education, health, climate protection and an affordable life,” and against any return of military conscription. Organisers said more than 140,000 people had signed up online.

Berlin police expected about 10,000 people at the Brandenburg Gate. Some shops on the Kurfuerstendamm boulevard boarded up their windows, although authorities said they were unaware of specific threats of violence. Protests were expected to begin in the early afternoon.

In Barcelona, Spain, Catalan police planned to activate their highest-level alert after an anonymous TikTok network called Blocus urged new gatherings. Rioting there last Saturday (October 24, 2026) led to about 130 arrests, mostly of minors.
Italian police were on alert after clashes in Milan, Turin and Bologna, and calls to protest circulated on TikTok in Belgium, the Netherlands, Austria, Switzerland and Portugal.

articles.title: Iran says fishermen found after accusing U.S. of attack in Hormuz

fullParagraphs: Two fishermen from Qeshm, who had gone missing following an attack by the American enemy on their fishing boat this morning, have been found, state television said
Iran said two fishermen it had reported missing on Saturday (October 31, 2026) have now been found, following what it called a U.S. attack on a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.
"Two fishermen from Qeshm, who had gone missing following an attack by the American enemy on their fishing boat this morning, have been found," state television said.

Earlier, state TV had cited a provincial official as saying that two fishermen had gone missing and two others were wounded in what he called an attack by the United States on their vessel in the crucial Hormuz waterway.
AFP has contacted for comment the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM), which oversees American military operations in the region.

articles.title: India’s first fusion power company takes key steps
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Designs for the first privately built tokamak, a nuclear reactor that uses fusion to produce energy, could be firmed up in 2027 by Bengaluru-based startup Pranos Fusion
If all goes to plan, India may see designs for the first privately built tokamak, a nuclear reactor that uses fusion to produce energy, firmed up in 2027.

Bengaluru-based startup Pranos Fusion has built PRAGYA, a small doughnut shaped tokamak, to test plasma control and superconducting magnets. This is a gateway to building PRANIK, a much larger tokomak that will have plasma heated up to millions of degrees — more than the interior of the Sun — necessary to fuse hydrogen atoms and create energy.

“By 2027, we expect to finalise the blueprint for PRANIK and be on our way to building a practical reactor that can produce energy. To be able to actually produce electricity from fusion is a further step away,” Shaurya Kaushal, co-founder and CEO of Pranos Fusion, said.

The company is currently incubated out of the Institute of Plasma Research, a body affiliated to the Department of Atomic Energy and the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), Bengaluru, an institute with the Department of Science and Technology.

Nuclear plants everywhere employ fission — a chain reaction involving uranium nuclei to produce heat that is used to generate electricity. Fusion, on the other hand, releases energy when light atomic nuclei merge, and usually involves joining two forms of hydrogen — deuterium and tritium — into helium and a fast neutron. However, this requires the fuel to be heated to around 100 million degrees Celsius, far hotter than any solid wall could withstand. In tokamaks, powerful magnets hold this superheated plasma away from the walls, keeping it hot enough for fusion to continue.
Pranos Fusion was one of the deeptech startups showcased at the Emerging Science Technology and Innovation Conclave held here last week.

“Electricity from a fusion reactor is still far away and would be expensive now, however the need for any source of energy is only going to grow,” Roshan George, co-founder and a Computer Science engineer from the Manipal Institute of Technology. “Fusion’s advantage is that while [it’s] nuclear power, it doesn’t need radioactive material like uranium. India already produces plenty of deuterium. Fusion reactions are also not chain reactions, and therefore the risk of a runaway reaction [like in a fission reactor] is almost absent,” Mr. George said.

The largest tokamak under construction is the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor in southern France, a collaboration between China, the European Union, India, Japan, Russia, South Korea, and the U.S. It is designed to produce about 10 times the heating power fed into its plasma. Bogged by delays, a 2024 revision moved the start of research operations to 2034 and full deuterium-tritium operation to 2039, adding about €5 billion to the cost. IPR manages India’s home-grown tokamak reactors, including ADITYA and the Steady State Tokamak (SST-1). It is also the nodal domestic agency to manage India’s contributions to International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor.

The cost of a private tokamak depends on scale, Mr. Kaushal, who holds a Ph.D. from JNCASR, and a mechanical engineering degree from BITS Pilani, said. A compact research machine like PRAGYA is “a comparatively modest investment”, while one designed to reach net energy gain is far larger. Private fusion companies worldwide have raised over $13 billion, he said, and the leading net-gain programmes have each raised hundreds of millions of dollars or more.

Pranos Fusion says compact machines, HTS (high-temperature superconducting) magnets, and India’s manufacturing base can bring costs down substantially. It is backed by Ankur Capital, pi Ventures and Industrial47, and has raised $7.2 million. HTS electromagnets are wound from materials that carry electric current with no resistance when cooled below a critical temperature.

Britain’s JET tokamak produced a record 69 megajoules of fusion energy in 2023, though less than the heating power supplied. In December 2022, the U.S. National Ignition Facility, which uses lasers rather than magnets, achieved ignition, releasing more fusion energy than the laser light delivered to the fuel. This, however, does not count the electricity needed to run the lasers. Magnets made from high-temperature superconductors (HTS) have reached fields of around 20 tesla in tests, making smaller, stronger-field machines feasible.

In an email, Mr. Kaushal said the company is structured in a way its technology generates value before a power plant exists. It has two platforms — JENGA, simulation, design and control software that works as a digital twin of the machine, and MAGGA, its HTS magnet programme.

The cost of a private tokamak depends on scale, Mr. Kaushal, who holds a Ph.D. from JNCASR, and a mechanical engineering degree from BITS Pilani, said. A compact research machine like PRAGYA is “a comparatively modest investment”, while one designed to reach net energy gain is far larger. Private fusion companies worldwide have raised over $13 billion, he said, and the leading net-gain programmes have each raised hundreds of millions of dollars or more.

Pranos Fusion says compact machines, HTS (high-temperature superconducting) magnets, and India’s manufacturing base can bring costs down substantially. It is backed by Ankur Capital, pi Ventures and Industrial47, and has raised $7.2 million. HTS electromagnets are wound from materials that carry electric current with no resistance when cooled below a critical temperature.

Britain’s JET tokamak produced a record 69 megajoules of fusion energy in 2023, though less than the heating power supplied. In December 2022, the U.S. National Ignition Facility, which uses lasers rather than magnets, achieved ignition, releasing more fusion energy than the laser light delivered to the fuel. This, however, does not count the electricity needed to run the lasers. Magnets made from high-temperature superconductors (HTS) have reached fields of around 20 tesla in tests, making smaller, stronger-field machines feasible.

In an email, Mr. Kaushal said the company is structured in a way its technology generates value before a power plant exists. It has two platforms — JENGA, simulation, design and control software that works as a digital twin of the machine, and MAGGA, its HTS magnet programme.

articles.title: NASA telescope on verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission's chief scientist
An ageing NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower.
The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday (October 30, 2026).

Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission's chief scientist.

Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope's dwindling path.

Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning, yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. Swift blasted off on November 20, 2004, to search for some of the biggest explosions in the universe — gamma ray bursts and supernovas.

“We've known this day would come since before Swift was launched. At least in low-Earth orbit, what goes up must come down. And that end is catastrophic,” said Pennsylvania State University's John Nousek, an astronomer who led the control team.

Intense solar activity over the past few years dragged Swift down faster than usual. NASA hired Katalyst Space a year ago to mount a rush rescue. But the company's three-armed robot named Link ran into trouble after launching in July and got no closer than 7 miles to 9 miles (12 kilometres to 15 kilometres) to the telescope. Link plunged back to Earth in September.

Swift resumed observations once the rescue attempt was called off, discovering even more gamma ray bursts and other ultrahigh-energy events. But by late October, the telescope was too low to remain steady for observations, and its systems were shut down.

Its final tally — more than 2,000 gamma ray bursts and 1,400 exploding stars, not to mention a slew of comets, asteroids, and star-shredding black holes. The telescope's superpower was its ability to swivel swiftly — thus its name — toward erupting celestial events.

NASA considered Swift a first responder for the Hubble and Webb space telescopes and others that would follow its alerts and provide deeper investigations. Scientists are still figuring out how to fill the gap.

“Our fervent hope is that the lessons learned by the successes of Swift can be applied to new generations of space missions to accelerate our discoveries about the universe,” Mr. Nousek said in an email.

articles.title: Why investors are worried despite Alphabet’s 25% revenue growth and Google Cloud’s revenue more than doubling | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Google’s parent company is investing heavily in artificial intelligence infrastructure as its cloud business expands. But the spending is weighing on cash flow, while AI-powered search raises questions about the future of its advertising business

Alphabet reported strong growth in the September quarter, but the results also highlighted the cost of keeping pace with the artificial intelligence (AI) race. The company is investing heavily in computing infrastructure to develop and run AI models and services. At the same time, AI is changing how people use Google Search, raising questions about how the company will continue to earn money from its biggest advertising business.
The concerns are not about whether the Alphabet is growing. They are about how much it will have to spend to sustain that growth, and whether its AI investments will generate enough returns.

articles.title: Shetty Institute of Technology hosts TechNova and NextGen Hackathon in Kalaburagi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Shetty Institute of Technology (SIT), Kalaburagi, hosted TechNova 2026 and the AIC T-Hub NextGen Hackathon 2026 from October 27 to 30, bringing together 89 teams from educational institutions across the country.

TechNova, held on October 27 and 28, featured 26 teams from South India, with Robotics 2.0 among the major attractions. Winners in various categories received cash prizes ranging from ₹5,000 to ₹50,000.
The 36-hour NextGen Hackathon, organised in collaboration with AIC T-Hub on October 29 and 30, saw 63 teams comprising 220 students develop innovative solutions to real-world problems.
Pardha Saradhi of CMR College of Engineering and Technology, Hyderabad, won first place, followed by Smartronics of Symbiosis Skills and Professional University, Pune, and Latents of SIT, Kalaburagi.

Three teams – Technora Crews from SIT, Caffeine and Catastrophe from the Central University of Karnataka, Kalaburagi, and Core4 from NK Orchid College of Engineering, Solapur – were selected for further support from T-Hub.

SIT Director Anirudh Shetty said the events aimed to bring industry exposure, innovation opportunities and the start-up ecosystem closer to students in Kalaburagi. Director Shweta Shetty said such initiatives encouraged students to explore their potential, collaborate and develop practical skills beyond academics.
The four-day programme concluded with cultural performances, music, dance and other entertainment activities on October 30.

articles.title: Protesters smear ink on Addanda Cariappa’s face over his play on Gandhiji
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Controversial theatre personality and former Mysuru Rangayana director Addanda C. Cariappa was allegedly attacked and his face smeared with ink by a group of protesters during the staging of a play on Mahatma Gandhi’s assassination at Suchitra Film Academy in Banashankari on Saturday.

The incident occurred during the staging of Gandhi Hatheya Kicchu , organised by Rangabhoomi Trust (R), Kodagu, at Naga Links, Banashankari II Stage. Mr. Cariappa, who wrote and directed the play, was confronted by protesters who objected to its portrayal of Mahatma Gandhi.

The protesters, led by one Kushal Hanumegowda, lodged a complaint with the Banashankari police, accusing Mr. Cariappa of spreading misinformation about Gandhi and portraying him as “anti-national” and a “slave of Muslims” in the play. The complaint was signed by 14 persons.

The complainants alleged that the play sought to blame the Congress and Mahatma Gandhi for the Partition of the country and made misleading references to the “payment of ₹50 crore to Pakistan”. They also objected to members of the audience being made to raise slogans condemning Mahatma Gandhi during the performance.

The complaint further alleged that tickets for the Bengaluru staging had been sold on the black market in Mysuru. When the complainants questioned the alleged sale, Mr. Cariappa reportedly abused them using vulgar language.
The complainants sought legal action against Mr. Cariappa, the actors who performed in the play, and others associated with its staging.

articles.title: First import container arrives at Vizhinjam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The vessel carrying the first import consignment to Vizhinjam since full-scale export-import (EXIM) cargo operations commenced at Vizhinjam International Seaport in August called at the port here on Saturday, marking the beginning of a new chapter in the State’s maritime trade.

The first import container to Vizhinjam was booked from Ningbo in China and arrived aboard the vessel MSC Sabrina III. It was booked by BP2G Logistics and Ship Chandlers Private Limited, a Thiruvananthapuram-based start-up, on behalf of the city’s business enterprise, M/s Alteir Group.
The consignment comprises a full container load (FCL) of engineered building boards used in the construction sector as an alternative to conventional plywood.

With import operations now under way at Vizhinjam, containers can be unloaded, cleared and transported directly to markets across Keralam. This will reduce local entrepreneurs’ dependence on distant ports, helping them cut transportation costs and delivery times. The revenue generated through cargo handling and logistics activities will also remain within the State.

The development is expected to create employment opportunities for customs brokers, freight forwarders, transport operators, warehouse operators and port workers, while strengthening Keralam’s position as a maritime trade destination, authorities said.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 31 Oct 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

First import container arrives at Vizhinjam

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

The vessel carrying the first import consignment to Vizhinjam since full-scale export-import (EXIM) cargo operations commenced at Vizhinjam International Seaport in August called at the port here on Saturday, marking the beginning of a new chapter in the State’s maritime trade.

The first import container to Vizhinjam was booked from Ningbo in China and arrived aboard the vessel MSC Sabrina III. It was booked by BP2G Logistics and Ship Chandlers Private Limited, a Thiruvananthapuram-based start-up, on behalf of the city’s business enterprise, M/s Alteir Group.

The consignment comprises a full container load (FCL) of engineered building boards used in the construction sector as an alternative to conventional plywood.

With import operations now under way at Vizhinjam, containers can be unloaded, cleared and transported directly to markets across Keralam. This will reduce local entrepreneurs’ dependence on distant ports, helping them cut transportation costs and delivery times. The revenue generated through cargo handling and logistics activities will also remain within the State.

The development is expected to create employment opportunities for customs brokers, freight forwarders, transport operators, warehouse operators and port workers, while strengthening Keralam’s position as a maritime trade destination, authorities said.

In a post on X, Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi alleged that the deletion of one in every seven voters from electoral rolls amounted to an admission that the 2024 Lok Sabha election was illegitimate. He accused Gyanesh Kumar and others of treason and warned of action against them.

BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad criticised Rahul Gandhi for holding a symbolic ‘mock Parliament’ programme, accusing the Congress of ridiculing constitutional institutions. He also alleged that Jawaharlal Nehru became Prime Minister through vote theft and challenged Gandhi to resign.

Speaking at the INDIA bloc’s public impeachment programme against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi alleged that the deletion of 13.3 crore voter names had undermined the legitimacy of the 2024 Lok Sabha election. He claimed the number of deleted voters far exceeded the 3% vote margin between the Opposition and the BJP-led alliance.
ormer West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee arrived in the national capital to attend the INDIA bloc rally scheduled for November 1 at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge outlined six allegations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in the INDIA bloc’s public impeachment resolution, accusing him of facilitating alleged vote theft, deleting 13.2 crore voter names, changing Form 6 and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah.

articles.title: 43 women rescued in illegal human egg harvesting racket in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police examine alleged recruitment of women across States, suspected use of rented premises and links with fertility centres and ART banks in Hyderabad

Eight people were arrested and 43 women from West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and other States were rescued during simultaneous raids at four premises in Hyderabad as police busted an alleged illegal human egg harvesting and commercial sale racket involving recruitment, transportation and accommodation of women for oocyte donation procedures.

The raids were conducted by Begumpet and Saroornagar police along with the Special Operations Team of the Malkajgiri Commissionerate at premises in Prakash Nagar, Begumpet, Erragadda, Saroornagar and Gopalapuram. Police seized documents, mobile phones and other material, while the identities, recruitment circumstances and medical histories of the rescued women are being verified.

Malkajgiri Police Commissioner B. Sumathi said the investigation was examining how women were recruited from different States and brought to Hyderabad after being offered ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 for each egg donation cycle. “We are examining the recruitment, transportation, accommodation and medical procedures, including whether the required legal and safety protocols were followed,” she said.

During the investigation, the women reportedly told police that hormonal injections and medicines were being administered to them in connection with the proposed procedures. Police seized five vials of Humog HP 150 I.U. injections, a syringe, two needles, Primolut and Meprate tablets and other material.

Police said inspections of the premises also raised concerns about the absence of authorised medical supervision and biomedical waste disposal arrangements. The investigation is also examining medical records, informed consent, donor frequency, insurance and safety protocols, as well as the statutory compliance of fertility centres and ART banks under the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, 2021.

Among those arrested in connection with the Begumpet and Saroornagar cases are Amit Sharma, 44, described as the alleged main organiser, Nikkat Parveen, 31, an alleged co-organiser and recruiter, Reshma Khatoon, 26, an IVF agent or sub-agent, Meghavath Srinivas alias Sonu, 23, Jepray Pradeep, 27, Sk. Parveen, 42, Vijay Bhagwah Rao Salunke, 46, and Pankaj Soni, 52. Emirisheetty Durga Prasad, 42, a businessman from Saroornagar, was also arrested in connection with one of the Saroornagar cases.

Police said Amit Sharma had been operating from a rented premises at Prakash Nagar, Begumpet, for about two years, paying ₹50,000 a month. Nikkat Parveen allegedly recruited women, particularly from West Bengal, through agents and coordinated their transportation to Hyderabad.

The preliminary investigation indicates that organisers, recruiters, agents and intermediaries allegedly identified women in different States by offering monetary incentives, transported them to Hyderabad, accommodated them in rented premises and referred them to fertility-related service providers for ovarian stimulation and oocyte retrieval procedures.

The investigation is also focusing on identifying recruitment agents, tracing the transportation of the women, verifying suspected forged Aadhaar cards, affidavits and other documents, and tracing financial transactions and commissions. Police are examining whether there were instances of coercion, deception, exploitation or human trafficking and whether fertility centres and ART banks complied with statutory requirements.

The cases were registered under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Sections 29 and 33 of the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, 2021. Further investigation is under way.

articles.title: CM to open women’s policy summit on November 2
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will inaugurate a two-day women’s policy summit in the State capital on November 2.
The event ‘Her Summit 2026’ will be organised as part of the Makalkoppam scheme.

Minister for Women and Child Development Bindhu Krishna said the government aimed at announcing the new women’s policy on March 8, International Women’s Day, next year. The new policy was intended for women’s social, financial, and political empowerment for an equitable, safe, and progressive Keralam.

Employment-financial empowerment and entrepreneurship; political representation and leadership; education-health-psychological welfare; women safety and laws; and cyber safety are the five main areas of discussion at the summit.

articles.title: IOC says crude Q2 price volatile as procurement swings between discounts and premiums
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Anuj Jain, Director (Finance) at Indian Oil also stated under-recoveries on LPG is projected at ₹309/cylinder in November and ₹370/cylinder in December.

Crude oil procurement remained volatile during the September quarter, with Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) sourcing supplies at discounts of up to $5 per barrel and premiums of as much as $12, Anuj Jain, Director (Finance), told investors during a post-results call on Saturday.

The Delhi-headquartered refiner’s net profit more than doubled year-on-year to ₹21,630 crore in the second quarter, supported by improved refining margins and a brief decline in benchmark crude oil prices.
Mr. Jain said LPG under-recoveries stood at ₹184 per cylinder in September before rising to ₹229 in October. These are projected to increase further to ₹309 in November and ₹370 in December.

Explaining the volatility in procurement costs, he said crude purchases during the quarter ranged from a discount of $5 per barrel to a premium of $12 against prevailing benchmark prices. In the first quarter, the range was from zero discount or premium to a premium of $18 per barrel.
Effective procurement prices depend on several factors, including whether supplies are contracted on a free-on-board (FOB) or delivered-at-place (DAP) basis, freight costs and the grade of crude.

Russian crude accounted for around 55% of IOC’s crude basket during the first half of the fiscal, followed by supplies from the Middle East, primarily Saudi Arabia and Dubai, at 24%. Africa, including Angola and Nigeria, contributed about 10%, while Brazil accounted for 7%. Supplies from the U.S. and Venezuela made up the remaining 2-5% and 3-4%, respectively.
Around 87% of the company’s crude procurement during the period came through spot sourcing. Mr. Jain said.
Responding to a question on whether spot purchases entailed higher costs, he said such sourcing did not necessarily mean paying a premium, as prices varied across region/geography.
“Now, within spot you have Russian crude. Sometimes, we are getting a high discount, sometimes we are paying a premium as well,” Mr. Jain said.

“In the few months, we have seen huge, discounted crude coming in from Iraq. So, the moment it is available, we are buying huge quantities from Iraq also. That used to be our staple diet before the [West Asia] crisis as well.”
He added that procurement economics were also influenced by effective negotiations, which played an important role in determining the final price.

articles.title: Towards recognising women farmers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Maharashtra’s passage of the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, brings into focus the structural bias against the female agricultural workforce, highlights the need for a database of women farmers and using it to ensure access to welfare schemes

Picture a farmer. The image that comes to mind is of a man. But when one looks at who is actually farming, she is increasingly likely to be a woman. This perception-reality mismatch is caused by age-old practices of collecting data, designing policies and defining who a farmer is. It makes millions of women who work on farms, make agricultural decisions and contribute to production nearly invisible. That may, however, finally be beginning to change.

In July 2026, Maharashtra passed the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, through a Woman Farmer Certificate. The Bill arrives nearly two decades after that policy, and 15 years after a comparable law was first proposed at the national level (a lapsed bill introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 2011). It is, in effect, the culmination of three decades of women farmers’ movements backed by civil society organisations.

articles.title: Clashes break out between police and protesters in Paris
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween
The French government estimated that 320,000 people protested nationwide on Saturday (October 31, 2026) in demonstrations focused on high living costs, fewer than in previous demonstrations.

Mass protests on October 17 drew more than 500,000 people around France, and demonstrations on October 24 drew 410,000, according to government estimates. Organisers’ turnout estimates are much higher.

The Interior Ministry told reporters that of the 320,000 protesting on Saturday (October 31, 2026), 70,000 people are estimated to have turned out for the main protest in Paris, which police moved outside the city centre to reduce the risk of unrest around government buildings and tourist sites after a last-minute court battle.

This is the third consecutive weekend of protests over living costs and education, deploying 70,000 police and gendarmes and rerouting the Paris march to the capital's edge as youth-led demonstrations spread across Europe.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez had warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween.

Paris police had banned union and “yellow vest” marches through the city centre, ordering demonstrations to follow a single route along the capital's outer boulevards, from Porte de Bagnolet to Porte de Charenton. Unions and student groups challenged the restrictions in court, but lost.
President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday (October 26, 2026) that marches would stay out of city centres to protect shops.
Police also barred entry to Place de la Republique and Les Halles, both hit by rioting and looting on October 17, from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026) and Sunday (November 1, 2026).

Unaccompanied minors face a separate 9 p.m. curfew around the Champs-Elysees. A Paris court on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) suspended an earlier curfew on minors as a serious and illegal infringement of freedom of movement.
The movement began with high school students protesting school conditions and broadened into anger over living costs.

Authorities counted about 550,000 protesters nationwide on October 17, when rioters looted hundreds of shops, and 410,000 last Saturday (October 31, 2026), when rallies were largely peaceful but police made more than 1,300 arrests.

In Germany, a youth initiative called “Gen Z regelt” — roughly “Gen Z's got this” — urged protests in some 30 cities “for education, health, climate protection and an affordable life,” and against any return of military conscription. Organisers said more than 140,000 people had signed up online.

articles.title: Pakistan PM orders fast-tracking of development projects in Gilgit-Baltistan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The development assumes significance for India as Gilgit-Baltistan is illegally and forcibly occupied by Pakistan
Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has directed officials to accelerate ongoing federal development projects in the controversial Gilgit-Baltistan region and ensure timely release of funds.

Mr. Sharif issued the directions while chairing a meeting in Islamabad on Friday (October 30, 2026) to review the progress of development projects in the region bordering China. Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain also attended the meeting.

The development assumes significance for India as Gilgit-Baltistan is illegally and forcibly occupied by Pakistan. The region is also a key component of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), which passes through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.
India has consistently opposed the CPEC projects passing through territories under Pakistan's illegal occupation, citing concerns over its sovereignty and territorial integrity.

According to state-run broadcaster Radio Pakistan , Mr. Sharif directed the authorities to remove all bottlenecks hindering development projects on a priority basis and ensure effective coordination among the relevant institutions to expedite implementation.

The meeting also reviewed progress on hydropower, infrastructure and solar energy projects in Gilgit-Baltistan. The Prime Minister directed the earliest possible completion of the 100-megawatt solar power project initiated by the federal government for the region.
The meeting also discussed the completion of the China-funded Naltar power project and the installation of digital infrastructure in the region.
The Prime Minister called for regular monitoring of development projects, particularly those related to the energy sector.

A report of a committee constituted in July on the Prime Minister's directives was also presented at the meeting. It reviewed the status of ongoing federal development projects, hurdles in their implementation and measures needed to ensure their timely completion.
Mr. Sharif is likely to visit Gilgit-Baltistan on November 1, the state-run broadcaster reported.

Gilgit-Baltistan, located in northern Pakistan, holds strategic importance because of its geographical proximity to China and its position along the route of the CPEC, a flagship infrastructure and connectivity initiative linking China's Xinjiang region with Pakistan's Gwadar port.
India maintains that the entire Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, including the so-called Gilgit-Baltistan, are integral and inalienable parts of the country.

articles.title: Quad delivering results for people in Indo-Pacific: Rubio
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The group reviewed progress in turning shared priorities into real benefits for the Indo-Pacific region

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, Japan's Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong in Atlanta, U.S., on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting on Saturday (October 31, 2026).
The group reviewed progress in turning shared priorities into real benefits for the Indo-Pacific region amid plans to host a Quad leaders' summit in the Philippines next month.

“I was pleased to meet with my Quad counterparts in Atlanta and discuss the real progress we have made in turning our shared priorities into real benefits for the Indo-Pacific,” Mr. Rubio said in a post on X.

“As our nations continue building reliable and open supply chains, supporting next-generation technologies, increasing maritime cooperation, and securing critical minerals, the United States, Australia, India, and Japan are delivering results for our people and the nations in the region,” Mr. Rubio added.
Mr. Jaishankar said the meeting focused on giving impetus to bilateral relations.
“Appreciated @SecRubio’s hospitality in Atlanta for the @g20org FMM. Took stock of our bilateral cooperation,” Mr. Jaishankar said in a post on X.
This was the third Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting held this year. Earlier, the Ministers met in New Delhi in May and in Manila in July.
Moves are underway to convene a Quad Leaders' Summit, hosted by U.S. President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the ASEAN-East Asian Summits in mid-November.

articles.title: UN ends its Somalia political mission after three decades
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: UNSOM was established by the UN Security Council in 2013 to support Somali authorities in the transition to democracy and the rule of law after more than two decades of conflict involving militias, Islamist groups and criminal gangs

The United Nations political mission in Somalia ended on Saturday (October 30, 2026) after a two-year transition, closing a chapter of more than three decades of UN peacebuilding operations in the east African nation.

UNSOM was established by the UN Security Council in 2013 to support Somali authorities in the transition to democracy and the rule of law after more than two decades of conflict involving militias, Islamist groups and criminal gangs.
It started as UN Political Office for Somalia (UNPOS) in 1995.

In May 2024, Somalia's President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud asked the UN to end the mission ahead of the expiry of its mandate in October that year. He later revised the request, proposing a two-year transition period.
During the transition, UNSOM was renamed the UN Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS).

"Today is not an end to the partnership between the United Nations and Somalia-rather, it marks the conclusion of one chapter and the beginning of another," said Raisedon Zenenga, UNTMIS officer-in-charge and the UN secretary-general's deputy special representative for Somalia in a statement.
"While significant challenges remain, the closure of UNTMIS comes after considerable progress by Somalia since the early years of international efforts to support the country's recovery," he added.
The mission's mandates have been transferred to either Somali institutions or the UN country team.

The transition comes as Al-Qaeda-linked Al-Shabaab, which has fought the Somali government for two decades, continues to control large swathes of central Somalia despite a major international military campaign against it.

The fight against Al-Shabaab is increasingly threatened by international funding cuts, particularly after the United States withdrew all funding for a key UN logistics mission, casting doubt over the future of military operations.
Somalia is due to hold parliamentary and presidential elections next May, with persistent insecurity and opposition disputes threatening the process.

UNSOM was established by the UN Security Council in 2013 to support Somali authorities in the transition to democracy and the rule of law after more than two decades of conflict involving militias, Islamist groups and criminal gangs.

It started as UN Political Office for Somalia (UNPOS) in 1995.

In May 2024, Somalia's President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud asked the UN to end the mission ahead of the expiry of its mandate in October that year. He later revised the request, proposing a two-year transition period.

During the transition, UNSOM was renamed the UN Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS).

"Today is not an end to the partnership between the United Nations and Somalia-rather, it marks the conclusion of one chapter and the beginning of another," said Raisedon Zenenga, UNTMIS officer-in-charge and the UN secretary-general's deputy special representative for Somalia in a statement.

"While significant challenges remain, the closure of UNTMIS comes after considerable progress by Somalia since the early years of international efforts to support the country's recovery," he added.

The mission's mandates have been transferred to either Somali institutions or the UN country team.

The transition comes as Al-Qaeda-linked Al-Shabaab, which has fought the Somali government for two decades, continues to control large swathes of central Somalia despite a major international military campaign against it.

The fight against Al-Shabaab is increasingly threatened by international funding cuts, particularly after the United States withdrew all funding for a key UN logistics mission, casting doubt over the future of military operations.

Somalia is due to hold parliamentary and presidential elections next May, with persistent insecurity and opposition disputes threatening the process.

articles.title: Quad ministers express ‘grave concerns’ over economic coercion

fullParagraphs: Foreign Ministers from the United States, India, Japan and Australia on Saturday (October 31, 2026) jointly raised serious concerns about "economic coercion" like export curbs and practices leading to overproduction, in veiled criticism of China.
"The four ministers expressed grave concerns regarding economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions," said a statement from the Quad alliance in Atlanta, Georgia.

The grouping also recognised the "importance of critical sea lanes, the uninterrupted flow of commerce, energy security, and the unhindered passage and safety of maritime crews and vessels without the imposition of tolls."
It called for "the absolute necessity to protect and preserve navigational rights and freedoms in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait."

articles.title: Modi says Opposition has become destructive force; calls for unity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones for eight development projects worth ₹118.88 crore, taking the total outlay for the 31 projects to ₹426.71 crore

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (October 31, 2026) attacked the Opposition, saying it had turned into “ avrodh paksh [obstructive side]” rather than “ virodh paksh [opposing side]”, and underscored that the country needs to stay united.
He was addressing a gathering at the Parade Ground in Gujarat’s Ekta Nagar on the occasion of Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, marking the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
“It is our misfortune that the Opposition has turned into avrodh paksh ,” Mr. Modi said.

In a veiled reference to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s foreign trips, the Prime Minister asked, “Who is secretly meeting whom in foreign countries? Forces opposed to India are extending their support to whom? Who is speaking the language of India’s enemies?”
He said the nation needs to stand united against such forces and alleged that the Opposition wants to divide the people of the country.
“Social media is being used as a weapon, rumours are being spread, and India’s image is being tarnished,” he alleged.

“I said last year that we would not rest until the country was free from Naxalism and Maoism; that promise has been fulfilled. Though we have finished Naxals, the threat of ‘ dimagi (intellectual) Naxals’ remains very high,” Mr. Modi said.
He told the gathering that India’s next big steps include completely securing the country’s borders, stopping infiltration and demographic changes, and moving towards a secular civil code.
“ Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (One India, Best India) and Viksit Bharat are our two goals,” he said, adding that the country is proceeding on the path shown by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, he said.

Meanwhile, the Prime Minister inaugurated 23 development projects worth ₹307.83 crore to boost tourism and civic infrastructure at Ekta Nagar. He also laid the foundation stones for eight development projects worth ₹118.88 crore, taking the total outlay for the 31 projects to ₹426.71 crore.
Earlier in the day, Mr. Modi paid floral tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel at the Statue of Unity to mark his birth anniversary.
Newly launched projects aim to upgrade visitor facilities and civic infrastructure around the world’s tallest statue, which has developed into a major tourism hub.

articles.title: After ‘Arnab’, Andhra Pradesh may face another severe cyclonic storm
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The depression over Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 2; landfall is expected between Narsapur and Nellore on November 3, with maximum wind speed of 120 kmph

Just days after Cyclone Arnab left a trail of destruction in Andhra Pradesh, weather experts warn that the State may face another severe cyclonic storm next week. The weather system developing over the Andaman Sea is expected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 2.
A low-pressure area formed over the south Andaman Sea on October 29, a day after Cyclone Arnab made landfall along the Kakinada-Narsapur coast in the intervening night of October 27 and 28.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, in its 3.30 p.m. bulletin on Saturday, said the low-pressure area intensified into a well-marked low-pressure system over the Southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas of Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Andaman sea at around 5.30 a.m.

The system moved west-northwestwards and concentrated into a depression by 11.30 a.m. By 5.30 p.m., it centered over south-east Bay of Bengal, about 960 km east-southeast of Chennai, 980 km southeast of Vishakhapatnam, and 1,030 km southeast of Machilipatnam and 1,080 km east-southeast of Ongole.

Another IMD bulletin issued at 7.30 p.m. said the weather system may move west-northwestwards and intensify into a deep depression over south-east Bay of Bengal by the midnight, into a cyclonic storm over south-west and west-central Bay of Bengal by Sunday and further into a severe cylonic storm by November 2.

This time, landfall is expected in the early hours of November 3 between Narsapur and Nellore along the Andhra Pradesh coast, with a maximum wind speed of 120 kmph. The Central Andhra Pradesh is likely to be affected, the bulletin said.

According to Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA), scattered moderate to heavy rainfall is expected in Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Markapuram and Nellore districts on November 1 and scattered heavy to very heavy rainfall is expected in Eluru, West Godavari, NTR, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Palnadu, Prakasam, Markapuram, Nellore and Tirupati districts on November 2.

Sea conditions are likely to remain rough from November 1, worsening on November 2. Squally winds, with a speed reaching 40 kmph to 50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, are likely along and off Andhra Pradesh, North Tamil Nadu and Puducherry coasts from November 1 and increase gradually on November 2.
Fishermen have been advised to stay off the coast from November 2 to 4.

articles.title: Eradicating corruption is collective responsibility: Upa Lokayukta B. Veerappa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “It seems all of us have collectively nurtured the demon of corruption within society. It is impossible to eradicate corruption solely through the Lokayukta or any other institution. Every individual in society must resolve to eliminate it,’’ Upa Lokayukta Justice B. Veerappa said in Belagavi on Friday.
He was speaking after inaugurating a pending cases disposal camp pertaining to the Belagavi and Bailhongal subdivisions, at the Central Hall of the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha.

“In these critical times, when the legislature and the executive appear to be faltering, it seems that the judiciary and the media, often termed the ‘fourth pillar’ of democracy, are also becoming increasingly ineffective. Yet, whenever injustice occurs in society, the judiciary and the press continue to uphold the Constitution by raising their voices,” he said.

“The Karnataka Lokayukta has left a distinct mark in the country through its impartial investigations and operations. Nevertheless, it is not always possible to ensure justice for everyone. Society and families should socially boycott those who engage in corruption,” he said.

“If corruption is eradicated, India will become a powerful nation. Society itself is responsible for the rise in the number of educated fraudsters. Society is heading toward a state of decline because people accept money in exchange for their votes during elections. Things will only improve if society changes. If we set aside selfishness and banish the demon of corruption, India will become the world’s most powerful nation. Corruption has now turned into a competition, and nature itself is sounding an alarm. We must realize this,” he said.

He quoted Rashtrakavi Kuvempu who had advocated Sarvarigu Sama Balu, Sarvarigu Sama Palu (equal share for all, equal life for all) . “This is in accordance with the spirit of the Constitution of India’s assurance of equal rights have been granted to everyone. We should follow this,” he said.

“However, even eight decades of independence, constitutional rights remain a distant mirage for a significant portion of the population. We fight solely for our rights, yet there is a visible lack of interest regarding our duties across all sectors. While we may take a pledge to work without corruption, we simultaneously engage in corrupt practices,” he said.

“As a result of the persistent efforts of the Lokayukta institution, the government has issued an order mandating the allotment of housing sites to all ex-servicemen and their legal heirs in their respective districts or taluks. This government order follows a year and a half of continuous advocacy. The process of identifying and distributing these sites must now be carried out on a war footing,” he said.

The Upa Lokayukta expressed concern that the filing of false cases , often by individuals acting as proxies, was delaying the adjudication of genuine matters and the delivery of justice. He issued a stern warning that complainants who file false cases against government officials could face up to three years in imprisonment. “The Lokayukta has the authority to take strict action against officials found to be negligent in the discharge of their duties. Officials should perform their work with diligence, caution, and integrity,” he said.

articles.title: Govt. sanctions special funds for alternative drinking water sources amid El Nino concerns
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State government has sanctioned special funds to ensure uninterrupted drinking water supply in view of possible scarcity due to El Nino conditions, Panchayat Raj, Rural Development and Rural Water Supply (RWS) Minister Danasari Anasuya Seethakka said on Saturday.

The government has approved ₹120 crore for alternative drinking water arrangements linked to Singur reservoir to cater to Sangareddy, Medak, Kamareddy and Nizamabad districts, while ₹1 crore each has been sanctioned for other districts to meet immediate needs, the Minister said.

During a teleconference with Mission Bhagiratha and Public Health engineers to review the drinking water situation and preparedness, she directed officials to expedite alternative arrangements using the sanctioned funds and ensure there is no disruption in drinking water supply.

She instructed engineers to map villages where Mission Bhagiratha supply is likely to be disrupted and areas where groundwater levels have depleted, and to make local water sources available, including hand pumps, single-phase and three-phase water supply schemes and open wells.
In scarcity-hit habitations, officials were asked to explore hiring private borewells and arranging tankers for water transportation, she said.

Emphasising water conservation, Seethakka called for taking awareness campaigns on judicious use of water and El Nino impact to the village level and for continuous monitoring of reservoir storage levels as per government guidelines.

She also directed officials to take steps for groundwater recharge, especially in areas like Hyderabad, Medchal, Khammam and Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri which received recent rains. Soak pits and magic pits near drinking water sources should be made functional to ensure percolation, and all ongoing recharge works should be completed within two days, she ordered.
